[2026-05-22T11:02:14.482Z] [INFO]       "content": "//! Translation pipeline.\n//!\n//! Public entry point: [`TranslationPipeline::translate`].\n//!\n//! ## Stages\n//!\n//! 1. **Formalize** — `formalize(source_surface, source_lang)` projects the\n//!    natural-language surface into a [`MeaningId`] by consulting\n//!    Wiktionary (for the page that defines the lemma) and Wikidata\n//!    (for the language-neutral Q-item or Lexeme sense). The\n//!    [`MeaningId`] is the semantic meta-language identifier; it never\n//!    embeds any single language.\n//!\n//! 2. **Deformalize** — `deformalize(meaning_id, target_lang)` renders a\n//!    surface form in the target language by:\n//!\n//!    a. running a Wikidata SPARQL lexeme-join (P5137) when the meaning\n//!    is backed by a Wikidata lexeme, **or**\n//!\n//!    b. parsing the source-edition Wiktionary translation table for\n//!    the target language code, **or**\n//!\n//!    c. parsing the target-edition Wiktionary's `=== Перевод ===` /\n//!    `===Translations===` block in reverse.\n//!\n//! [`Translation`], so the resulting links-notation trace shows\n//! exactly which API responses fed the answer.\n\nuse super::dictionary;\nuse super::http::{HttpClient, HttpError};\nuse super::meaning::MeaningId;\nuse super::wikidata::Wikidata;\nuse super::wiktionary::{Wiktionary, WiktionaryCandidate};\n\n/// `true` when `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` is set in the environment.\n///\n/// Reading the env var on every call would be wasteful, but tests rely on\n/// per-process toggling, so we re-check each call here (cheap stdlib lookup).\nfn translation_debug_enabled() -> bool {\n    std::env::var(\"FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG\")\n        .ok()\n        .is_some_and(|value| !value.is_empty() && value != \"0\")\n}\n\n/// Emit a structured debug line to stderr when\n/// `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1`. The Wikidata SPARQL lexeme join (`P5137`)\n/// returns the first matching lexeme regardless of part of speech, so\n/// common noun ↔ verb homographs (e.g. English `milk` → Russian\n/// `доить` \"to milk\", `water` → `поливать` \"to water\") land on the\n/// verb. Each tuple is\n/// `(source_lang, lemma_lower, target_lang, canonical_noun_surface)`.\nconst POLYSEMY_OVERRIDES: &[(&str, &str, &str, &str)] = &[\n    // English nouns where Wikidata returned the verb (\"en\", \"fish\", \"ru\", \"рыба\"),\n    (\"en\", \"friend\", \"ru\", \"друг\"),\n    (\"en\", \"phone\", \"ru\", \"телефон\"),\n    (\"en\", \"salt\", \"ru\", \"соль\"),\n    (\"en\", \"grape\", POLYSEMY_OVERRIDES {\n        if *src == source_lang && *tgt == target_lang && *lemma == key {\n            // Remove existing entries for the canonical surface, then\n            // push it at the front.\n            candidates.retain(|c| c.surface != *canonical);\n            candidates.insert(\n                0,\n                WiktionaryCandidate {\n                    surface: (*canonical).to_owned(),\n                    qualifier: None,\n                },\n            );\n            provenance.push(format!(\n Borrows a single HTTP client (typically a\n/// `CachedHttpClient`) for every Wiktionary and Wikidata call.\npub struct TranslationPipeline<'a, T: HttpClient + ?Sized> {\n    http: &'a T,\n}\n\nimpl<'a, T: HttpClient + ?Sized> TranslationPipeline<'a, T> {\n    pub const fn new(http: &'a T) -> Self {\n        Self { http }\n    }\n\n    /// Translate `surface` from `source_lang` to `target_lang`.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Ok(Translation)` even when the candidate list is empty\n    /// — callers can detect translation gaps by inspecting\n    /// [`Translation::candidates`].\n    pub fn translate(\n        &self,\n        surface: &str,\n        source_lang: &str,\n        target_lang: &str,\n    ) -> Result<Translation, HttpError> {\n        translation_debug(\n            \"translate\",\n            &format!(\"start surface={surface:?} {source_lang}->{target_lang}\"),\n        );\n        if source_lang == target_lang {\n            translation_debug(\"translate\", \"identity (source==target)\");\n            return Ok(Translation {\n                source_surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                source_lang: source_lang.to_owned(),\n                target_lang: target_lang.to_owned(),\n                meaning: MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, surface),\n                candidates: vec![WiktionaryCandidate {\n                    surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                    qualifier: None,\n                }],\n                provenance: vec![\"identity\".to_owned()],\n            });\n        }\n\n        let mut provenance: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        let page_title = normalize_page_title(surface);\n        translation_debug(\"translate\", &format!(\"page_title={page_title:?}\"));\n\n        // Stage 0: consult the offline dictionary first. Misses fall through to the live HTTP\n        // stages below; the same surface is matched against the entry's\n        // canonical lemma and its inflected aliases.\n        let dict =           .unwrap_or(page_title.as_str());\n            provenance.push(format!(\n                \"dictionary:{source_lang}:{lemma}->{target_lang}:{target_surface}\"\n            ));\n            translation_debug(\n                \"stage0\",\n                &format!(\"dictionary hit {source_lang}:{lemma}->{target_lang}:{target_surface}\"),\n            );\n            return Ok(Translation {\n                source_surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                source_lang: source_lang.to_owned(),\n                target_lang: target_lang.to_owned(),\n                meaning: MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, lemma),\n                candidates: vec![WiktionaryCandidate {\n                    surface: target_surface.to_owned(),\n                    qualifier: MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &page_title);\n        match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&page_title, target_lang) {\n            Ok(found) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{page_title}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                ));\n                translation_debug(\"stage1\", &format!(\"source-edition error: {error}\"));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1a: many high-traffic pages keep translations on a\n        // `/translations` subpage (`{{see translation subpage|...}}`).\n        // Try that subpage when the main page yielded nothing.\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            let subpage = format!(\"{page_title}/translations\");\n            match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&subpage, target_lang) {\n                Ok(found) if !found.is_empty() => {\n                    provenance.push(format!(\n                        \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{subpage}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                    ));\n                    blocks = found;\n                }\n                Ok(_) => {}\n                Err(error) => {\n                    provenance.push(format!(\n                        \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{subpage}#translations->error({error})\",\n                    ));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1b: when the source-edition table came up empty, try the\n        // target-edition Wiktionary in reverse. The target page lists\n        // the source language under its own translation block — useful\n        // when the source edition is sparse (common for ru → en).\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            if let Some(reverse) = reverse_lookup(\n                self.http,\n                surface,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n            ) {\n                blocks = reverse;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1d: phrasal-variant fallback. Some natural phrases don't\n        // have their own Wiktionary entry (e.g. ru:\"как у тебя дела\") but\n        // a shorter canonical form does (ru:\"как дела\"). Stop\n        // at the first variant that produces at least one block.\n        let mut active_page_title = page_title.clone();\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            for variant in phrasal_variants(&page_title, source_lang) {\n                provenance.push(format!(\"wiktionary:{source_lang}:variant->{variant}\"));\n                match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&variant, target_lang) {\n                    Ok(found) if !found.is_empty() => {\n                        provenance.push(format!(\n                            \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{variant}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                        ));\n                        blocks = found;\n                        active_page_title.clone_from(&variant);\n                        meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &variant);\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    Ok(_) => {}\n                    Err(error) => {\n                        provenance.push(format!(\n                            \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{variant}#translations->error({error})\"\n                        ));\n                    }\n                }\n                if let Some(reverse) = reverse_lookup(\n                    self.http,\n                    &variant,\n                    source_lang,\n                    target_lang,\n                    &mut provenance,\n                ) {\n                    blocks = reverse;\n                    active_page_title.clone_from(&variant);\n                    meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &variant);\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1c: pick the most likely sense block when the source word\n        // is polysemous (multiple blocks). For each block, count how\n        // many candidates round-trip — that is, how many target-edition\n        // pages list the source surface as a translation. The block with\n        // the highest confirmation rate wins; ties fall back to source\n        // order.\n        let candidates = if blocks.is_empty() {\n            Vec::new()\n        } else {\n            select_best_block(\n                self.http,\n                &active_page_title,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n                blocks,\n            )\n        };\n\n        // Stage 2: pull the Wikidata Q-item / Lexeme sense — even if\n        // we already have a translation surface, we want the trace to\n        // expose the canonical meaning id. We open the page that\n/// is most likely to *exist* on the target edition for the source word.\n/// Russian Wiktionary, for instance, hosts pages for Russian words and\n/// records their translations into other languages under\n/// `=== Перевод ===`.\nfn reverse_lookup<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    surface: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n) -> Option<Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>>> {\n    let page_title = normalize_page_title(surface);\n    for edition in [source_lang, target_lang] {\n        let wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(edition, http);\n        match wiktionary.translation_blocks(&page_title, target_lang) {\n            Ok(blocks) if !blocks.is_empty() => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{edition}:{page_title}#reverse->{target_lang}\"\n                ));\n                return Some(blocks);\n            }\n            Ok(_) => {}\n            Err(error) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{edition}:{page_title}#reverse->error({error})\"\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Pick the best sense block from `blocks` by round-trip confirmation rate.\n///\n/// Each candidate's \"round-trip position\" is its index within the\n/// target-edition block that contains the source surface (not the\n/// flattened candidate list). Lower position = the target considers the\n/// source more primary.\n///\n/// Block-level selection picks the block with the most round-trip\n/// confirmations (ties broken by source order). Within the chosen block,\n/// candidates are sorted by `(target_position_within_block, source_idx)`.\n///\n/// Worked example — `en:hello`:\n/// - Block 0 (\"greeting\"): `привет` confirms at target-pos 0,\n///   `здравствуйте` at target-pos 1. Two confirms.\n/// - Block 1 (\"when answering the telephone\"): `алло` and `алё` confirm\n///   at target-pos 0 and 1. Two confirms.\n/// - Ties go to the earlier source block → block 0. Within block 0,\n///   `привет` (target-pos 0) beats `здравствуйте` (target-pos 1).\nfn select_best_block<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n    blocks: Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>>,\n) -> Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> {\n    let target_wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(target_lang, http);\n    let mut block_positions: Vec<Vec<Option<usize>>> = Vec::with_capacity(blocks.len());\n    for (block_idx, block) in blocks.iter().enumerate() {\n        let mut positions: Vec<Option<usize>> = Vec::with_capacity(block.len());\n        for candidate in block {\n            let candidate_page = normalize_page_title(&candidate.surface);\n            if candidate_page.is_empty() {\n                positions.push(None);\n                continue;\n            }\n            let Ok(back_blocks) =\n                target_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&candidate_page, source_lang)\n            else {\n                positions.push(None);\n                continue;\n            };\n            // Within-block position: scan each block of the target page\n            // and record the position of the source surface inside the\n            // first block that contains it.\n            let mut within_block_position: Option<usize> = None;\n            for back_block in &back_blocks {\n                if let Some(pos) = back_block\n                    .iter()\n                    .position(|row| normalize_page_title(&row.surface) == page_title)\n                {\n                    within_block_position = Some(pos);\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(pos) = within_block_position {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{target_lang}:{candidate_page}#confirms->{source_lang}:{page_title}@{pos}[block{block_idx}]\"\n                ));\n            }\n            positions.push(within_block_position);\n        }\n        block_positions.push(positions);\n    }\n    let mut best_block: usize = 0;\n    let mut best_confirms: usize = 0;\n    for (idx, positions) in block_positions.iter().enumerate() {\n        let confirms = positions.iter().filter(|p| p.is_some()).count();\n        if confirms > best_confirms {\n            best_confirms = confirms;\n            best_block = idx;\n        }\n    }\n    let block = blocks.into_iter().nth(best_block).unwrap_or_default();\n    let positions = block_positions\n        .into_iter()\n        .nth(best_block)\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n    let mut indexed: Vec<(usize, Option<usize>, WiktionaryCandidate)> = block\n        .into_iter()\n        .zip(positions)\n        .enumerate()\n        .map(|(idx, (cand, pos))| (idx, pos, cand))\n        .collect();\n    indexed.sort_by_key(|(idx, pos, _)| {\n        pos.as_ref()\n            .map_or((1usize, 0, *idx), |p| (0usize, *p, *idx))\n    });\n    indexed.into_iter().map(|(_, _, cand)| cand).collect()\n}\n\n/// Upgrade a Wiktionary-only [`MeaningId`] to a Wikidata-backed one when\n/// SPARQL returns a lexeme that matches the surface in the upgrade_meaning_via_wikidata<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n    candidates: &mut Err(error) => {\n            provenance.push(format!(\"wikidata:search->error({error})\"));\n            return None;\n        }\n    };\n    let first = hits.first()?;\n    provenance.push(format!(\"wikidata:sparql->error({error})\"));\n            return Some(MeaningId::from_sense(first.id.clone()));\n        }\n    };\n    if !lemmas.is_empty() {\n {\n        let candidate = WiktionaryCandidate {\n            surface: lemma.value,\n            qualifier: None,\n        };\n        if !candidates.iter().any(|c| c.surface == candidate.surface) {\n            candidates.push(candidate);\n        }\n    }\n    Some(MeaningId::from_sense(first.id.clone()))\n}\n\nfn compositional_candidates(\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n) -> Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> {\n    if !source_lang.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"ru\") || !target_lang.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"en\") {\n        return \"compositional:ru->en:{page_title}=>variant:{variant}\"\n            ));\n            return vec![WiktionaryCandidate {\n                surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                qualifier: translated.push(surface);\n    }\n\n    let surface = capitalize_ascii_first(&translated.join(\" \"));\n    provenance.push(format!(\"compositional:ru->en:{page_title}\"));\n [2026-05-22T11:07:12.049Z] [INFO]       "content": "//! Translation pipeline.\n//!\n//! Public entry point: [`TranslationPipeline::translate`].\n//!\n//! ## Stages\n//!\n//! 1. **Formalize** — `formalize(source_surface, source_lang)` projects the\n//!    natural-language surface into a [`MeaningId`] by consulting\n//!    Wiktionary (for the page that defines the lemma) and Wikidata\n//!    (for the language-neutral Q-item or Lexeme sense). The\n//!    [`MeaningId`] is the semantic meta-language identifier; it never\n//!    embeds any single language.\n//!\n//! 2. **Deformalize** — `deformalize(meaning_id, target_lang)` renders a\n//!    surface form in the target language by:\n//!\n//!    a. running a Wikidata SPARQL lexeme-join (P5137) when the meaning\n//!    is backed by a Wikidata lexeme, **or**\n//!\n//!    b. parsing the source-edition Wiktionary translation table for\n//!    the target language code, **or**\n//!\n//!    c. parsing the target-edition Wiktionary's `=== Перевод ===` /\n//!    `===Translations===` block in reverse.\n//!\n//! [`Translation`], so the resulting links-notation trace shows\n//! exactly which API responses fed the answer.\n\nuse super::dictionary;\nuse super::http::{HttpClient, HttpError};\nuse super::meaning::MeaningId;\nuse super::wikidata::Wikidata;\nuse super::wiktionary::{Wiktionary, WiktionaryCandidate};\n\n/// `true` when `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` is set in the environment.\n///\n/// Reading the env var on every call would be wasteful, but tests rely on\n/// per-process toggling, so we re-check each call here (cheap stdlib lookup).\nfn translation_debug_enabled() -> bool {\n    std::env::var(\"FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG\")\n        .ok()\n        .is_some_and(|value| !value.is_empty() && value != \"0\")\n}\n\n/// Emit a structured debug line to stderr when\n/// `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1`. The Wikidata SPARQL lexeme join (`P5137`)\n/// returns the first matching lexeme regardless of part of speech, so\n/// common noun ↔ verb homographs (e.g. English `milk` → Russian\n/// `доить` \"to milk\", `water` → `поливать` \"to water\") land on the\n/// verb. Each tuple is\n/// `(source_lang, lemma_lower, target_lang, canonical_noun_surface)`.\nconst POLYSEMY_OVERRIDES: &[(&str, &str, &str, &str)] = &[\n    // English nouns where Wikidata returned the verb (\"en\", \"fish\", \"ru\", \"рыба\"),\n    (\"en\", \"friend\", \"ru\", \"друг\"),\n    (\"en\", \"phone\", \"ru\", \"телефон\"),\n    (\"en\", \"salt\", \"ru\", \"соль\"),\n    (\"en\", \"grape\", (*canonical).to_owned(),\n                    qualifier: None,\n                },\n            );\n            provenance.push(format!(\n Borrows a single HTTP client (typically a\n/// `CachedHttpClient`) for every Wiktionary and Wikidata call.\npub struct TranslationPipeline<'a, T: HttpClient + ?Sized> {\n    http: &'a T,\n}\n\nimpl<'a, T: HttpClient + ?Sized> TranslationPipeline<'a, T> {\n    pub const fn new(http: &'a T) -> Self {\n        Self { http }\n    }\n\n    /// Translate `surface` from `source_lang` to `target_lang`.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Ok(Translation)` even when the candidate list is empty\n    /// — callers can detect translation gaps by inspecting\n    /// [`Translation::candidates`].\n    pub fn translate(\n        &self,\n        surface: &str,\n        source_lang: &str,\n        target_lang: &str,\n    ) -> Result<Translation, HttpError> {\n        translation_debug(\n            \"translate\",\n            &format!(\"start surface={surface:?} {source_lang}->{target_lang}\"),\n        );\n        if source_lang == target_lang {\n            translation_debug(\"translate\", \"identity (source==target)\");\n            return Ok(Translation {\n                source_surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                source_lang: source_lang.to_owned(),\n                target_lang: target_lang.to_owned(),\n                meaning: MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, surface),\n                candidates: vec![WiktionaryCandidate {\n                    surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                    qualifier: None,\n                }],\n                provenance: vec![\"identity\".to_owned()],\n            });\n        }\n\n        let mut provenance: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        let page_title = normalize_page_title(surface);\n        translation_debug(\"translate\", &format!(\"page_title={page_title:?}\"));\n\n        // Stage 0: consult the offline dictionary first. Misses fall through to the live HTTP\n        // stages below; the same surface is matched against the entry's\n        // canonical lemma and its inflected aliases.\n        let dict =           .unwrap_or(page_title.as_str());\n            provenance.push(format!(\n                \"dictionary:{source_lang}:{lemma}->{target_lang}:{target_surface}\"\n            ));\n            translation_debug(\n                \"stage0\",\n                &format!(\"dictionary hit {source_lang}:{lemma}->{target_lang}:{target_surface}\"),\n            );\n            return Ok(Translation {\n                source_surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                source_lang: source_lang.to_owned(),\n                target_lang: target_lang.to_owned(),\n                meaning: MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, lemma),\n                candidates: vec![WiktionaryCandidate {\n                    surface: target_surface.to_owned(),\n                    qualifier: MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &page_title);\n        match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&page_title, target_lang) {\n            Ok(found) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{page_title}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                ));\n                translation_debug(\"stage1\", \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{subpage}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                    ));\n                    blocks = found;\n                }\n                Ok(_) => {}\n                Err(error) => {\n                    provenance.push(format!(\n                        \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{subpage}#translations->error({error})\",\n                    ));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1b: when the source-edition table came up empty, try the\n        // target-edition Wiktionary in reverse. The target page lists\n        // the source language under its own translation block — useful\n        // when the source edition is sparse (common for ru → en).\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            if let Some(reverse) = reverse_lookup(\n                self.http,\n                surface,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n            ) {\n                blocks = reverse;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1d: phrasal-variant fallback. Some natural phrases don't\n        // have their own Wiktionary entry (e.g. ru:\"как у тебя дела\") but\n        // a shorter canonical form does (ru:\"как дела\"). Stop\n        // at the first variant that produces at least one block.\n        let mut active_page_title = page_title.clone();\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            for variant in phrasal_variants(&page_title, source_lang) {\n                provenance.push(format!(\"wiktionary:{source_lang}:variant->{variant}\"));\n                match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&variant, target_lang) {\n                    Ok(found) if !found.is_empty() => {\n                        provenance.push(format!(\n                            \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{variant}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                        ));\n                        blocks = found;\n                        active_page_title.clone_from(&variant);\n                        meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &variant);\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    Ok(_) => {}\n                    Err(error) => {\n                        provenance.push(format!(\n                            \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{variant}#translations->error({error})\"\n                        ));\n                    }\n                }\n                if let Some(reverse) = reverse_lookup(\n                    self.http,\n                    &variant,\n                    source_lang,\n                    target_lang,\n                    &mut provenance,\n                ) {\n                    blocks = reverse;\n                    active_page_title.clone_from(&variant);\n                    meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &variant);\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1c: pick the most likely sense block when the source word\n        // is polysemous (multiple blocks). For each block, count how\n        // many candidates round-trip — that is, how many target-edition\n        // pages list the source surface as a translation. The block with\n        // the highest confirmation rate wins; ties fall back to source\n        // order.\n        let candidates = if blocks.is_empty() {\n            Vec::new()\n        } else {\n            select_best_block(\n                self.http,\n                &active_page_title,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n                blocks,\n            )\n        };\n\n        // Stage 2: pull the Wikidata Q-item / Lexeme sense — even if\n        // we already have a translation surface, we want the trace to\n        // expose the canonical meaning id. We open the page that\n/// is most likely to *exist* on the target edition for the source word.\n/// Russian Wiktionary, for instance, hosts pages for Russian words and\n/// records their translations into other languages under\n/// `=== Перевод ===`.\nfn reverse_lookup<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    surface: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n) -> Option<Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>>> {\n    let page_title = normalize_page_title(surface);\n    for edition in [source_lang, target_lang] {\n        let wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(edition, http);\n        match wiktionary.translation_blocks(&page_title, target_lang) {\n            Ok(blocks) if !blocks.is_empty() => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{edition}:{page_title}#reverse->{target_lang}\"\n                ));\n                return Some(blocks);\n            }\n            Ok(_) => {}\n            Err(error) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{edition}:{page_title}#reverse->error({error})\"\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Pick the best sense block from `blocks` by round-trip confirmation rate.\n///\n/// Each candidate's \"round-trip position\" is its index within the\n/// target-edition block that contains the source surface (not the\n/// flattened candidate list). Lower position = the target considers the\n/// source more primary.\n///\n/// Block-level selection picks the block with the most round-trip\n/// confirmations (ties broken by source order). Within the chosen block,\n/// candidates are sorted by `(target_position_within_block, source_idx)`.\n///\n/// Worked example — `en:hello`:\n/// - Block 0 (\"greeting\"): `привет` confirms at target-pos 0,\n///   `здравствуйте` at target-pos 1. Two confirms.\n/// - Block 1 (\"when answering the telephone\"): `алло` and `алё` confirm\n///   at target-pos 0 and 1. Two confirms.\n/// - Ties go to the earlier source block → block 0. Within block 0,\n///   `привет` (target-pos 0) beats `здравствуйте` (target-pos 1).\nfn select_best_block<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n    blocks: Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>>,\n) -> Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> {\n    let target_wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(target_lang, http);\n    let mut block_positions: Vec<Vec<Option<usize>>> = Vec::with_capacity(blocks.len());\n    for (block_idx, block) in blocks.iter().enumerate() {\n        let mut positions: Vec<Option<usize>> = Vec::with_capacity(block.len());\n        for candidate in block {\n            let candidate_page = normalize_page_title(&candidate.surface);\n            if candidate_page.is_empty() {\n                positions.push(None);\n                continue;\n            }\n            let Ok(back_blocks) =\n                target_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&candidate_page, source_lang)\n            else {\n                positions.push(None);\n                continue;\n            };\n            // Within-block position: scan each block of the target page\n            // and record the position of the source surface inside the\n            // first block that contains it.\n            let mut within_block_position: Option<usize> = None;\n            for back_block in &back_blocks {\n                if let Some(pos) = back_block\n                    .iter()\n                    .position(|row| normalize_page_title(&row.surface) == page_title)\n                {\n                    within_block_position = Some(pos);\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(pos) = within_block_position {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{target_lang}:{candidate_page}#confirms->{source_lang}:{page_title}@{pos}[block{block_idx}]\"\n                ));\n            }\n            positions.push(within_block_position);\n        }\n        block_positions.push(positions);\n    }\n    let mut best_block: usize = 0;\n    let mut best_confirms: usize = 0;\n    for (idx, positions) in block_positions.iter().enumerate() {\n        let confirms = positions.iter().filter(|p| p.is_some()).count();\n        if confirms > best_confirms {\n            best_confirms = confirms;\n            best_block = idx;\n        }\n    }\n    let block = blocks.into_iter().nth(best_block).unwrap_or_default();\n    let positions = block_positions\n        .into_iter()\n        .nth(best_block)\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n    let mut indexed: Vec<(usize, Option<usize>, WiktionaryCandidate)> = block\n        .into_iter()\n        .zip(positions)\n        .enumerate()\n        .map(|(idx, (cand, pos))| (idx, pos, cand))\n        .collect();\n    indexed.sort_by_key(|(idx, pos, _)| {\n        pos.as_ref()\n            .map_or((1usize, 0, *idx), |p| (0usize, *p, *idx))\n    });\n    indexed.into_iter().map(|(_, _, cand)| cand).collect()\n}\n\n/// Upgrade a Wiktionary-only [`MeaningId`] to a Wikidata-backed one when\n/// SPARQL returns a lexeme that matches the surface in the upgrade_meaning_via_wikidata<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n    candidates: &mut Err(error) => {\n            provenance.push(format!(\"wikidata:search->error({error})\"));\n            return None;\n        }\n    };\n    let first = hits.first()?;\n    provenance.push(format!(\"wikidata:sparql->error({error})\"));\n            return Some(MeaningId::from_sense(first.id.clone()));\n        }\n    };\n    if !lemmas.is_empty() {\n            candidates.push(candidate);\n        }\n    }\n    Some(MeaningId::from_sense(first.id.clone()))\n}\n\nfn compositional_candidates(\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n) -> Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> {\n    if !source_lang.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"ru\") || !target_lang.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"en\") {\n        return translated.push(surface);\n    }\n\n    let surface = capitalize_ascii_first(&translated.join(\" \"));\n    provenance.push(format!(\"compositional:ru->en:{page_title}\"));\n The query is robust because it\n    /// does not depend on P5972 (\"translation\") which is sparsely\n    /// populated.\n    pub fn lexeme_translations(\n        &self,\n        source_lexeme_id: &str,\n        target_lang_iso: &str,\n    ) -> Result<Vec<SparqlLemma>, HttpError> {\n        let query = format!(\n            \"SELECT DISTINCT ?lemma WHERE {{ \\\n               wd:{source_lexeme_id} ontolex:sense ?source_sense . \\\n               ?source_sense wdt:P5137 ?meaning . \\\n               ?lexeme ontolex:sense ?sense . \\\n               ?sense wdt:P5137 ?meaning . \\\n               ?lexeme dct:language ?language . \\\n               ?language wdt:P218 \\\"{target_lang_iso}\\\" . \\\n               ?lexeme wikibase:lemma ?lemma . \\\n             }}\"\n        );\n        let body = self.sparql(&query)?;\n        Ok(parse_sparql_lemmas(&body))\n    }\n\n    /// Search for a Lexeme by lemma on a specific language.\n    pub fn search_lexeme(\n        &self,\n        lemma: &str,\n        language_iso: &str,\n    ) -> Result<Vec<LexemeSearchHit>, HttpError> {\n        let url = format!(\n            \"https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities\\\n             &search={lemma}&language={lang}&type=lexeme&format=json\\\n             &uselang={lang}&limit=5\",\n            lemma = query_encode(lemma),\n            lang = query_encode(language_iso),\n        );\n        let body = self.http.get(&url)?;\n        Ok(parse_wbsearch_hits(&body))\n    }\n}\n\n/// One row of a SPARQL SELECT result for `?lemma`. The `xml:lang` tag is\n/// preserved so callers can distinguish multiple forms returned for the\n/// same lexeme.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct SparqlLemma {\n    pub value: String,\n    pub language: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// One hit from `action=wbsearchentities&type=lexeme`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct LexemeSearchHit {\n    pub id: String,\n    pub label: String,\n}\n\n/// Parse the bindings array of a SPARQL `SELECT ?lemma` result.\n///\n/// We do a targeted string scan rather than full JSON parsing — the\n/// structure is fixed and pulling in `serde_json::Value` for one shape\n/// would be heavyweight. The scan handles unicode escapes via the\n/// wiktionary JSON-string decoder helper.\n#[must_use]\npub fn parse_sparql_lemmas(body: &str) -> Vec<SparqlLemma> {\n    let mut out: Vec<SparqlLemma> = Vec::new();\n    let mut cursor = 0usize;\n    while let Some(start) = body[cursor..].find(\"\\\"lemma\\\"\") {\n        let absolute = cursor + start;\n        // The lemma binding is encoded as a JSON object such as\n        // `{\"xml:lang\": \"ru\", \"type\": \"literal\", \"value\": \"привет\"}`. Returns the\n/// byte offset of the closing brace (inclusive of itself).\nfn find_matching_brace(input: &str) -> Option<usize> {\n    let bytes = input.as_bytes();\n    if bytes.is_empty() || bytes[0] != b'{' {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let mut depth: u32 = 0;\n    let mut in_string = false;\n    let mut escape = false;\n    for (offset, byte) in bytes.iter().enumerate() {\n        if escape {\n            escape = false;\n            continue;\n        }\n        match (*byte, in_string) {\n            (b'\\\\', true) => escape = true,\n            (b'\"', _) => in_string = !in_string,\n            (b'{', false) => depth += 1,\n            (b'}', false) => {\n                depth -= 1;\n                if depth == 0 {\n                    return Some(offset + 1);\n All three roots are\n  gitignored — the cache is a local accelerator, not pre-seeded data —\n  so the PR diff stays under 3,000 files. Other formalisation flows\n  (entity resolution, fact lookup) reuse the same buckets.\n- `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs` seed list expanded so the\n  offline cache covers the full demo vocabulary, writing into the new\n  semantic-keyed cache root (`data/` by default).\n- `tests/unit/docs_requirements.rs` exempts the new cache roots when\n  scanning for deferred labels so raw Wiktionary bodies (which contain\n  three-letter ISO 639-3 language codes that coincide with deferred-label\n  vocabulary) don't trip the scanner.\n\nCase study and provenance live in `docs/case-studies/issue-221/`.\n",

Indentation contract:\n730\t  //   formal_ai_seed_bundle             (top-level, indent 0)\n731\t  //     file \"data/seed/X.lino\"         (indent 2)\n732\t  //       <line of X.lino>              (indent 4)\n733\t  //       <line of X.lino>\n734\t  //     file \"data/seed/Y.lino\"\n735\t  //       ...\n736\t  function parseBundle(text) {\n737\t    var lines = String(text || \"\").split(/\\r?\\n/);\n738\t    var sections = [];\n739\t    var current = null;\n740\t    for (var i = 0; i < lines.length; i += 1) {\n741\t      var line = lines[i];\n742\t      if (line === \"\") {\n743\t        if (current) current.text += \"\\n\";\n744\t        continue;\n745\t      }\n746\t      var indentMatch = /^(\\s*)/.exec(line);\n747\t      var indent = indentMatch ? verb-shaped.\n    (\"en\", \"phone\", \"hi\", \"फ़ोन\"),\n    // Russian nouns where the ru→en mapping landed on a non-canonical\n    // English noun (e.g. язык → \"tongue\" rather than target) triple matches, move the canonical noun to the\n/// front so [`Translation::primary_surface`] returns it.\nfn apply_polysemy_override(\n    surface: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    candidates: &mut Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n) {\n    let key = surface.to_lowercase();\n    for (src, lemma, tgt, canonical) in POLYSEMY_OVERRIDES {\n        if *src == source_lang && *tgt == target_lang && *lemma == key {\n            // Remove existing entries for the canonical surface, then\n            // push it at the front.\n            candidates.retain(|c| c.surface != *canonical);\n            candidates.insert(\n                0,\n                WiktionaryCandidate {\n                    surface: (*canonical).to_owned(),\n                    qualifier: None,\n                },\n            );\n            provenance.push(format!(\n                \"polysemy-override:{src}:{lemma}->{tgt}:{canonical}\"\n            ));\n            translation_debug(\n                \"polysemy\",\n                &format!(\"override {src}:{lemma}->{tgt} = {canonical}\"),\n            );\n            return;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Result of a translation request.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Translation {\n    pub source_surface: String,\n    pub source_lang: String,\n    pub target_lang: String,\n    pub meaning: MeaningId,\n    pub candidates: Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>,\n    pub provenance: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl Translation {\n    /// The best target-language surface form. Picks the first\n    /// unqualified candidate, falling back to the first candidate.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn primary_surface(&self) -> Option<&str> {\n        self.candidates\n            .iter()\n            .find(|c| c.qualifier.is_none())\n            .or_else(|| self.candidates.first())\n            .map(|c| c.surface.as_str())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Translation pipeline. Borrows a single HTTP client (typically a\n/// `CachedHttpClient`) for every Wiktionary and Wikidata call.\npub struct TranslationPipeline<'a, T: HttpClient + ?Sized> {\n    http: &'a T,\n}\n\nimpl<'a, T: HttpClient + ?Sized> TranslationPipeline<'a, T> {\n    pub const fn new(http: &'a T) -> Self {\n        Self { http }\n    }\n\n    /// Translate `surface` from `source_lang` to `target_lang`.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Ok(Translation)` even when the candidate list is empty\n    /// — callers can detect translation gaps by inspecting\n    /// [`Translation::candidates`].\n    pub fn translate(\n        &self,\n        surface: &str,\n        source_lang: &str,\n        target_lang: &str,\n    ) -> Result<Translation, HttpError> {\n        translation_debug(\n            \"translate\",\n            &format!(\"start surface={surface:?} {source_lang}->{target_lang}\"),\n        );\n        if source_lang == target_lang {\n            translation_debug(\"translate\", \"identity (source==target)\");\n            return Ok(Translation {\n                source_surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                source_lang: source_lang.to_owned(),\n                target_lang: target_lang.to_owned(),\n                meaning: MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, surface),\n                candidates: vec![WiktionaryCandidate {\n                    surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                    qualifier: None,\n                }],\n                provenance: vec![\"identity\".to_owned()],\n            });\n        }\n\n        let mut provenance: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        let page_title = normalize_page_title(surface);\n        translation_debug(\"translate\", &format!(\"page_title={page_title:?}\"));\n\n        // Stage 0: consult the offline dictionary first. The 128-noun\n        // `.lino` registry catches the most frequent words without a\n        // network round trip, which keeps the browser worker responsive\n        // and CI deterministic. Misses fall through to the live HTTP\n        // stages below; the same surface is matched against the entry's\n        // canonical lemma and its inflected aliases.\n        let dict = dictionary::shared();\n        if let Some(target_surface) = dict.lookup(&page_title, source_lang, target_lang) {\n            let lemma = dict\n                .lemma(&page_title, source_lang)\n                .unwrap_or(page_title.as_str());\n            provenance.push(format!(\n                \"dictionary:{source_lang}:{lemma}->{target_lang}:{target_surface}\"\n            ));\n            translation_debug(\n                \"stage0\",\n                &format!(\"dictionary hit {source_lang}:{lemma}->{target_lang}:{target_surface}\"),\n            );\n            return Ok(Translation {\n                source_surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                source_lang: source_lang.to_owned(),\n                target_lang: target_lang.to_owned(),\n                meaning: MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, lemma),\n                candidates: vec![WiktionaryCandidate {\n                    surface: target_surface.to_owned(),\n                    qualifier: None,\n                }],\n                provenance,\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1: formalize — fetch the source-edition Wiktionary page.\n        // This single fetch usually carries translations for every target\n        // language, grouped by sense (one block per `{{trans-top}}` on\n        // English Wiktionary, one per `{{перев-блок}}` on Russian).\n        let source_wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(source_lang, self.http);\n        let mut blocks: Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>> = Vec::new();\n        let mut meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &page_title);\n        match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&page_title, target_lang) {\n            Ok(found) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{page_title}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                ));\n                translation_debug(\"stage1\", &format!(\"source-edition blocks={}\", found.len()));\n                if !found.is_empty() {\n                    blocks = found;\n                }\n            }\n            Err(error) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{page_title}#translations->error({error})\",\n                ));\n                translation_debug(\"stage1\", &format!(\"source-edition error: {error}\"));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1a: many high-traffic pages keep translations on a\n        // `/translations` subpage (`{{see translation subpage|...}}`).\n        // Try that subpage when the main page yielded nothing.\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            let subpage = format!(\"{page_title}/translations\");\n            match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&subpage, target_lang) {\n                Ok(found) if !found.is_empty() => {\n                    provenance.push(format!(\n                        \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{subpage}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                    ));\n                    blocks = found;\n                }\n                Ok(_) => {}\n                Err(error) => {\n                    provenance.push(format!(\n                        \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{subpage}#translations->error({error})\",\n                    ));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1b: when the source-edition table came up empty, try the\n        // target-edition Wiktionary in reverse. The target page lists\n        // the source language under its own translation block — useful\n        // when the source edition is sparse (common for ru → en).\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            if let Some(reverse) = reverse_lookup(\n                self.http,\n                surface,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n            ) {\n                blocks = reverse;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1d: phrasal-variant fallback. Some natural phrases don't\n        // have their own Wiktionary entry (e.g. ru:\"как у тебя дела\") but\n        // a shorter canonical form does (ru:\"как дела\"). Generate\n        // alternate forms by stripping language-specific filler\n        // sub-phrases and retry Stages 1 + 1a + 1b on each variant. Stop\n        // at the first variant that produces at least one block.\n        let mut active_page_title = page_title.clone();\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            for variant in phrasal_variants(&page_title, source_lang) {\n                provenance.push(format!(\"wiktionary:{source_lang}:variant->{variant}\"));\n                match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&variant, target_lang) {\n                    Ok(found) if !found.is_empty() => {\n                        provenance.push(format!(\n                            \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{variant}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                        ));\n                        blocks = found;\n                        active_page_title.clone_from(&variant);\n                        meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &variant);\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    Ok(_) => {}\n                    Err(error) => {\n                        provenance.push(format!(\n                            \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{variant}#translations->error({error})\"\n                        ));\n                    }\n                }\n                if let Some(reverse) = reverse_lookup(\n                    self.http,\n                    &variant,\n                    source_lang,\n                    target_lang,\n                    &mut provenance,\n                ) {\n                    blocks = reverse;\n                    active_page_title.clone_from(&variant);\n                    meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &variant);\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1c: pick the most likely sense block when the source word\n        // is polysemous (multiple blocks). For each block, count how\n        // many candidates round-trip — that is, how many target-edition\n        // pages list the source surface as a translation. The block with\n        // the highest confirmation rate wins; ties fall back to source\n        // order.\n        let candidates = if blocks.is_empty() {\n            Vec::new()\n        } else {\n            select_best_block(\n                self.http,\n                &active_page_title,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n                blocks,\n            )\n        };\n\n        // Stage 2: pull the Wikidata Q-item / Lexeme sense — even if\n        // we already have a translation surface, we want the trace to\n        // expose the canonical meaning id. Failures here do not block\n        // the translation.\n        let mut candidates = candidates;\n        if let Some(updated) = upgrade_meaning_via_wikidata(\n            self.http,\n            &active_page_title,\n            source_lang,\n            target_lang,\n            &mut provenance,\n            &mut candidates,\n        ) {\n            meaning = updated;\n        }\n\n        if candidates.is_empty() {\n            candidates = compositional_candidates(\n                &active_page_title,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Polysemy: when the lemma is a known noun↔verb homograph,\n        // promote the canonical noun translation to the front of the\n        // candidate list. See [`POLYSEMY_OVERRIDES`].\n        apply_polysemy_override(\n            &active_page_title,\n            source_lang,\n            target_lang,\n            &mut candidates,\n            &mut provenance,\n        );\n\n        translation_debug(\n            \"translate\",\n            &format!(\n                \"done candidates={} primary={:?} meaning={:?}\",\n                candidates.len(),\n                candidates\n                    .iter()\n                    .find(|c| c.qualifier.is_none())\n                    .or_else(|| candidates.first())\n                    .map(|c| c.surface.as_str()),\n                meaning,\n            ),\n        );\n        Ok(Translation {\n            source_surface: surface.to_owned(),\n            source_lang: source_lang.to_owned(),\n            target_lang: target_lang.to_owned(),\n            meaning,\n            candidates,\n            provenance,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// Try the target-edition Wiktionary in reverse. We open the page that\n/// is most likely to *exist* on the target edition for the source word.\n/// Russian Wiktionary, for instance, hosts pages for Russian words and\n/// records their translations into other languages under\n/// `=== Перевод ===`.\nfn reverse_lookup<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    surface: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n) -> Option<Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>>> {\n    let page_title = normalize_page_title(surface);\n    for edition in [source_lang, target_lang] {\n        let wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(edition, http);\n        match wiktionary.translation_blocks(&page_title, target_lang) {\n            Ok(blocks) if !blocks.is_empty() => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{edition}:{page_title}#reverse->{target_lang}\"\n                ));\n                return Some(blocks);\n            }\n            Ok(_) => {}\n            Err(error) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{edition}:{page_title}#reverse->error({error})\"\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Pick the best sense block from `blocks` by round-trip confirmation rate.\n///\n/// Each candidate's \"round-trip position\" is its index within the\n/// target-edition block that contains the source surface (not the\n/// flattened candidate list). Lower position = the target considers the\n/// source more primary.\n///\n/// Block-level selection picks the block with the most round-trip\n/// confirmations (ties broken by source order). Within the chosen block,\n/// candidates are sorted by `(target_position_within_block, source_idx)`.\n///\n/// Worked example — `en:hello`:\n/// - Block 0 (\"greeting\"): `привет` confirms at target-pos 0,\n///   `здравствуйте` at target-pos 1. Two confirms.\n/// - Block 1 (\"when answering the telephone\"): `алло` and `алё` confirm\n///   at target-pos 0 and 1. Two confirms.\n/// - Ties go to the earlier source block → block 0. Within block 0,\n///   `привет` (target-pos 0) beats `здравствуйте` (target-pos 1).\nfn select_best_block<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n    blocks: Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>>,\n) -> Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> {\n    let target_wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(target_lang, http);\n    let mut block_positions: Vec<Vec<Option<usize>>> = Vec::with_capacity(blocks.len());\n    for (block_idx, block) in blocks.iter().enumerate() {\n        let mut positions: Vec<Option<usize>> = Vec::with_capacity(block.len());\n        for candidate in block {\n            let candidate_page = normalize_page_title(&candidate.surface);\n            if candidate_page.is_empty() {\n                positions.push(None);\n                continue;\n            }\n            let Ok(back_blocks) =\n                target_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&candidate_page, source_lang)\n            else {\n                positions.push(None);\n                continue;\n            };\n            // Within-block position: scan each block of the target page\n            // and record the position of the source surface inside the\n            // first block that contains it.\n            let mut within_block_position: Option<usize> = None;\n            for back_block in &back_blocks {\n                if let Some(pos) = back_block\n                    .iter()\n                    .position(|row| normalize_page_title(&row.surface) == page_title)\n                {\n                    within_block_position = Some(pos);\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(pos) = within_block_position {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{target_lang}:{candidate_page}#confirms->{source_lang}:{page_title}@{pos}[block{block_idx}]\"\n                ));\n            }\n            positions.push(within_block_position);\n        }\n        block_positions.push(positions);\n    }\n    let mut best_block: usize = 0;\n    let mut best_confirms: usize = 0;\n    for (idx, positions) in block_positions.iter().enumerate() {\n        let confirms = positions.iter().filter(|p| p.is_some()).count();\n        if confirms > best_confirms {\n            best_confirms = confirms;\n            best_block = idx;\n        }\n    }\n    let block = blocks.into_iter().nth(best_block).unwrap_or_default();\n    let positions = block_positions\n        .into_iter()\n        .nth(best_block)\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n    let mut indexed: Vec<(usize, Option<usize>, WiktionaryCandidate)> = block\n        .into_iter()\n        .zip(positions)\n        .enumerate()\n        .map(|(idx, (cand, pos))| (idx, pos, cand))\n        .collect();\n    indexed.sort_by_key(|(idx, pos, _)| {\n        pos.as_ref()\n            .map_or((1usize, 0, *idx), |p| (0usize, *p, *idx))\n    });\n    indexed.into_iter().map(|(_, _, cand)| cand).collect()\n}\n\n/// Upgrade a Wiktionary-only [`MeaningId`] to a Wikidata-backed one when\n/// SPARQL returns a lexeme that matches the surface in the source\n/// language. Also appends any extra lemma forms returned by the\n/// translation query — they are stored as additional candidates so\n/// callers can disambiguate (formal vs informal, dialect, etc).\nfn upgrade_meaning_via_wikidata<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n    candidates: &mut Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>,\n) -> Option<MeaningId> {\n    let wikidata = Wikidata::new(http);\n    let hits = match wikidata.search_lexeme(page_title, source_lang) {\n        Ok(hits) => hits,\n        Err(error) => {\n            provenance.push(format!(\"wikidata:search->error({error})\"));\n            return None;\n        }\n    };\n    let first = hits.first()?;\n    provenance.push(format!(\"wikidata:lexeme:{}\", first.id));\n    let lemmas = match wikidata.lexeme_translations(&first.id, target_lang) {\n        Ok(rows) => rows,\n        Err(error) => {\n            provenance.push(format!(\"wikidata:sparql->error({error})\"));\n            return Some(MeaningId::from_sense(first.id.clone()));\n        }\n    };\n    if !lemmas.is_empty() {\n        provenance.push(format!(\n            \"wikidata:sparql:{}->{} ({} lemmas)\",\n            first.id,\n            target_lang,\n            lemmas.len()\n        ));\n    }\n    for lemma in lemmas {\n        let candidate = WiktionaryCandidate {\n            surface: lemma.value,\n            qualifier: None,\n        };\n        if !candidates.iter().any(|c| c.surface == candidate.surface) {\n            candidates.push(candidate);\n        }\n    }\n    Some(MeaningId::from_sense(first.id.clone()))\n}\n\nfn compositional_candidates(\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n) -> Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> {\n    if !source_lang.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"ru\") || !target_lang.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"en\") {\n        return Vec::new();\n    }\n\n    if let Some(surface) = russian_phrase_to_english(page_title) {\n        provenance.push(format!(\"compositional:ru->en:{page_title}\"));\n        return vec![WiktionaryCandidate {\n            surface: surface.to_owned(),\n            qualifier: None,\n        }];\n    }\n\n    // The HTTP variant fallback already tried `phrasal_variants` against\n    // Wiktionary; reuse the same elision rules for the compositional\n    // table so politeness-marked phrases like `как у тебя дела` collapse\n    // to the canonical `как дела` entry.\n    for variant in phrasal_variants(page_title, source_lang) {\n        if let Some(surface) = russian_phrase_to_english(&variant) {\n            provenance.push(format!(\n                \"compositional:ru->en:{page_title}=>variant:{variant}\"\n            ));\n            return vec![WiktionaryCandidate {\n                surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                qualifier: None,\n            }];\n        }\n    }\n\n    let words: Vec<&str> = page_title.split_whitespace().collect();\n    if !(2..=4).contains(&words.len()) {\n        return Vec::new();\n    }\n\n    let mut translated = Vec::with_capacity(words.len());\n    for word in words {\n        let Some(surface) = russian_word_to_english(word) else {\n            return Vec::new();\n        };\n        translated.push(surface);\n    }\n\n    let surface = capitalize_ascii_first(&translated.join(\" \"));\n    provenance.push(format!(\"compositional:ru->en:{page_title}\"));\n    vec![WiktionaryCandidate {\n        surface,\n        qualifier: None,\n    }]\n}\n\nfn russian_phrase_to_english(page_title: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {\n    match page_title {\n        \"кто ты\" | \"кто ты такой\" | \"кто ты такая\" | \"кто вы\" | \"кто вы такой\" | \"кто вы такая\" => {\n            Some(\"Who are you?\")\n        }\n        \"что это\" | \"что это такое\" => Some(\"What is this?\"),\n        // Russian small-talk variants → \"how are you\". `phrasal_variants`\n        // strips the dative-of-possession infix (`у тебя`, `у вас`, …)\n        // so callers may arrive at the bare `как дела` form.\n        \"как дела\" => Some(\"how are you\"),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\nfn russian_word_to_english(word: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {\n    match word {\n        \"доброе\" | \"добрый\" | \"добрая\" | \"добрые\" | \"доброго\" | \"добрую\" | \"добрым\" | \"хорошее\"\n        | \"хороший\" | \"хорошая\" | \"хорошие\" | \"хорошего\" | \"хорошую\" | \"хорошим\" => {\n            Some(\"good\")\n        }\n        \"яблоко\" | \"яблока\" | \"яблоку\" | \"яблоком\" | \"яблоке\" | \"яблоки\" | \"яблок\" | \"яблокам\"\n        | \"яблоками\" | \"яблоках\" => Some(\"apple\"),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\nfn capitalize_ascii_first(surface: &str) -> String {\n    let mut chars = surface.chars();\n    let Some(first) = chars.next() else {\n        return String::new();\n    };\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(surface.len());\n    out.extend(first.to_uppercase());\n    out.extend(chars);\n    out\n}\n\n/// Generate alternate phrasal forms to retry when the original page is\n/// missing on Wiktionary.\n///\n/// Languages differ in which optional words can be elided without\n/// changing meaning. We encode the elisions per source language; for now\n/// we cover Russian (`у тебя/у вас/у нас/...` infix between question word\n/// and noun).\n///\n/// Variants are returned in priority order — the caller stops at the\n/// first one that produces translations.\n#[must_use]\npub fn phrasal_variants(page_title: &str, source_lang: &str) -> Vec<String> {\n    let mut variants: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n    if source_lang.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"ru\") {\n        // Russian dative-of-possession infix: `как у тебя дела` and\n        // `как у вас дела` collapse to the canonical `как дела`. This\n        // covers the politeness variants without changing semantics.\n        let pronouns = [\n            \"у тебя\",\n            \"у вас\",\n            \"у нас\",\n            \"у меня\",\n            \"у них\",\n            \"у него\",\n            \"у неё\",\n            \"у нее\",\n        ];\n        for pronoun in &pronouns {\n            // Strip the pronoun as a whole-word infix surrounded by spaces.\n            let needle = format!(\" {pronoun} \");\n            if let Some(idx) = page_title.find(&needle) {\n                let mut alt = String::with_capacity(page_title.len() - needle.len() + 1);\n                alt.push_str(&page_title[..idx]);\n                alt.push(' ');\n                alt.push_str(&page_title[idx + needle.len()..]);\n                let alt = alt.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(\" \");\n                if !alt.is_empty() && alt != page_title && !variants.contains(&alt) {\n                    variants.push(alt);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    variants\n}\n\n/// Normalize a surface fragment into a Wiktionary page title.\n///\n/// - Trim whitespace.\n/// - Strip terminal punctuation (`?`, `!`, `.`, `。`, `？`, `！`).\n/// - Lower-case the first letter (Wiktionary stores most page titles in\n///   lower case for content words; redirects handle the capitalized\n///   variants but we want a stable cache key).\n#[must_use]\npub fn normalize_page_title(surface: &str) -> String {\n    let trimmed = surface\n        .trim()\n        .trim_end_matches(['?', '!', '.', '。', '？', '！', '．']);\n    let mut chars = trimmed.chars();\n    let Some(first) = chars.next() else {\n        return String::new();\n    };\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(trimmed.len());\n    for character in first.to_lowercase() {\n        out.push(character);\n    }\n    out.extend(chars);\n    out\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use std::sync::Mutex;\n\n    struct StubHttp {\n        responses: Mutex<std::collections::HashMap<String, String>>,\n    }\n\n    impl StubHttp {\n        fn new(pairs: &[(&str,                    status: 404,\n                    body: format!(\"no stubbed response for {url}\"),\n                })\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn Err(error) => {\n                    provenance.push(format!(\n                        \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{subpage}#translations->error({error})\",\n                    ));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1b: when the source-edition table came up empty, try the\n        // target-edition Wiktionary in reverse. The target page lists\n        // the source language under its own translation block — useful\n        // when the source edition is sparse (common for ru → en).\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            if let Some(reverse) = reverse_lookup(\n                self.http,\n                surface,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n            ) {\n                blocks = reverse;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1d: phrasal-variant fallback. Some natural phrases don't\n        // have their own Wiktionary entry (e.g. ru:\"как у тебя дела\") but\n        // a shorter canonical form does (ru:\"как дела\"). Within block 0,\n///   `привет` (target-pos 0) beats `здравствуйте` (target-pos 1).\nfn select_best_block<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n    blocks: Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>>,\n) -> Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> {\n    let target_wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(target_lang, http);\n    positions.push(None);\n                continue;\n            }\n            let Ok(back_blocks) =\n                target_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&candidate_page, source_lang)\n                    \"wiktionary:{target_lang}:{candidate_page}#confirms->{source_lang}:{page_title}@{pos}[block{block_idx}]\"\n                ));\n            }\n            positions.push(within_block_position);\n        }\n        block_positions.push(positions);\n    }\n    let mut best_block: usize = 0;\n    let mut best_confirms: usize = 0;\n    for (idx, positions)     best_block = idx;\n        }\n    }\n    let block = blocks.into_iter().nth(best_block).unwrap_or_default();\n    let positions = block_positions\n        .into_iter()\n        .nth(best_block)\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n    let mut indexed: Vec<(usize, Option<usize>, WiktionaryCandidate)> = block\n        .into_iter()\n        .zip(positions)\n        .enumerate()\n        .map(|(idx, indexed.into_iter().map(|(_, _, cand)| cand).collect()\n}\n\n/// Upgrade a Wiktionary-only [`MeaningId`] to a Wikidata-backed one when\n/// SPARQL returns a lexeme that matches the surface in the upgrade_meaning_via_wikidata<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n    candidates: &mut Err(error) => {\n            provenance.push(format!(\"wikidata:search->error({error})\"));\n            return None;\n        }\n    };\n    let first = hits.first()?;\n [2026-05-22T11:13:46.057Z] [INFO]     "originalFile": "//! Translation pipeline.\n//!\n//! Public entry point: [`TranslationPipeline::translate`].\n//!\n//! ## Stages\n//!\n//! 1. **Formalize** — `formalize(source_surface, source_lang)` projects the\n//!    natural-language surface into a [`MeaningId`] by consulting\n//!    Wiktionary (for the page that defines the lemma) and Wikidata\n//!    (for the language-neutral Q-item or Lexeme sense). The\n//!    [`MeaningId`] is the semantic meta-language identifier; it never\n//!    embeds any single language.\n//!\n//! 2. **Deformalize** — `deformalize(meaning_id, target_lang)` renders a\n//!    surface form in the target language by:\n//!\n//!    a. running a Wikidata SPARQL lexeme-join (P5137) when the meaning\n//!    is backed by a Wikidata lexeme, **or**\n//!\n//!    b. parsing the source-edition Wiktionary translation table for\n//!    the target language code, **or**\n//!\n//!    c. parsing the target-edition Wiktionary's `=== Перевод ===` /\n//!    `===Translations===` block in reverse.\n//!\n//! Used to trace each pipeline stage\n/// when investigating issues like #221 (common-noun translation gaps).\nfn translation_debug(stage: &str, message: &str) {\n    if translation_debug_enabled() {\n        eprintln!(\"[formal-ai translation] {stage}: {message}\");\n    }\n}\n\n/// Result of a translation request.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Translation {\n    pub source_surface: String,\n    pub source_lang: String,\n    pub target_lang: String,\n    pub meaning: MeaningId,\n    pub candidates: Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>,\n    pub provenance: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl Translation {\n    /// The best target-language surface form. Picks the first\n    /// unqualified candidate, falling back to the first candidate.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn primary_surface(&self) -> Option<&str> {\n        self.candidates\n            .iter()\n            .find(|c| c.qualifier.is_none())\n            .or_else(|| self.candidates.first())\n            .map(|c| c.surface.as_str())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Translation pipeline. The 128-noun\n        // `.lino` registry catches the most frequent words without a\n        // network round trip, which keeps the browser worker responsive\n        // and CI deterministic. Misses fall through to the live HTTP\n        // stages below; the same surface is matched against the entry's\n        // canonical lemma and its inflected aliases.\n        let dict = dictionary::shared();\n        if let Some(target_surface) = dict.lookup(&page_title, source_lang, target_lang) {\n            let lemma = dict\n                .lemma(&page_title, source_lang)\n                .unwrap_or(page_title.as_str());\n            provenance.push(format!(\n                \"dictionary:{source_lang}:{lemma}->{target_lang}:{target_surface}\"\n            ));\n            translation_debug(\n                \"stage0\",\n                &format!(\"dictionary hit {source_lang}:{lemma}->{target_lang}:{target_surface}\"),\n            );\n            return Ok(Translation {\n                source_surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                source_lang: source_lang.to_owned(),\n                target_lang: target_lang.to_owned(),\n                meaning: MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, lemma),\n                candidates: vec![WiktionaryCandidate {\n                    surface: target_surface.to_owned(),\n                    qualifier: None,\n                }],\n                provenance,\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1: formalize — fetch the source-edition Wiktionary page.\n        // This single fetch usually carries translations for every target\n        // language, grouped by sense (one block per `{{trans-top}}` on\n        // English Wiktionary, one per `{{перев-блок}}` on Russian).\n        let source_wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(source_lang, self.http);\n        let mut blocks: Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>> = Vec::new();\n        let mut meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &page_title);\n        match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&page_title, target_lang) {\n            Ok(found) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{page_title}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                ));\n                translation_debug(\"stage1\", &format!(\"source-edition blocks={}\", found.len()));\n                if !found.is_empty() {\n                    blocks = found;\n                }\n            }\n            Err(error) => {\n &format!(\"source-edition error: {error}\"));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1a: many high-traffic pages keep translations on a\n        // `/translations` subpage (`{{see translation subpage|...}}`).\n        // Try that subpage when the main page yielded nothing.\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            let subpage = format!(\"{page_title}/translations\");\n            match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&subpage, target_lang) {\n                Ok(found) if !found.is_empty() => {\n                    provenance.push(format!(\n                        \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{subpage}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                    ));\n                    blocks = found;\n                }\n                Ok(_) => {}\n                Err(error) => {\n                    provenance.push(format!(\n                        \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{subpage}#translations->error({error})\",\n                    ));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1b: when the source-edition table came up empty, try the\n        // target-edition Wiktionary in reverse. The target page lists\n        // the source language under its own translation block — useful\n        // when the source edition is sparse (common for ru → en).\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            if let Some(reverse) = reverse_lookup(\n                self.http,\n                surface,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n            ) {\n                blocks = reverse;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1d: phrasal-variant fallback. Some natural phrases don't\n        // have their own Wiktionary entry (e.g. ru:\"как у тебя дела\") but\n        // a shorter canonical form does (ru:\"как дела\"). Generate\n        // alternate forms by stripping language-specific filler\n        // sub-phrases and retry Stages 1 + 1a + 1b on each variant. Stop\n        // at the first variant that produces at least one block.\n        let mut active_page_title = page_title.clone();\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            for variant in phrasal_variants(&page_title, source_lang) {\n                provenance.push(format!(\"wiktionary:{source_lang}:variant->{variant}\"));\n                match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&variant, target_lang) {\n                    Ok(found) if !found.is_empty() => {\n                        provenance.push(format!(\n                            \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{variant}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                        ));\n                        blocks = found;\n                        active_page_title.clone_from(&variant);\n                        meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &variant);\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    Ok(_) => {}\n                    Err(error) => {\n                        provenance.push(format!(\n                            \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{variant}#translations->error({error})\"\n                        ));\n                    }\n                }\n                if let Some(reverse) = reverse_lookup(\n                    self.http,\n                    &variant,\n                    source_lang,\n                    target_lang,\n                    &mut provenance,\n                ) {\n                    blocks = reverse;\n                    active_page_title.clone_from(&variant);\n                    meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &variant);\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1c: pick the most likely sense block when the source word\n        // is polysemous (multiple blocks). For each block, count how\n        // many candidates round-trip — that is, how many target-edition\n        // pages list the source surface as a translation. The block with\n        // the highest confirmation rate wins; ties fall back to source\n        // order.\n        let candidates = if blocks.is_empty() {\n            Vec::new()\n        } else {\n            select_best_block(\n                self.http,\n                &active_page_title,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n                blocks,\n            )\n        };\n\n        // Stage 2: pull the Wikidata Q-item / Lexeme sense — even if\n        // we already have a translation surface, we want the trace to\n        // expose the canonical meaning id.
