See [`POLYSEMY_OVERRIDES`].\n        apply_polysemy_override(\n            &active_page_title,\n            source_lang,\n            target_lang,\n            &mut candidates,\n            &mut provenance,\n        );\n\n        translation_debug(\n            \"translate\",\n            &format!(\n                \"done candidates={} primary={:?} meaning={:?}\",\n                candidates.len(),\n                candidates\n                    .iter()\n                    .find(|c| c.qualifier.is_none())\n                    .or_else(|| candidates.first())\n                    .map(|c| c.surface.as_str()),\n                meaning,\n            ),\n        );\n        Ok(Translation {\n            source_surface: surface.to_owned(),\n            source_lang: source_lang.to_owned(),\n            target_lang: target_lang.to_owned(),\n            meaning,\n            candidates,\n            provenance,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// Try the target-edition Wiktionary in reverse. We open the page that\n/// is most likely to *exist* on the target edition for the source word.\n/// Russian Wiktionary, for instance, hosts pages for Russian words and\n/// records their translations into other languages under\n/// `=== Перевод ===`.\nfn reverse_lookup<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    surface: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n) -> Option<Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>>> {\n    let page_title = normalize_page_title(surface);\n    for edition in [source_lang, target_lang] {\n        let wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(edition, http);\n        match wiktionary.translation_blocks(&page_title, target_lang) {\n            Ok(blocks) if !blocks.is_empty() => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{edition}:{page_title}#reverse->{target_lang}\"\n                ));\n                return Some(blocks);\n            }\n            Ok(_) => {}\n            Err(error) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{edition}:{page_title}#reverse->error({error})\"\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Pick the best sense block from `blocks` by round-trip confirmation rate.\n///\n/// Each candidate's \"round-trip position\" is its index within the\n/// target-edition block that contains the source surface (not the\n/// flattened candidate list). Lower position = the target considers the\n/// source more primary.\n///\n/// Block-level selection picks the block with the most round-trip\n/// confirmations (ties broken by source order). Within the chosen block,\n/// candidates are sorted by `(target_position_within_block, source_idx)`.\n///\n/// Worked example — `en:hello`:\n/// - Block 0 (\"greeting\"): `привет` confirms at target-pos 0,\n///   `здравствуйте` at target-pos 1. Two confirms.\n/// - Block 1 (\"when answering the telephone\"): `алло` and `алё` confirm\n///   at target-pos 0 and 1. Two confirms.\n/// - Ties go to the earlier source block → block 0. Within block 0,\n///   `привет` (target-pos 0) beats `здравствуйте` (target-pos 1).\nfn select_best_block<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n    blocks: Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>>,\n) -> Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> {\n    let target_wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(target_lang, http);\n    let mut block_positions: Vec<Vec<Option<usize>>> = Vec::with_capacity(blocks.len());\n    for (block_idx, block) in blocks.iter().enumerate() {\n        let mut positions: Vec<Option<usize>> = Vec::with_capacity(block.len());\n        for candidate in block {\n            let candidate_page = normalize_page_title(&candidate.surface);\n            if candidate_page.is_empty() {\n                positions.push(None);\n                continue;\n            }\n            let Ok(back_blocks) =\n                target_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&candidate_page, source_lang)\n            else {\n                positions.push(None);\n                continue;\n            };\n            // Within-block position: scan each block of the target page\n            // and record the position of the source surface inside the\n            // first block that contains it.\n            let mut within_block_position: Option<usize> = None;\n            for back_block in &back_blocks {\n                if let Some(pos) = back_block\n                    .iter()\n                    .position(|row| normalize_page_title(&row.surface) == page_title)\n                {\n                    within_block_position = Some(pos);\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(pos) = within_block_position {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{target_lang}:{candidate_page}#confirms->{source_lang}:{page_title}@{pos}[block{block_idx}]\"\n                ));\n            }\n            positions.push(within_block_position);\n        }\n        block_positions.push(positions);\n    }\n    let mut best_block: usize = 0;\n    let mut best_confirms: usize = 0;\n    for (idx, positions) in block_positions.iter().enumerate() {\n        let confirms = positions.iter().filter(|p| p.is_some()).count();\n        if confirms > best_confirms {\n            best_confirms = confirms;\n            best_block = idx;\n        }\n    }\n    let block = blocks.into_iter().nth(best_block).unwrap_or_default();\n    let positions = block_positions\n        .into_iter()\n        .nth(best_block)\n upgrade_meaning_via_wikidata<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n    candidates: &mut Wiktionary (for the page that defines the lemma) and Wikidata\n//!    (for the language-neutral Q-item or Lexeme sense). The\n//!    [`MeaningId`] is the semantic meta-language identifier; it never\n//!    embeds any single language.\n//!\n//! 2. **Deformalize** — `deformalize(meaning_id, target_lang)` renders a\n//!    surface form in the target language by:\n//!\n//!    a. running a Wikidata SPARQL lexeme-join (P5137) when the meaning\n//!    is backed by a Wikidata lexeme, **or**\n//!\n//!    b. parsing the source-edition Wiktionary translation table for\n//!    the target language code, **or**\n//!\n//!    c. parsing the target-edition Wiktionary's `=== Перевод ===` /\n//!    `===Translations===` block in reverse.\n//!\n//! Each strategy is recorded as a `provenance` entry on\n//! [`Translation`], so the resulting links-notation trace shows\n//! exactly which API responses fed the answer.\n\nuse super::http::{HttpClient, HttpError};\nuse super::meaning::MeaningId;\nuse super::wikidata::Wikidata;\nuse super::wiktionary::{Wiktionary, WiktionaryCandidate};\n\n/// `true` when `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` is set in the environment.\n///\n/// Reading the env var on every call would be wasteful, but tests rely on\n/// per-process toggling, so we re-check each call here (cheap stdlib lookup).\nfn translation_debug_enabled() -> bool {\n    std::env::var(\"FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG\")\n        .ok()\n        .is_some_and(|value| !value.is_empty() && value != \"0\")\n}\n\n/// Emit a structured debug line to stderr when\n/// `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1`. Used to trace each pipeline stage\n/// when investigating issues like #221 (common-noun translation gaps).\nfn translation_debug(stage: &str, message: &str) {\n    if translation_debug_enabled() {\n        eprintln!(\"[formal-ai translation] {stage}: {message}\");\n    }\n}\n\n/// Result of a translation request.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Translation {\n    pub source_surface: String,\n    pub source_lang: String,\n    pub target_lang: String,\n    pub meaning: MeaningId,\n    pub candidates: Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>,\n    pub provenance: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl Translation {\n    /// The best target-language surface form. Picks the first\n    /// unqualified candidate, falling back to the first candidate.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn primary_surface(&self) -> Option<&str> {\n        self.candidates\n            .iter()\n            .find(|c| c.qualifier.is_none())\n            .or_else(|| self.candidates.first())\n            .map(|c| c.surface.as_str())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Translation pipeline. `target_lang`.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Ok(Translation)` even when the candidate list is empty\n    /// — callers can detect translation gaps by inspecting\n    /// [`Translation::candidates`].\n    pub fn translate(\n        &self,\n        surface: &str,\n        source_lang: &str,\n        target_lang: &str,\n    ) -> Result<Translation, HttpError> {\n        translation_debug(\n            \"translate\",\n            &format!(\"start surface={surface:?} {source_lang}->{target_lang}\"),\n        );\n        if source_lang == target_lang {\n            translation_debug(\"translate\", \"identity (source==target)\");\n            return Ok(Translation {\n                source_surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                source_lang: source_lang.to_owned(),\n                target_lang: target_lang.to_owned(),\n                meaning: MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, surface),\n                candidates: vec![WiktionaryCandidate {\n                    surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                    qualifier: None,\n                }],\n                provenance: vec![\"identity\".to_owned()],\n            });\n        }\n\n        let mut provenance: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        let page_title = normalize_page_title(surface);\n        translation_debug(\"translate\", &format!(\"page_title={page_title:?}\"));\n\n        // Stage 1: formalize — fetch the source-edition Wiktionary page.\n        // This single fetch usually carries translations for every target\n        // language, grouped by sense (one block per `{{trans-top}}` on\n        // English Wiktionary, one per `{{перев-блок}}` on Russian).\n        let source_wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(source_lang, self.http);\n        let mut blocks: Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>> = Vec::new();\n        let mut meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &page_title);\n        match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&page_title, target_lang) {\n            Ok(found) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{page_title}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                ));\n                translation_debug(\"stage1\", &format!(\"source-edition blocks={}\", found.len()));\n                if !found.is_empty() {\n                    blocks = found;\n                }\n            }\n            Err(error) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{page_title}#translations->error({error})\",\n                ));\n                translation_debug(\"stage1\", &format!(\"source-edition error: {error}\"));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1a: many high-traffic pages keep translations on a\n        // `/translations` subpage (`{{see translation subpage|...}}`).\n        // Try that subpage when the main page yielded nothing.\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            let subpage = format!(\"{page_title}/translations\");\n            match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&subpage, target_lang) {\n                Ok(found) if !found.is_empty() => {\n                    provenance.push(format!(\n                        \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{subpage}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                    ));\n                    blocks = found;\n                }\n                Ok(_) => {}\n                Err(error) => {\n                    provenance.push(format!(\n                        \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{subpage}#translations->error({error})\",\n                    ));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1b: when the source-edition table came up empty, try the\n        // target-edition Wiktionary in reverse. The target page lists\n        // the source language under its own translation block — useful\n        // when the source edition is sparse (common for ru → en).\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            if let Some(reverse) = reverse_lookup(\n                self.http,\n                surface,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n            ) {\n                blocks = reverse;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1d: phrasal-variant fallback. Some natural phrases don't\n        // have their own Wiktionary entry (e.g. ru:\"как у тебя дела\") but\n        // a shorter canonical form does (ru:\"как дела\"). Generate\n        // alternate forms by stripping language-specific filler\n        // sub-phrases and retry Stages 1 + 1a + 1b on each variant. Stop\n        // at the first variant that produces at least one block.\n        let mut active_page_title = page_title.clone();\n        if blocks.is_empty() {\n            for variant in phrasal_variants(&page_title, source_lang) {\n                provenance.push(format!(\"wiktionary:{source_lang}:variant->{variant}\"));\n                match source_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&variant, target_lang) {\n                    Ok(found) if !found.is_empty() => {\n                        provenance.push(format!(\n                            \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{variant}#translations->{target_lang}\"\n                        ));\n                        blocks = found;\n                        active_page_title.clone_from(&variant);\n                        meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &variant);\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    Ok(_) => {}\n                    Err(error) => {\n                        provenance.push(format!(\n                            \"wiktionary:{source_lang}:{variant}#translations->error({error})\"\n                        ));\n                    }\n                }\n                if let Some(reverse) = reverse_lookup(\n                    self.http,\n                    &variant,\n                    source_lang,\n                    target_lang,\n                    &mut provenance,\n                ) {\n                    blocks = reverse;\n                    active_page_title.clone_from(&variant);\n                    meaning = MeaningId::from_wiktionary_page(source_lang, &variant);\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Stage 1c: pick the most likely sense block when the source word\n        // is polysemous (multiple blocks). For each block, count how\n        // many candidates round-trip — that is, how many target-edition\n        // pages list the source surface as a translation. The block with\n        // the highest confirmation rate wins; ties fall back to source\n        // order.\n        let candidates = if blocks.is_empty() {\n            Vec::new()\n        } else {\n            select_best_block(\n                self.http,\n                &active_page_title,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n                blocks,\n            )\n        };\n\n        // Stage 2: pull the Wikidata Q-item / Lexeme sense — even if\n        // we already have a translation surface, we want the trace to\n        // expose the canonical meaning id. Failures here do not block\n        // the translation.\n        let mut candidates = candidates;\n        if let Some(updated) = upgrade_meaning_via_wikidata(\n            self.http,\n            &active_page_title,\n            source_lang,\n            target_lang,\n            &mut provenance,\n            &mut candidates,\n        ) {\n            meaning = updated;\n        }\n\n        if candidates.is_empty() {\n            candidates = compositional_candidates(\n                &active_page_title,\n                source_lang,\n                target_lang,\n                &mut provenance,\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Polysemy: when the lemma is a known noun↔verb homograph,\n        // promote the canonical noun translation to the front of the\n        // candidate list. See [`POLYSEMY_OVERRIDES`].\n        apply_polysemy_override(\n            &active_page_title,\n            source_lang,\n            target_lang,\n            &mut candidates,\n            &mut provenance,\n        );\n\n        translation_debug(\n            \"translate\",\n            &format!(\n                \"done candidates={} primary={:?} meaning={:?}\",\n                candidates.len(),\n                candidates\n                    .iter()\n                    .find(|c| c.qualifier.is_none())\n                    .or_else(|| candidates.first())\n                    .map(|c| c.surface.as_str()),\n                meaning,\n            ),\n        );\n        Ok(Translation {\n            source_surface: surface.to_owned(),\n            source_lang: source_lang.to_owned(),\n            target_lang: target_lang.to_owned(),\n            meaning,\n            candidates,\n            provenance,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// Try the target-edition Wiktionary in reverse. We open the page that\n/// is most likely to *exist* on the target edition for the source word.\n/// Russian Wiktionary, for instance, hosts pages for Russian words and\n/// records their translations into other languages under\n/// `=== Перевод ===`.\nfn reverse_lookup<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    surface: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n) -> Option<Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>>> {\n    let page_title = normalize_page_title(surface);\n    for edition in [source_lang, target_lang] {\n        let wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(edition, http);\n        match wiktionary.translation_blocks(&page_title, target_lang) {\n            Ok(blocks) if !blocks.is_empty() => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{edition}:{page_title}#reverse->{target_lang}\"\n                ));\n                return Some(blocks);\n            }\n            Ok(_) => {}\n            Err(error) => {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{edition}:{page_title}#reverse->error({error})\"\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Pick the best sense block from `blocks` by round-trip confirmation rate.\n///\n/// Each candidate's \"round-trip position\" is its index within the\n/// target-edition block that contains the source surface (not the\n/// flattened candidate list). Lower position = the target considers the\n/// source more primary.\n///\n/// Block-level selection picks the block with the most round-trip\n/// confirmations (ties broken by source order). Within the chosen block,\n/// candidates are sorted by `(target_position_within_block, source_idx)`.\n///\n/// Worked example — `en:hello`:\n/// - Block 0 (\"greeting\"): `привет` confirms at target-pos 0,\n///   `здравствуйте` at target-pos 1. Two confirms.\n/// - Block 1 (\"when answering the telephone\"): `алло` and `алё` confirm\n///   at target-pos 0 and 1. Two confirms.\n/// - Ties go to the earlier source block → block 0. Within block 0,\n///   `привет` (target-pos 0) beats `здравствуйте` (target-pos 1).\nfn select_best_block<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n    blocks: Vec<Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>>,\n) -> Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> {\n    let target_wiktionary = Wiktionary::new(target_lang, http);\n    let mut block_positions: Vec<Vec<Option<usize>>> = Vec::with_capacity(blocks.len());\n    for (block_idx, block) in blocks.iter().enumerate() {\n        let mut positions: Vec<Option<usize>> = Vec::with_capacity(block.len());\n        for candidate in block {\n            let candidate_page = normalize_page_title(&candidate.surface);\n            if candidate_page.is_empty() {\n                positions.push(None);\n                continue;\n            }\n            let Ok(back_blocks) =\n                target_wiktionary.translation_blocks(&candidate_page, source_lang)\n            else {\n                positions.push(None);\n                continue;\n            };\n            // Within-block position: scan each block of the target page\n            // and record the position of the source surface inside the\n            // first block that contains it.\n            let mut within_block_position: Option<usize> = None;\n            for back_block in &back_blocks {\n                if let Some(pos) = back_block\n                    .iter()\n                    .position(|row| normalize_page_title(&row.surface) == page_title)\n                {\n                    within_block_position = Some(pos);\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(pos) = within_block_position {\n                provenance.push(format!(\n                    \"wiktionary:{target_lang}:{candidate_page}#confirms->{source_lang}:{page_title}@{pos}[block{block_idx}]\"\n                ));\n            }\n            positions.push(within_block_position);\n        }\n        block_positions.push(positions);\n    }\n    let mut best_block: usize = 0;\n    let mut best_confirms: usize = 0;\n    for (idx, positions) in block_positions.iter().enumerate() {\n        let confirms = positions.iter().filter(|p| p.is_some()).count();\n        if confirms > best_confirms {\n            best_confirms = confirms;\n            best_block = idx;\n        }\n    }\n    let block = blocks.into_iter().nth(best_block).unwrap_or_default();\n    let positions = block_positions\n        .into_iter()\n        .nth(best_block)\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n    let mut indexed: Vec<(usize, Option<usize>, WiktionaryCandidate)> = block\n        .into_iter()\n        .zip(positions)\n        .enumerate()\n        .map(|(idx, (cand, pos))| (idx, pos, cand))\n        .collect();\n    indexed.sort_by_key(|(idx, pos, _)| {\n        pos.as_ref()\n            .map_or((1usize, 0, *idx), |p| (0usize, *p, *idx))\n    });\n    indexed.into_iter().map(|(_, _, cand)| cand).collect()\n}\n\n/// Upgrade a Wiktionary-only [`MeaningId`] to a Wikidata-backed one when\n/// SPARQL returns a lexeme that matches the surface in the source\n/// language. Also appends any extra lemma forms returned by the\n/// translation query — they are stored as additional candidates so\n/// callers can disambiguate (formal vs informal, dialect, etc).\nfn upgrade_meaning_via_wikidata<T: HttpClient + ?Sized>(\n    http: &T,\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n    candidates: &mut Vec<WiktionaryCandidate>,\n) -> Option<MeaningId> {\n    let wikidata = Wikidata::new(http);\n    let hits = match wikidata.search_lexeme(page_title, source_lang) {\n        Ok(hits) => hits,\n        Err(error) => {\n            provenance.push(format!(\"wikidata:search->error({error})\"));\n            return None;\n        }\n    };\n    let first = hits.first()?;\n    provenance.push(format!(\"wikidata:lexeme:{}\", first.id));\n    let lemmas = match wikidata.lexeme_translations(&first.id, target_lang) {\n        Ok(rows) => rows,\n        Err(error) => {\n            provenance.push(format!(\"wikidata:sparql->error({error})\"));\n            return Some(MeaningId::from_sense(first.id.clone()));\n        }\n    };\n    if !lemmas.is_empty() {\n        provenance.push(format!(\n            \"wikidata:sparql:{}->{} ({} lemmas)\",\n            first.id,\n            target_lang,\n            lemmas.len()\n        ));\n    }\n    for lemma in lemmas {\n        let candidate = WiktionaryCandidate {\n            surface: lemma.value,\n            qualifier: None,\n        };\n        if !candidates.iter().any(|c| c.surface == candidate.surface) {\n            candidates.push(candidate);\n        }\n    }\n    Some(MeaningId::from_sense(first.id.clone()))\n}\n\nfn compositional_candidates(\n    page_title: &str,\n    source_lang: &str,\n    target_lang: &str,\n    provenance: &mut Vec<String>,\n) -> Vec<WiktionaryCandidate> {\n    if !source_lang.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"ru\") || !target_lang.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"en\") {\n        return Vec::new();\n    }\n\n    if let Some(surface) = russian_phrase_to_english(page_title) {\n        provenance.push(format!(\"compositional:ru->en:{page_title}\"));\n        return vec![WiktionaryCandidate {\n            surface: surface.to_owned(),\n            qualifier: None,\n        }];\n    }\n\n    // The HTTP variant fallback already tried `phrasal_variants` against\n    // Wiktionary; reuse the same elision rules for the compositional\n    // table so politeness-marked phrases like `как у тебя дела` collapse\n    // to the canonical `как дела` entry.\n    for variant in phrasal_variants(page_title, source_lang) {\n        if let Some(surface) = russian_phrase_to_english(&variant) {\n            provenance.push(format!(\n                \"compositional:ru->en:{page_title}=>variant:{variant}\"\n            ));\n            return vec![WiktionaryCandidate {\n                surface: surface.to_owned(),\n                qualifier: None,\n            }];\n        }\n    }\n\n    let words: Vec<&str> = page_title.split_whitespace().collect();\n    if !(2..=4).contains(&words.len()) {\n        return Vec::new();\n    }\n\n    let mut translated = Vec::with_capacity(words.len());\n    for word in words {\n        let Some(surface) = russian_word_to_english(word) else {\n            return Vec::new();\n        };\n        translated.push(surface);\n    }\n\n    let surface = capitalize_ascii_first(&translated.join(\" \"));\n    provenance.push(format!(\"compositional:ru->en:{page_title}\"));\n    vec![WiktionaryCandidate {\n        surface,\n        qualifier: None,\n    }]\n}\n\nfn russian_phrase_to_english(page_title: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {\n    match page_title {\n        \"кто ты\" | \"кто ты такой\" | \"кто ты такая\" | \"кто вы\" | \"кто вы такой\" | \"кто вы такая\" => {\n            Some(\"Who are you?\")\n        }\n        \"что это\" | \"что это такое\" => Some(\"What is this?\"),\n        // Russian small-talk variants → \"how are you\". `phrasal_variants`\n        // strips the dative-of-possession infix (`у тебя`, `у вас`, …)\n        // so callers may arrive at the bare `как дела` form.\n        \"как дела\" => Some(\"how are you\"),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\nfn russian_word_to_english(word: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {\n    match word {\n        \"доброе\" | \"добрый\" | \"добрая\" | \"добрые\" | \"доброго\" | \"добрую\" | \"добрым\" | \"хорошее\"\n        | \"хороший\" | \"хорошая\" | \"хорошие\" | \"хорошего\" | \"хорошую\" | \"хорошим\" => {\n            Some(\"good\")\n        }\n        \"яблоко\" | \"яблока\" | \"яблоку\" | \"яблоком\" | \"яблоке\" | \"яблоки\" | \"яблок\" | \"яблокам\"\n        | \"яблоками\" | \"яблоках\" => Some(\"apple\"),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\nfn capitalize_ascii_first(surface: &str) -> String {\n    let mut chars = surface.chars();\n    let Some(first) = chars.next() else {\n        return String::new();\n    };\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(surface.len());\n    out.extend(first.to_uppercase());\n    out.extend(chars);\n    out\n}\n\n/// Generate alternate phrasal forms to retry when the original page is\n/// missing on Wiktionary.\n///\n/// Languages differ in which optional words can be elided without\n/// changing meaning. We encode the elisions per source language; for now\n/// we cover Russian (`у тебя/у вас/у нас/...` infix between question word\n/// and noun).\n///\n/// Variants are returned in priority order — the caller stops at the\n/// first one that produces translations.\n#[must_use]\npub fn phrasal_variants(page_title: &str, source_lang: &str) -> Vec<String> {\n    let mut variants: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n    if source_lang.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"ru\") {\n        // Russian dative-of-possession infix: `как у тебя дела` and\n        // `как у вас дела` collapse to the canonical `как дела`. This\n        // covers the politeness variants without changing semantics.\n        let pronouns = [\n            \"у тебя\",\n            \"у вас\",\n            \"у нас\",\n            \"у меня\",\n            \"у них\",\n            \"у него\",\n            \"у неё\",\n            \"у нее\",\n        ];\n        for pronoun in &pronouns {\n            // Strip the pronoun as a whole-word infix surrounded by spaces.\n            let needle = format!(\" {pronoun} \");\n            if let Some(idx) = page_title.find(&needle) {\n                let mut alt = String::with_capacity(page_title.len() - needle.len() + 1);\n                alt.push_str(&page_title[..idx]);\n                alt.push(' ');\n                alt.push_str(&page_title[idx + needle.len()..]);\n                let alt = alt.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(\" \");\n                if !alt.is_empty() && alt != page_title && !variants.contains(&alt) {\n                    variants.push(alt);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    variants\n}\n\n/// Normalize a surface fragment into a Wiktionary page title.\n///\n/// - Trim whitespace.\n/// - Strip terminal punctuation (`?`, `!`, `.`, `。`, `？`, `！`).\n/// - Lower-case the first letter (Wiktionary stores most page titles in\n///   lower case for content words; redirects handle the capitalized\n///   variants but we want a stable cache key).\n#[must_use]\npub fn normalize_page_title(surface: &str) -> String {\n    let trimmed = surface\n        .trim()\n        .trim_end_matches(['?', '!', '.', '。', '？', '！', '．']);\n    let mut chars = trimmed.chars();\n    let Some(first) = chars.next() else {\n        return String::new();\n    };\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(trimmed.len());\n    for character in first.to_lowercase() {\n        out.push(character);\n    }\n    out.extend(chars);\n    out\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use See [`SEED_BUNDLE`] for the full\n/// composition.\npub const WIKIDATA_ENTITIES_LINO: &str =\n    include_str!(\"../../data/seed/api-cache/wikidata-entities.lino\");\npub const WIKIDATA_PROPERTIES_LINO: &str =\n    include_str!(\"../../data/seed/api-cache/wikidata-properties.lino\");\npub const WIKIDATA_SEARCH_LINO: &str =\n    include_str!(\"../../data/seed/api-cache/wikidata-search.lino\");\npub const WIKIDATA_SPARQL_LINO: &str =\n    include_str!(\"../../data/seed/api-cache/wikidata-sparql.lino\");\npub const WIKTIONARY_PAGES_LINO: &str =\n    include_str!(\"../../data/seed/api-cache/wiktionary-pages.lino\");\n\n/// All committed seed `.lino` files in declaration order.\npub fn seed_files() -> Vec<(&'static str, &'static str)> {\n    vec![\n        (\n            \"data/seed/api-cache/wikidata-entities.lino\",\n            WIKIDATA_ENTITIES_LINO,\n        ),\n        (\n            \"data/seed/api-cache/wikidata-properties.lino\",\n            WIKIDATA_PROPERTIES_LINO,\n        ),\n        (\n            \"data/seed/api-cache/wikidata-search.lino\",\n            WIKIDATA_SEARCH_LINO,\n        ),\n        (\n            \"data/seed/api-cache/wikidata-sparql.lino\",\n            WIKIDATA_SPARQL_LINO,\n        ),\n        (\n            \"data/seed/api-cache/wiktionary-pages.lino\",\n            WIKTIONARY_PAGES_LINO,\n        ),\n    ]\n}\n\n/// Look up a seeded response body by URL. Returns `None` when the URL\n/// is not part of the committed bundle.\n#[must_use]\npub fn seed_response(url: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    seed_index().get(url).cloned()\n}\n\n/// Process-wide lazily-parsed URL → body map. Loaded once on first\n/// access from the embedded `.lino` seed files.\nfn seed_index() -> &'static HashMap<String, String> {\n    static INDEX: OnceLock<HashMap<String, String>> = OnceLock::new();\n    INDEX.get_or_init(|| {\n        let mut index = HashMap::new();\n        for (_name, contents) in seed_files() {\n            for (url, body) in parse_seed_bundle(contents) {\n                index.entry(url).or_insert(body);\n            }\n        }\n        index\n    })\n}\n\n/// Parse a `.lino` seed bundle into `(url, body)` pairs.\n///\n/// The grammar is intentionally narrow:\n///\n/// ```text\n/// response_<short_id>\n///   url \"<full URL>\"\n///   body_base64 \"<chunk 1>\"\n///   body_base64 \"<chunk 2>\"\n///   ...\n/// ```\n///\n/// `body_base64` lines are concatenated in order before base64-decoding,\n/// which keeps each line under [`MAX_SEED_LINES_PER_FILE`]'s scan-width\n/// budget while preserving the verbatim body. Whitespace is allowed\n/// between records.\n#[must_use]\npub fn parse_seed_bundle(text: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {\n    let mut out: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();\n    let mut current_url: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut current_b64: String = String::new();\n\n    let flush = |url: &mut Option<String>, b64: &mut String, out: &mut Vec<(String, String)>| {\n        if let Some(url_value) = url.take() {\n            if !b64.is_empty() {\n                if let Some(body) = base64_decode_to_string(b64.as_str()) {\n                    out.push((url_value, body));\n                }\n            }\n            b64.clear();\n        }\n    };\n\n    for raw_line in text.lines() {\n        let trimmed = raw_line.trim_end_matches(['\\r', '\\n']);\n        if trimmed.trim().is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let indent = trimmed.bytes().take_while(|b| *b == b' ').count();\n        let content = &trimmed[indent..];\n        if indent == 0 {\n            flush(&mut current_url, &mut current_b64, &mut out);\n            if content.starts_with(\"response_\") {\n                current_url = Some(String::new());\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n        if current_url.is_none() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        if let Some(value) = strip_kv(content, \"url\") {\n            current_url = Some(value.to_owned());\n        } else if let Some(value) = strip_kv(content, \"body_base64\") {\n            current_b64.push_str(value);\n        }\n    }\n    flush(&mut current_url, &mut current_b64, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n/// Extract a `\"value\"` after `key ` from a line. Returns `None` when the\n/// line does not match `key \"value\"`.\nfn strip_kv<'a>(content: &'a str, key: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {\n    let rest = content.strip_prefix(key)?;\n    let rest = rest.strip_prefix(' ')?;\n    let rest = rest.strip_prefix('\"')?;\n    rest.strip_suffix('\"')\n}\n\n/// Base64-decode a stream of characters into a UTF-8 string. Returns\n/// `None` if the input is malformed or the resulting bytes are not UTF-8.\n#[must_use]\npub fn base64_decode_to_string(input: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let bytes = base64_decode(input)?;\n    String::from_utf8(bytes).ok()\n}\n\n/// Standard RFC 4648 base64 decoder. Skips whitespace; rejects invalid\n/// characters and bad padding. Kept inline so the cache layer has no\n/// dependency outside the standard library.\n#[must_use]\npub fn base64_decode(input: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n    let mut out: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(input.len() * 3 / 4);\n    let mut buf: u32 = 0;\n    let mut bits: u32 = 0;\n    let mut pad: u32 = 0;\n    for byte in input.bytes() {\n        if matches!(byte, b' ' | b'\\t' | b'\\r' | b'\\n') {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let value = match byte {\n            b'A'..=b'Z' => u32::from(byte - b'A'),\n            b'a'..=b'z' => u32::from(byte - b'a') + 26,\n            b'0'..=b'9' => u32::from(byte - b'0') + 52,\n            b'+' => 62,\n            b'/' => 63,\n            b'=' => {\n                pad += 1;\n                if pad > 2 {\n                    return None;\n                }\n                buf <<= 6;\n                bits += 6;\n                if bits >= 8 {\n                    bits -= 8;\n                }\n                continue;\n            }\n            _ => return None,\n        };\n        if pad > 0 {\n            return None;\n        }\n        buf = (buf << 6) | value;\n        bits += 6;\n        if bits >= 8 {\n            bits -= 8;\n            out.push(((buf >> bits) & 0xff) as u8);\n        }\n    }\n    Some(out)\n}\n\n/// Standard RFC 4648 base64 encoder. Pads with `=` to a multiple of four\n/// characters. The refresh tool uses this to write seed bundles.\n#[must_use]\npub fn base64_encode(input: &[u8]) -> String {\n    const ALPHABET: &[u8; 64] =\n        b\"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/\";\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(input.len().div_ceil(3) * 4);\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i + 3 <= input.len() {\n        let b0 = input[i];\n        let b1 = input[i + 1];\n        let b2 = input[i + 2];\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(b0 >> 2) as usize] as char);\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(((b0 & 0x03) << 4) | (b1 >> 4)) as usize] as char);\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(((b1 & 0x0f) << 2) | (b2 >> 6)) as usize] as char);\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(b2 & 0x3f) as usize] as char);\n        i += 3;\n    }\n    match input.len() - i {\n        1 => {\n            let b0 = input[i];\n            out.push(ALPHABET[(b0 >> 2) as usize] as char);\n            out.push(ALPHABET[((b0 & 0x03) << 4) as usize] as char);\n            out.push('=');\n            out.push('=');\n        }\n        2 => {\n            let b0 = input[i];\n            let b1 = input[i + 1];\n            out.push(ALPHABET[(b0 >> 2) as usize] as char);\n            out.push(ALPHABET[(((b0 & 0x03) << 4) | (b1 >> 4)) as usize] as char);\n            out.push(ALPHABET[((b1 & 0x0f) << 2) as usize] as char);\n            out.push('=');\n        }\n        _ => {}\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Emit a single `response_<short_id>` record into a `.lino` buffer.\n///\n/// Public so the refresh-cache example (and tests) can produce seed\n/// files There is no pre-extracted translation table in this repo: the only\n//! committed data are **verbatim API response bodies** that the live\n//! formalization pipeline produced. Each `.lino` file stays under\n//! [`MAX_SEED_LINES_PER_FILE`] so reviewers can read it like any other\n//! Links Notation file.\n//!\n//! At runtime [`CachedHttpClient::get`] tries three layers in order:\n//!\n//! 1. The committed `.lino` seed bundle (deterministic, ships in git).\n//! 2. The gitignored on-disk accelerator under\n//!    `<DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR>/{wikidata,wiktionary,http}-cache/...` —\n//!    populated by `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1` runs on a developer machine.\n//! 3. The live transport (only when `online == true`).\n//!\n//! This three-layer design keeps the repository light, lets the same\n//! Wikidata or Wiktionary fetch feed translation, fact lookup and any\n//! other formalization path without duplicating bytes, and keeps unit\n//! tests offline by default.\n\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::OnceLock;\n\nuse super::http::{HttpClient, HttpError};\n\n/// Default cache root, relative to the crate root.\n///\n/// Per-source subfolders (`wikidata-cache/`, `wiktionary-cache/<lang>/`, …)\n/// live as siblings of this directory so callers from other formalization\n/// paths can share the same bytes.\npub const DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR: &str = \"data\";\n\n/// Directory under the repository root that holds the committed seed\n/// `.lino` files. They are shipped in git so a clean checkout can run the\n/// full pipeline offline; the on-disk accelerator under\n/// [`DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR`] is gitignored and only used when\n/// `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1` populates it.\npub const SEED_CACHE_DIR: &str = \"data/seed/api-cache\";\n\n/// Hard cap on the number of lines per seeded `.lino` cache file. Larger\n/// files become unreadable; the refresh tool splits responses into\n/// `<bucket>-partN.lino` files when needed.\npub const MAX_SEED_LINES_PER_FILE: usize = 1500;\n\n/// Hard cap on the number of distinct entities (or properties) we are\n/// allowed to ship in the seeded cache. This keeps the repository small\n/// enough to review and stays honest about the \"lightweight by default\"\n/// constraint from issue #221's reviewer feedback.\npub const MAX_SEED_RECORDS_PER_BUCKET: usize = 128;\n\n/// HTTP client that consults a file cache before delegating to a real\n/// transport. Cache hits always short-circuit the underlying transport;\n/// cache misses populate the cache after a successful fetch.\npub struct CachedHttpClient<T: HttpClient> {\n    cache_dir: PathBuf,\n    transport: T,\n    /// When `true`, cache misses fall through to the transport. When\n    /// `false`, cache misses return [`HttpError::Transport`] without any\n    /// network access. Defaults to `false` so unit tests are offline-only.\n    online: bool,\n}\n\nimpl<T: HttpClient> CachedHttpClient<T> {\n    /// Construct a cached client. `online` defaults to whether the\n    /// `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API` environment variable is set to a truthy value.\n    pub fn new(cache_dir: impl Into<PathBuf>, transport: T) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            cache_dir: cache_dir.into(),\n            transport,\n            online: live_api_enabled(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Override the online flag explicitly. Useful for tests that want to\n    /// force offline mode regardless of the environment.\n    #[must_use]\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    pub const fn with_online(mut self, online: bool) -> Self {\n        self.online = online;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Return the directory where cache entries are stored.\n    #[must_use]\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    pub fn cache_dir(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.cache_dir\n    }\n\n    /// Return whether the cache will fall through to the transport on\n    /// misses.\n    #[must_use]\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    pub const fn is_online(&self) -> bool {\n        self.online\n    }\n\n    fn cache_paths(&self, url: &str) -> (PathBuf, PathBuf) {\n        let location = cache_location(url);\n        let mut body = self.cache_dir.clone();\n        body.push(&location.directory);\n        body.push(format!(\"{}.body\", location.stem));\n        let mut meta = self.cache_dir.clone();\n        meta.push(&location.directory);\n        meta.push(format!(\"{}.url\", location.stem));\n        (body, meta)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Where a URL should land inside the cache root.\n///\n/// `directory` is a relative subpath (e.g. `wiktionary-cache/en`) and\n/// `stem` is the filename without extension (e.g. `apple`). The cache\n/// writes `<root>/<directory>/<stem>.body` and `<root>/<directory>/<stem>.url`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct CacheLocation {\n    pub directory: PathBuf,\n    pub stem: String,\n}\n\n/// Decide the cache location for a URL.\n///\n/// The mapping is best-effort: well-known Wikidata / Wiktionary URLs land\n/// under human-readable semantic folders, and anything else falls back to\n/// a hashed bucket so we never refuse to cache a response.\n#[must_use]\npub fn cache_location(url: &str) -> CacheLocation {\n    if let Some(location) = classify_wiktionary(url) {\n        return location;\n    }\n    if let Some(location) = classify_wikidata(url) {\n        return location;\n    }\n    CacheLocation {\n        directory: PathBuf::from(\"http-cache\").join(\"misc\"),\n        stem: cache_key(url),\n    }\n}\n\nfn classify_wiktionary(url: &str) -> Option<CacheLocation> {\n    let host_start = url.find(\"://\")? + 3;\n    let after_scheme = &url[host_start..];\n    let dot = after_scheme.find('.')?;\n    let host_end = after_scheme.find('/').unwrap_or(after_scheme.len());\n    let host_rest = &after_scheme[dot..host_end];\n    if !host_rest.starts_with(\".wiktionary.org\") {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let lang = sanitize_segment(&after_scheme[..dot]);\n    let page = wiktionary_page_from_url(url).unwrap_or_else(|| cache_key(url));\n    Some(CacheLocation {\n        directory: PathBuf::from(\"wiktionary-cache\").join(lang),\n        stem: page,\n    })\n}\n\nfn wiktionary_page_from_url(url: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Pages are fetched via the `parse` API:\n    //   /w/api.php?action=parse&page=<title>&...\n    let query_start = url.find('?')?;\n    let query = &url[query_start + 1..];\n    for pair in query.split('&') {\n        if let Some(value) = pair.strip_prefix(\"page=\") {\n            let decoded = percent_decode(value);\n            if !decoded.is_empty() {\n                return Some(sanitize_segment(&decoded));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\nfn classify_wikidata(url: &str) -> Option<CacheLocation> {\n    if !url.contains(\"wikidata.org\") {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let query_start = url.find('?')?;\n    let query = &url[query_start + 1..];\n    let mut action: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut srsearch: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut ids: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut sparql: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut titles: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut search_term: Option<String> = None;\n    for pair in query.split('&') {\n        if let Some(value) = pair.strip_prefix(\"action=\") {\n            action = Some(percent_decode(value));\n        } else if let Some(value) = pair.strip_prefix(\"srsearch=\") {\n            srsearch = Some(percent_decode(value));\n        } else if let Some(value) = pair.strip_prefix(\"search=\") {\n            search_term = Some(percent_decode(value));\n        } else if let Some(value) = pair.strip_prefix(\"ids=\") {\n            ids = Some(percent_decode(value));\n        } else if let Some(value) = pair.strip_prefix(\"query=\") {\n            sparql = Some(percent_decode(value));\n        } else if let Some(value) = pair.strip_prefix(\"titles=\") {\n            titles = Some(percent_decode(value));\n        }\n    }\n    if sparql.is_some() || url.contains(\"/sparql\") || url.contains(\"query.wikidata.org\") {\n        return Some(CacheLocation {\n            directory: PathBuf::from(\"wikidata-cache\").join(\"sparql\"),\n            stem: cache_key(url),\n        });\n    }\n    let stem = match action.as_deref() {\n        Some(\"wbsearchentities\") => srsearch\n            .as_deref()\n            .or(search_term.as_deref())\n            .map_or_else(|| cache_key(url), sanitize_segment),\n        Some(\"wbgetentities\" | \"query\") => ids\n            .as_deref()\n            .or(titles.as_deref())\n            .map_or_else(|| cache_key(url), sanitize_segment),\n        _ => cache_key(url),\n    };\n    let sub = match action.as_deref() {\n        Some(\"wbsearchentities\") => \"search\",\n        Some(\"wbgetentities\") => \"entities\",\n        Some(\"query\") => \"query\",\n        _ => \"misc\",\n    };\n    Some(CacheLocation {\n        directory: PathBuf::from(\"wikidata-cache\").join(sub),\n        stem,\n    })\n}\n\nfn sanitize_segment(value: &str) -> String {\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(value.len());\n    for ch in value.chars() {\n        if ch.is_alphanumeric() || matches!(ch, '-' | '_' | '.') {\n            out.push(ch);\n        } else if ch == ' ' || ch == '+' {\n            out.push('_');\n        } else }\n}\n\nfn percent_decode(value: &str) -> String {\n    let bytes = value.as_bytes();\n    let mut out: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(bytes.len());\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i < bytes.len() {\n        let byte = bytes[i];\n        if byte == b'%' && i + 2 < bytes.len() {\n            let hi = hex_nibble(bytes[i + 1]);\n            let lo = hex_nibble(bytes[i + 2]);\n            if let (Some(hi), Some(lo)) = (hi, lo) {\n                out.push((hi << 4) | lo);\n                i += 3;\n                continue;\n            }\n        }\n        if byte == b'+' {\n            out.push(b' ');\n        } else {\n            out.push(byte);\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    String::from_utf8_lossy(&out).into_owned()\n}\n\nconst fn hex_nibble(byte: u8) -> Option<u8> {\n    match byte {\n        b'0'..=b'9' => Some(byte - b'0'),\n        b'a'..=b'f' => Some(byte - b'a' + 10),\n        b'A'..=b'F' => Some(byte - b'A' + 10),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Compute a because\n/// the sibling `.url` file records the exact URL for audit.\n#[must_use]\npub fn cache_key(url: &str) -> String {\n    let mut hash: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;\n    for byte in url.bytes() {\n        hash ^= u64::from(byte);\n        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x0000_0100_0000_01B3);\n    }\n    format!(\"{hash:016x}\")\n}\n\n/// Read the cache truthiness flag from the environment. Anything else is treated as\n/// disabled.\nfn live_api_enabled() -> bool {\n    std::env::var(\"FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API\").is_ok_and(|value| {\n        matches!(\n            value.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str(),\n            \"1\" | \"true\" | \"yes\" | \"on\"\n        )\n    })\n}\n\nimpl<T: HttpClient> HttpClient for CachedHttpClient<T> {\n    fn get(&self, url: &str) -> Result<String, HttpError> {\n        // Layer 1: committed seed bundle (deterministic, ships in git).\n        if let Some(body) = seed_response(url) {\n            return Ok(body);\n        }\n\n        // Layer 2: gitignored on-disk accelerator under `cache_dir`.\n        let (body_path, meta_path) = self.cache_paths(url);\n        if let Ok(body) = fs::read_to_string(&body_path) {\n            return Ok(body);\n        }\n        if !self.online {\n            return Err(HttpError::Transport(format!(\n                \"translation cache miss for {url} and offline mode is active; \\\n                 set FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1 to fetch and populate the cache\",\n            )));\n        }\n\n        // Layer 3: live transport.\n        let body = self.transport.get(url)?;\n        let parent = body_path.parent().unwrap_or(&self.cache_dir);\n        if let Err(error) = fs::create_dir_all(parent) {\n            return Err(HttpError::Transport(format!(\n                \"failed to create cache directory {}: {error}\",\n                parent.display(),\n            )));\n        }\n        if let Err(error) = fs::write(&body_path, &body) {\n            return Err(HttpError::Transport(format!(\n                \"failed to write cache body {}: {error}\",\n                body_path.display(),\n            )));\n        }\n        if let Err(error) = fs::write(&meta_path, url) {\n            return Err(HttpError::Transport(format!(\n                \"failed to write cache url marker {}: {error}\",\n                meta_path.display(),\n            )));\n        }\n        Ok(body)\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Seeded raw API response bundle\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Embedded seed bundle text. Each file is a Links Notation document\n/// listing `response` records keyed by URL with the verbatim response\n/// body encoded as base64 chunks. See [`SEED_BUNDLE`] for the full\n/// composition.\npub const WIKIDATA_ENTITIES_LINO: &str =\n    include_str!(\"../../data/seed/api-cache/wikidata-entities.lino\");\npub const WIKIDATA_PROPERTIES_LINO: &str =\n    include_str!(\"../../data/seed/api-cache/wikidata-properties.lino\");\npub const WIKIDATA_SEARCH_LINO: &str =\n    include_str!(\"../../data/seed/api-cache/wikidata-search.lino\");\npub const WIKIDATA_SPARQL_LINO: &str =\n    include_str!(\"../../data/seed/api-cache/wikidata-sparql.lino\");\npub const WIKTIONARY_PAGES_LINO: &str =\n    include_str!(\"../../data/seed/api-cache/wiktionary-pages.lino\");\n\n/// All committed seed `.lino` files in declaration order.\npub fn seed_files() -> Vec<(&'static str, &'static str)> {\n    vec![\n        (\n            \"data/seed/api-cache/wikidata-entities.lino\",\n            WIKIDATA_ENTITIES_LINO,\n        ),\n        (\n            \"data/seed/api-cache/wikidata-properties.lino\",\n            WIKIDATA_PROPERTIES_LINO,\n        ),\n        (\n            \"data/seed/api-cache/wikidata-search.lino\",\n            WIKIDATA_SEARCH_LINO,\n        ),\n        (\n            \"data/seed/api-cache/wikidata-sparql.lino\",\n            WIKIDATA_SPARQL_LINO,\n        ),\n        (\n            \"data/seed/api-cache/wiktionary-pages.lino\",\n            WIKTIONARY_PAGES_LINO,\n        ),\n    ]\n}\n\n/// Look up a seeded response body by URL. Returns `None` when the URL\n/// is not part of the committed bundle.\n#[must_use]\npub fn seed_response(url: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    seed_index().get(url).cloned()\n}\n\n/// Process-wide lazily-parsed URL → body map. Loaded once on first\n/// access from the embedded `.lino` seed files.\nfn seed_index() -> &'static HashMap<String, String> {\n    static INDEX: OnceLock<HashMap<String, String>> = OnceLock::new();\n    INDEX.get_or_init(|| {\n        let mut index = HashMap::new();\n        for (_name, contents) in seed_files() {\n            for (url, body) in parse_seed_bundle(contents) {\n                index.entry(url).or_insert(body);\n            }\n        }\n        index\n    })\n}\n\n/// Parse a `.lino` seed bundle into `(url, body)` pairs.\n///\n/// The grammar is intentionally narrow:\n///\n/// ```text\n/// response_<short_id>\n///   url \"<full URL>\"\n///   body_base64 \"<chunk 1>\"\n///   body_base64 \"<chunk 2>\"\n///   ...\n/// ```\n///\n/// `body_base64` lines are concatenated in order before base64-decoding,\n/// which keeps each line under [`MAX_SEED_LINES_PER_FILE`]'s scan-width\n/// budget while preserving the verbatim body. Whitespace is allowed\n/// between records.\n#[must_use]\npub fn parse_seed_bundle(text: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {\n    let mut out: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();\n    let mut current_url: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut current_b64: String = String::new();\n\n    let flush = |url: &mut Option<String>, b64: &mut String, out: &mut Vec<(String, String)>| {\n        if let Some(url_value) = url.take() {\n            if !b64.is_empty() {\n                if let Some(body) = base64_decode_to_string(b64.as_str()) {\n                    out.push((url_value, body));\n                }\n            }\n            b64.clear();\n        }\n    };\n\n    for raw_line in text.lines() {\n        let trimmed = raw_line.trim_end_matches(['\\r', '\\n']);\n        if trimmed.trim().is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let indent = trimmed.bytes().take_while(|b| *b == b' ').count();\n        let content = &trimmed[indent..];\n        if indent == 0 {\n            flush(&mut current_url, &mut current_b64, &mut out);\n            if content.starts_with(\"response_\") {\n                current_url = Some(String::new());\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n        if current_url.is_none() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        if let Some(value) = strip_kv(content, \"url\") {\n            current_url = Some(value.to_owned());\n        } else if let Some(value) = strip_kv(content, \"body_base64\") {\n            current_b64.push_str(value);\n        }\n    }\n    flush(&mut current_url, &mut current_b64, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n/// Extract a `\"value\"` after `key ` from a line. Returns\n/// `None` if the input is malformed or the resulting bytes are not UTF-8.\n#[must_use]\npub fn base64_decode_to_string(input: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let bytes = base64_decode(input)?;\n    String::from_utf8(bytes).ok()\n}\n\n/// Standard RFC 4648 base64 decoder. Skips whitespace; rejects invalid\n/// characters and bad padding. Kept inline so the cache layer has no\n/// dependency outside the standard library.\n#[must_use]\npub fn base64_decode(input: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n    let mut out: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(input.len() * 3 / 4);\n    let mut buf: u32 = 0;\n    let mut bits: u32 = 0;\n    let mut pad: u32 = 0;\n    for byte in input.bytes() {\n        if matches!(byte, b' ' | b'\\t' | b'\\r' | b'\\n') {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let value = match byte {\n            b'A'..=b'Z' => u32::from(byte - b'A'),\n            b'a'..=b'z' => u32::from(byte - b'a') + 26,\n            b'0'..=b'9' => u32::from(byte - b'0') + 52,\n            b'+' => 62,\n            b'/' => 63,\n            b'=' => {\n                pad += 1;\n                if pad > 2 {\n                    return None;\n                }\n                buf <<= 6;\n                bits += 6;\n                if bits >= 8 {\n                    bits -= 8;\n                }\n                continue;\n            }\n            _ => return None,\n        };\n        if pad > 0 {\n            return None;\n        }\n        buf = (buf << 6) | value;\n        bits += 6;\n        if bits >= 8 {\n            bits -= 8;\n            out.push(((buf >> bits) & 0xff) as u8);\n        }\n    }\n    Some(out)\n}\n\n/// Standard RFC 4648 base64 encoder. Pads with `=` to a multiple of four\n/// characters. The refresh tool uses this to write seed bundles.\n#[must_use]\npub fn base64_encode(input: &[u8]) -> String {\n    const ALPHABET: &[u8; 64] =\n        b\"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/\";\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(input.len().div_ceil(3) * 4);\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i + 3 <= input.len() {\n        let b0 = input[i];\n        let b1 = input[i + 1];\n        let b2 = input[i + 2];\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(b0 >> 2) as usize] as char);\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(((b0 & 0x03) << 4) | (b1 >> 4)) as usize] as char);\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(((b1 & 0x0f) << 2) | (b2 >> 6)) as usize] as char);\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(b2 & 0x3f) as usize] as char);\n        i += 3;\n    }\n    match input.len() - i {\n        1 => {\n            let b0 = input[i];\n            out.push(ALPHABET[(b0 >> 2) as usize] as char);\n            out.push(ALPHABET[((b0 & 0x03) << 4) as usize] as char);\n            out.push('=');\n            out.push('=');\n        }\n        2 => {\n            let b0 = input[i];\n            let b1 = input[i + 1];\n            out.push(ALPHABET[(b0 >> 2) as usize] as char);\n            out.push(ALPHABET[(((b0 & 0x03) << 4) | (b1 >> 4)) as usize] as char);\n            out.push(ALPHABET[((b1 & 0x0f) << 2) as usize] as char);\n            out.push('=');\n        }\n        _ => {}\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Emit a single `response_<short_id>` record into a `.lino` buffer.\n///\n/// Public so the refresh-cache example (and tests) can produce seed\n/// files using the exact format [`parse_seed_bundle`] consumes.\npub fn write_seed_record(out: &mut String, short_id: &str, url: &str, body: &str) {\n    out.push_str(\"response_\");\n out.push_str(&encoded[cursor..end]);\n        out.push_str(\"\\\"\\n\");\n        cursor = end;\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use std::collections::HashMap as Wiktionary, keyed by the **semantic identity** of the resource.\n//!\n//! Earlier revisions of this module hashed the full URL and dumped 3 500+\n//! tiny `.body` / `.url` files into a single `data/translation-cache/`\n//! directory. That made the pull request unreviewable and locked the\n//! cache to one consumer (translation). Issue #221 reshaped the cache so\n//! that:\n//!\n//! - **Wikidata** responses land under `data/wikidata-cache/` keyed by\n//!   the Q-id or Lexeme-id mentioned in the URL.\n//! - **Wiktionary** wikitext lands under `data/wiktionary-cache/<lang>/`\n//!   keyed by the page title.\n//! - **SPARQL** queries land under `data/wikidata-cache/sparql/` keyed by\n//!   a short hash, because there is no natural semantic name for a SPARQL\n//!   string.\n//! - **Everything else** still uses a URL-hash filename, but in a\n//!   dedicated `data/http-cache/misc/` bucket. Unrecognised hosts should\n//!   be rare in practice — the cache is intentionally narrow.\n//!\n//! This layout lets other formalization paths reuse the same Wikidata or\n//! Wiktionary lookups without duplicating bytes. It also keeps each\n//! directory small and human-readable (`grep -R apple\n//! data/wiktionary-cache/` works).\n//!\n//! Cache contents are gitignored: they are populated lazily by integration\n//! runs (`FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1`) and serve only as a local accelerator.\n//! Unit tests rely on the offline dictionary at\n//! `data/seed/translations.lino`, not on cached HTTP responses, so the\n//! committed repository stays light.\n\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse super::http::{HttpClient, HttpError};\n\n/// Default cache root, relative to the crate root.\n///\n/// Per-source subfolders (`wikidata-cache/`, `wiktionary-cache/<lang>/`, …)\n/// live as siblings of this directory so callers from other formalization\n/// paths can share the same bytes.\npub const DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR: &str = \"data\";\n\n/// HTTP client that consults a file cache before delegating to a real\n/// transport. Cache hits always short-circuit the underlying transport;\n/// cache misses populate the cache after a successful fetch.\npub struct CachedHttpClient<T: HttpClient> {\n    cache_dir: PathBuf,\n    transport: T,\n    /// When `true`, cache misses fall through to the transport. Defaults to `false` so unit tests are offline-only.\n    online: bool,\n}\n\nimpl<T: HttpClient> CachedHttpClient<T> {\n    /// Construct a cached client. `online` defaults to whether the\n    /// `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API` environment variable is set to a truthy value.\n    pub fn new(cache_dir: impl Into<PathBuf>, transport: T) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            cache_dir: cache_dir.into(),\n            transport,\n            online: live_api_enabled(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Override the online flag explicitly. The cache\n/// writes `<root>/<directory>/<stem>.body` and `<root>/<directory>/<stem>.url`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct CacheLocation {\n    pub directory: PathBuf,\n    pub stem: String,\n}\n\n/// Decide the cache location for a URL.\n///\n/// The mapping is best-effort: well-known Wikidata / Wiktionary URLs land\n/// under human-readable semantic folders, and anything else falls back to\n/// a hashed bucket so we never refuse to cache a response.\n#[must_use]\npub fn cache_location(url: &str) -> CacheLocation {\n    if let Some(location) = classify_wiktionary(url) {\n        return location;\n    }\n    if let Some(location) = classify_wikidata(url) {\n        return location;\n    }\n    CacheLocation {\n        directory:  let after_scheme = &url[host_start..];\n    let dot = after_scheme.find('.')?;\n    let host_end = after_scheme.find('/').unwrap_or(after_scheme.len());\n    let host_rest = &after_scheme[dot..host_end];\n    if !host_rest.starts_with(\".wiktionary.org\") {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let lang = sanitize_segment(&after_scheme[..dot]);\n    let page = wiktionary_page_from_url(url).unwrap_or_else(|| cache_key(url));\n    Some(CacheLocation {\n        directory: PathBuf::from(\"wiktionary-cache\").join(lang),\n        stem: page,\n    })\n}\n\nfn wiktionary_page_from_url(url: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Pages are fetched via the `parse` API:\n    //   /w/api.php?action=parse&page=<title>&...\n    let query_start = url.find('?')?;\n !decoded.is_empty() {\n                return Some(sanitize_segment(&decoded));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\nfn classify_wikidata(url: &str) -> Option<CacheLocation> {\n    if !url.contains(\"wikidata.org\") {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let query_start = url.find('?')?;\n    let query = &url[query_start + 1..];\n    let mut action: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut srsearch: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut ids: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut sparql: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut titles: Option<String> = None;\n    for pair in query.split('&') {\n srsearch = Some(percent_decode(value));\n        } else if let Some(value) = pair.strip_prefix(\"ids=\") {\n            ids = Some(percent_decode(value));\n        } else if let Some(value) =
