{\n  const haystack = String(normalized || \"\").toLowerCase();\n  const raw = String(prompt || \"\");\n  const rawLower = String(prompt || \"\").toLowerCase();\n  for (const { verb, op } of FORMALIZATION_VERBS) {\n    if (haystack.startsWith(verb + \" \") || haystack === verb) {\n      return {\n        op,\n        verb,\n        objectText: haystack === verb ? \"\" : normalized.slice(verb.length),\n        interpretations: [],\n      };\n    }\n    if (rawLower.startsWith(verb + \" \") || rawLower === verb) {\n      return {\n        op,\n        verb,\n        objectText: rawLower === verb ? \"\" : raw.slice(verb.length),\n        interpretations: [],\n      };\n    }\n    if (haystack.includes(\" \" + verb + \" \")) {\n      return { op, verb, objectText: null, interpretations: [] };\n    }\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nfunction fuzzyFormalizationMatch(prompt) {\n  const matches = FORMALIZATION_VERBS\n    .map((entry) => {\n      const match = fuzzyPrefixMatch(prompt, entry.verb);\n      return match ? Object.assign({ entry }, match) : null;\n    })\n    .filter(Boolean)\n    .sort((left, right) =>\n      left.typoCount - right.typoCount || right.end - left.end,\n    );\n  const best = matches[0];\n  if (!best) return null;\n  const peers = matches.filter(\n    (match) => match.typoCount === best.typoCount && match.end === best.end,\n  );\n  if (peers.length > 1) {\n    return {\n      ambiguous: true,\n      suggestions: peers.map((match) => match.entry.verb),\n      interpretations: [],\n    };\n  }\n  return {\n    op: best.entry.op,\n    verb: best.entry.verb,\n    objectText: String(prompt || \"\").slice(best.end),\n    interpretations: [best.interpretation],\n  };\n}\n\nfunction detectFormalizationMatch(prompt, normalized) {\n  return exactFormalizationMatch(prompt, normalized) || fuzzyFormalizationMatch(prompt);\n}\n\nfunction objectForFormalization(prompt, normalized, match) {\n  // For search-style ops we extract the explicit query the same way the web\n  // search handler does. For other ops we keep the prompt body that follows\n  // the detected verb so the tuple shows what the user is asking about.\n  const op = match && match.op;\n  if (op === \"OP:search\" || op === \"OP:lookup\") {\n    const query = extractWebSearchQuery(prompt, normalized);\n    if (query) return query;\n  }\n  if (op === \"OP:procedure\") {\n    const task = extractProceduralHowToTask(normalized);\n    if (task) return task.task;\n  }\n  const haystack = String(normalized || \"\").toLowerCase();\n  for (const { verb } of FORMALIZATION_VERBS) {\n    if (haystack.startsWith(verb + \" \")) {\n      return cleanSearchQuery(normalized.slice(verb.length));\n    }\n  }\n  if (match && typeof match.objectText === \"string\") {\n    return cleanSearchQuery(match.objectText);\n  }\n  return cleanSearchQuery(normalized || \"\");\n}\n\nfunction virtualObjectId(term) {\n  const trimmed = String(term || \"\").trim();\n  if (!trimmed) return \"?\";\n  return `?${trimmed}`;\n}\n\nfunction formatFormalizationTuple(parts) {\n  return `(${parts.filter(Boolean).join(\" \")})`;\n}\n\nfunction buildFormalization(prompt, normalized) {\n  const match = detectFormalizationMatch(prompt, normalized);\n  if (!match || match.ambiguous) {\n    const fallback = normalized || \"(empty)\";\n    return {\n      raw: String(prompt || \"\"),\n      subject: \"@USER\",\n      verb: \"OP:express\",\n      object: virtualObjectId(fallback),\n      tuple: formatFormalizationTuple([\"@USER\", \"OP:express\", virtualObjectId(fallback)]),\n      needsClarification: Boolean(match && match.ambiguous),\n      suggestions: match && match.suggestions ? if (probability >= 1) return true;\n  if (!randomize) return probability >= 0.5;\n  return Math.random() < probability;\n}\n\nfunction courtesyResponseFor(language, preferences) {\n  const prefs = definitionFusionByDefault(preferences) {\n  const value = preferences && preferences.definitionFusion;\n  if (value === true) return true;\n  if (value === false) return false;\n  const normalized = time.\n\nfunction normalizePrompt(prompt) {\n  const text = String(prompt || \"\");\n  const fromWasm = wasmNormalizePrompt(text);\n  if (fromWasm !== null) return fromWasm;\n  return text\n    .toLowerCase()\n    .replace(/[^\\p{L}\\p{N}]+/gu, \" \")\n    .trim();\n}\n\nfunction normalizeConceptTerm(value) {\n  let lower = String(value || \"\").toLowerCase();\n  for (const prefix of [\"the \", \"a \", \"an \"]) {\n    if (lower.startsWith(prefix)) {\n      lower = lower.slice(prefix.length);\n      break;\n    }\n  }\n  return lower.trim().replace(/[?.!,;:]+$/g, (Array.isArray(record.aliases) &&\n      record.aliases.some(\n        (alias) => normalizeConceptTerm(alias) === normalized,\n      ))\n  );\n}\n\nfunction recordMatchesQueryTerm(record, normalized, contextNormalized) {\n  if (recordMatchesTerm(record, normalized)) return true;\n  if (!contextNormalized) return false;\n  return recordMatchesTerm(record, `${normalized} contextRecord.aliases.some(\n      (alias) => normalizeConceptTerm(alias) === contextNormalized,\n    )\n  ) {\n    return true;\n  }\n  return (\n    Array.isArray(contextRecord.labels) &&\n    contextRecord.labels.some(\n      (label) => normalizeConceptTerm(label.text) === contextNormalized,\n    )\n  );\n}\n\nfunction resolveContextRecord(contextNormalized) {\n  if (!contextNormalized) return null;\n  for (const record of CONCEPT_CONTEXTS) {\n    if (contextRecordMatches(record, contextNormalized)) return record;\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nfunction recordHasContext(record, contextNormalized) {\n  if (\n    Array.isArray(record.contexts) &&\n    record.contexts.some(\n      (candidate) => normalizeConceptTerm(candidate) === contextNormalized,\n    )\n  ) {\n    return true;\n  }\n  // Registry fallback: resolve the user-supplied context through the\n  // concept-contexts registry and see whether the resolved record's slug is\n  // referenced by the concept's Matches the Rust\n  // ranker (src/concepts.rs::record_has_context).\n  const contextRecord = resolveContextRecord(contextNormalized);\n  if (contextRecord && Array.isArray(record.contextLinks)) {\n    return record.contextLinks.some(\n      (slug) => String(slug).trim() === contextRecord.slug,\n    );\n  }\n  return false;\n}\n\nfunction localizedConceptFor(record, language) {\n  if (!record || ||\n    null\n  );\n}\n\nfunction contextLabelFor(contextRecord, language) {\n  if (!contextRecord || !Array.isArray(contextRecord.labels)) {\n    return null;\n  }\n  const exact = contextRecord.labels.find(\n    (label) => label && label.language === language,\n  );\n  if (exact && exact.text) return exact.text;\n  const english = contextRecord.labels.find(\n    (label) => label && label.language === \"en\",\n  );\n  if (english && english.text) return english.text;\n  return contextRecord.slug || null;\n}\n\nfunction rankConceptForPair(termRaw, contextRaw) {\n  const normalized = normalizeConceptTerm(termRaw);\n  if (!normalized) return null;\n  const contextNormalized = contextRaw ? normalizeConceptTerm(contextRaw) : \"\";\n\n  const termMatches = CONCEPTS.filter((record) =>\n    recordMatchesQueryTerm(record, normalized, contextNormalized),\n  );\n  if (termMatches.length === 0) return null;\n\n  if (contextNormalized) {\n    const ctxHit = termMatches.find((record) =>\n      recordHasContext(record, contextNormalized),\n    );\n    if (ctxHit) {\n      return {\n        record: ctxHit,\n        contextMatch: true,\n        context: contextNormalized,\n      };\n    }\n  }\n\n  // No context match: prefer records with no contexts declared.\n  termMatches.sort((a, b) => {\n    const ac = (Array.isArray(a.contexts) && a.contexts.length > 0) ? 1 : 0;\n    const bc = (Array.isArray(b.contexts) && b.contexts.length > 0) ? 1 : 0;\n    return ac - bc;\n  });\n  return {\n    record: termMatches[0],\n    contextMatch: false,\n    context: contextNormalized || null,\n  };\n}\n\nfunction lookupConceptQuery(query) {\n  if (!query) return null;\n  const direct = rankConceptForPair(query.term, query.context);\n  if (query.context) {\n    const reversed = rankConceptForPair(query.context, query.term);\n    if (reversed && (!direct || (!direct.contextMatch && reversed.contextMatch))) {\n      return reversed;\n {\n    return {\n      coefficient: left.coefficient - right.coefficient,\n      constant: left.constant - right.constant,\n    };\n  }\n\n  function multiply(left, right) {\n    if (hasVariable(left) looksLikeRuntimeRuleUpdate(text) {\n  const raw = String(text || \"\");\n  const lower = raw.toLowerCase();\n  if (\n    (lower.includes(\"when i say\") && (lower.includes(\"answer\") || 1] === right[j - 1]\n        ? dp[i - 1][j - 1]\n        : 1 + Math.min(dp[i - 1][j - 1], dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1]);\n      if (\n        i > 1 &&\n        j > 1 &&\n        left[i - 1] === right[j - 2] &&\n        left[i - 2] === right[j - 1]\n      ) {\n        dp[i][j] = Math.min(dp[i][j], dp[i - 2][j - 2] + 1);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  return dp[m][n];\n}\n\nfunction isCloseTokenTypo(actual, expected) {\n  const left = String(actual || \"\").toLowerCase();\n  const right = String(expected || \"\").toLowerCase();\n  const leftLength = Array.from(left).length;\n  const rightLength = Array.from(right).length;\n  return Math.min(leftLength, rightLength) >= 4 && editDistance(left, right) === 1;\n}\n\nfunction leadingTokenSpans(value, limit) {\n  const text = String(value || \"\");\n  const spans = [];\n  const pattern = /\\S+/gu;\n  let match;\n  while ((match = pattern.exec(text)) !== null && spans.length < limit) {\n    spans.push({\n      start: match.index,\n      end: match.index + match[0].length,\n      text: match[0],\n    });\n  }\n  return spans;\n}\n\nfunction fuzzyPrefixMatch(value, prefix) {\n  const words = String(prefix || \"\").trim().split(/\\s+/u).filter(Boolean);\n  if (words.length === 0) return null;\n  const spans = leadingTokenSpans(value, words.length);\n  if (spans.length !== words.length) return null;\n  let typoCount = 0;\n  for (let i = 0; i < words.length; i += 1) {\n    const actual = spans[i].text;\n    const expected = words[i];\n    if (actual.toLowerCase() === expected.toLowerCase()) continue;\n    if (!isCloseTokenTypo(actual, expected)) return null;\n    typoCount += 1;\n  }\n  if (typoCount !== 1) return null;\n  const end = spans[spans.length - 1].end;\n  return {\n    typoCount,\n    end,\n    interpretation: {\n      original: String(value || \"\").slice(0, end),\n      corrected: String(prefix || \"\").trim(),\n    },\n  };\n}\n\nfunction stripKnownPrefix(value, prefixes) {\n  const text = String(value || \"\");\n  const lower = text.toLowerCase();\n  for (const prefix of prefixes) {\n    if (lower.startsWith(prefix)) {\n      return { value: text.slice(prefix.length).trimStart(), interpretation: null };\n    }\n  }\n  const matches = prefixes\n    .map((prefix) => fuzzyPrefixMatch(text, prefix))\n    .filter(Boolean)\n    .sort((left, right) =>\n      left.typoCount - part.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + part.slice(1) : part,\n    )\n    .join(\"\");\n}\n\nfunction wikipediaTermVariants(term) {\n  const seen = new Set();\n  const variants = [];\n  const push = (value) => {\n    if (!value) return;\n    const slug = String(value)\n      .trim()\n      .replace(/\\s+/g, \"_\")\n      .replace(/_+/g, \"_\");\n    if (!slug || seen.has(slug)) return;\n    seen.add(slug);\n    variants.push(slug);\n  };\n  const trimmed = String(term || \"\").trim();\n  push(trimmed);\n  push(capitalizeWords(trimmed));\n  push(capitalizeWords(trimmed.toLowerCase()));\n  push(trimmed.toLowerCase());\n  // Biography titles on Wikipedia (notably ru.wikipedia.org) use the\n  // \"Surname, Given names\" form: querying \"Илон Маск\" 404s, but \"Маск, Илон\"\n  // resolves. 0 : 1;\n      const next = Math.min(\n        previous[j] + 1,\n        current[j - 1] + 1,\n        previous[j - 1] + cost,\n      );\n      current[j] = next;\n      rowMin = Math.min(rowMin, next);\n    }\n    if (rowMin > limit) return limit + 1;\n    previous = current;\n  }\n  return previous[right.length];\n}\n\nfunction isNearLookupText(left, right) {\n  const a = compactLookupText(left);\n  const b = compactLookupText(right);\n  if (!a || !b) return false;\n  const maxLength = Math.max(a.length, b.length);\n  const limit = maxLength <= 8 ? 1 : 2;\n  return boundedEditDistance(a, b, limit) <= limit;\n}\n\nfunction isPlausibleWikipediaSearchMatch(summary, term) {\n  if (\n    !summary ||\n    (summary.matchKind !== \"search\" && summary.matchKind !== \"context_search\")\n  ) {\n    return true;\n  }\n  const termNormalized = normalizeLookupText(term);\n  if (!termNormalized) return true;\n  const termTokens = termNormalized.split(/\\s+/).filter(Boolean);\n  const candidates = [\n    summary.title,\n    summary.matchedTitle,\n    String(summary.matchedSlug || \"\").replace(/_/g, \" \"),\n    summary.extract,\n  ];\n  for (const candidate of candidates) {\n    const normalized = normalizeLookupText(candidate);\n    if (!normalized) continue;\n    if (normalized === termNormalized) return true;\n    const candidateTokens = new Set(normalized.split(/\\s+/).filter(Boolean));\n    if (\n      termTokens.length > 0 &&\n      termTokens.every((token) => candidateTokens.has(token))\n    ) {\n      return true;\n    }\n    if (isNearLookupText(termNormalized, normalized)) return true;\n  }\n  return false;\n}\n\n// Resolve a context-qualified term to a Wikipedia page slug via full-text page\n// search. Tries multiple query formulations (uppercase term, mixed case) on the\n// detected language host then on English, returning the first match found.\n// This helps disambiguate short acronyms like \"KISS\" or \"DRY\" when the user\n// provides a programming/domain context.\nasync function searchWikipediaSlug(term, context, language) {\n  if (typeof fetch !== \"function\") return null;\n  const apiHeaders = {\n    accept: \"application/json\",\n    \"api-user-agent\":\n      \"formal-ai-demo (https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai)\",\n  };\n  const upper = term.toUpperCase();\n  // Build candidate queries in preference order: uppercase term with context is\n  // most discriminating; plain term with context is the fallback.\n  const queries = [];\n  if (upper !== term) queries.push(`${upper} ${context}`.trim());\n  queries.push(`${term} ${context}`.trim());\n  const ordered = [language, \"en\"].filter(\n    (value, index, array) => value && array.indexOf(value) === index,\n  );\n  for (const lang of ordered) {\n    const base = WIKIPEDIA_SEARCH_HOSTS[lang] || WIKIPEDIA_SEARCH_HOSTS.en;\n    for (const query of queries) {\n      const url = `${base}?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}&limit=5`;\n      try {\n        const response = await fetch(url, { headers: apiHeaders });\n        if (!response || !response.ok) continue;\n        const data = await response.json();\n        if (!data || !Array.isArray(data.pages) || data.pages.length === 0)\n          continue;\n        // Return the key of the top result; callers will fetch the full summary.\n        const page = data.pages[0];\n        return {\n          slug: page.key,\n          title: page.title || page.key,\n          language: lang,\n          query,\n        };\n      } catch (_error) {\n        // Ignore and try next query / language host.\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nasync function fetchWikipediaSummary(term, language, context) {\n  if (typeof fetch !== \"function\") return null;\n  const apiHeaders = {\n    accept: \"application/json\",\n    \"api-user-agent\":\n      \"formal-ai-demo (https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai)\",\n  };\n\n  // When context is provided, first try a title-search to find the most\n  // relevant article slug (e.g. \"Kiss\" + \"рамках програмирования\" → \"KISS\n  // principle\"). This prevents ambiguous short terms from matching the wrong\n  // article (e.g. the rock band instead of the software design principle).\n  if (context) {\n    const found = await searchWikipediaSlug(term, context, language);\n    if (found) {\n      const summaryBase =\n        WIKIPEDIA_HOSTS[found.language] || WIKIPEDIA_HOSTS.en;\n      const url = `${summaryBase}/${encodeURIComponent(found.slug)}`;\n      try {\n        const response = await fetch(url, { headers: apiHeaders });\n        if (response && response.ok) {\n          const data = await response.json();\n          if (\n            data &&\n            typeof data === \"object\" &&\n            data.type !== \"disambiguation\"\n          ) {\n            const extract = String(data.extract || \"\").trim();\n            if (extract) {\n              const title = String(data.title || term);\n              const pageUrl =\n                (data.content_urls &&\n                  data.content_urls.desktop &&\n                  data.content_urls.desktop.page) ||\n                url;\n              return {\n                title,\n                extract,\n                url: pageUrl,\n                language: found.language,\n                matchKind: \"context_search\",\n                matchedSlug: found.slug,\n                matchedTitle: found.title || title,\n                searchQuery: found.query || \"\",\n              };\n            }\n          }\n        }\n      } catch (_error) {\n        // Fall through to bare-term lookup below.\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Bare-term fallback: try direct slug variants without context.\n  const hosts = wikipediaHostsFor(language);\n  const variants = wikipediaTermVariants(term);\n  for (const host of hosts) {\n    for (const slug of variants) {\n      const url = `${host.url}/${encodeURIComponent(slug)}`;\n      try {\n        const response = await fetch(url, { headers: apiHeaders });\n        if (!response || !response.ok) continue;\n        const data = await response.json();\n        if (!data || typeof data !== \"object\") continue;\n        if (data.type === \"disambiguation\") continue;\n        const extract = String(data.extract || \"\").trim();\n        if (!extract) continue;\n        const title = String(data.title || term);\n        const pageUrl =\n          (data.content_urls &&\n            data.content_urls.desktop &&\n            data.content_urls.desktop.page) ||\n          url;\n        return {\n          title,\n          extract,\n          url: pageUrl,\n          language: host.language,\n          matchKind: \"direct\",\n          matchedSlug: slug,\n        };\n      } catch (_error) {\n        // Swallow network/parse errors and continue to the next variant.\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  // All direct slug variants were disambiguation pages or not found. Use the\n  // full-text search endpoint to find the top-ranked article for the term\n  // (e.g. \"tesla\" → \"Tesla, Inc.\" instead of the disambiguation page).\n  const found = await searchWikipediaSlug(term, \"\", language);\n  if (found) {\n    const summaryBase = WIKIPEDIA_HOSTS[found.language] || WIKIPEDIA_HOSTS.en;\n    const url = `${summaryBase}/${encodeURIComponent(found.slug)}`;\n    try {\n      const response = await fetch(url, { headers: apiHeaders });\n      if (response && response.ok) {\n        const data = await response.json();\n        if (\n          data &&\n          typeof data === \"object\" &&\n          data.type !== \"disambiguation\"\n        ) {\n          const extract = String(data.extract || \"\").trim();\n          if (extract) {\n            const title = String(data.title || term);\n            const pageUrl =\n              (data.content_urls &&\n                data.content_urls.desktop &&\n                data.content_urls.desktop.page) ||\n              url;\n            return {\n              title,\n              extract,\n              url: pageUrl,\n              language: found.language,\n              matchKind: \"search\",\n              matchedSlug: found.slug,\n              matchedTitle: found.title || title,\n              searchQuery: found.query || \"\",\n            };\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    } catch (_error) {\n      // Search-based fallback failed; return null below.\n    }\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nfunction isClosestWikipediaMatch(summary) {\n  return summary && summary.matchKind === \"search\";\n}\n\nfunction closestMatchNote(summary, language) {\n  const title = summary && summary.title ? summary.title : \"the top result\";\n  if (language === \"ru\") {\n    return `Ближайшее совпадение по поиску Wikipedia: «${title}». Уточните, отвечать по этой статье Wikipedia?`;\n  }\n  if (language === \"zh\") {\n    return `你是指“${title}”吗？请确认后我再根据这篇 Wikipedia 文章回答。`;\n  }\n  if (language === \"hi\") {\n    return `क्या आपका मतलब \"${title}\" था? Please clarify before I answer from that Wikipedia article.`;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Wikidata-backed fact reasoning pipeline (issue #127).\n//\n// Rather than matching against hardcoded summaries in `data/seed/facts.lino`,\n// fact questions (\"what is the capital of X?\", \"столица X\", \"X की राजधानी\",\n// \"X的首都\") are parsed into a structured query\n// `{ relation, subjectTerm, language, forceFresh }`. The query is then\n// resolved against:\n//\n//   1. An in-memory cache (1-week TTL) keyed by `relation:subject:language`.\n//      The cache is pre-warmed from the seed `FACTS` entries so the test\n//      matrix stays deterministic offline.\n//   2. Wikidata `wbsearchentities` to resolve the subject term to a Q-ID.\n//   3. Wikidata `wbgetentities` to fetch the property claim (P36 = capital,\n//      P1082 = population, P38 = currency, P37 = official language, P30 =\n//      continent, P2046 = area, P35 = head of state, P6 = head of government).\n//   4. Detected in all\n// four supported languages plus a couple of common English phrasings.\nconst FORCE_FRESH_MARKERS = [\n  \"fresh\",\n  \"no cache\",\n  \"no-cache\",\n  \"without cache\",\n  \"skip cache\",\n  \"ignore cache\",\n  \"refresh\",\n  \"не из кэша\",\n  \"не из кеша\",\n  \"без кэша\",\n  \"без кеша\",\n  \"обнови\",\n  \"свежий ответ\",\n  \"свежие данные\",\n  \"ताज़ा\",\n  \"ताज़े\",\n  \"बिना कैश\",\n  \"नया जवाब\",\n  \"刷新\",\n  \"新鲜\",\n  \"不要缓存\",\n  \"不用缓存\",\n];\n\nfunction shouldForceFresh(normalized, prompt) {\n  const lowerPrompt = String(prompt || \"\").toLowerCase();\n  return FORCE_FRESH_MARKERS.some(\n    (marker) => normalized.includes(marker) || lowerPrompt.includes(marker),\n  );\n}\n\n// Multilingual relation patterns. Order matters: longer prefixes first.\nconst SUBJECT_TRIM_PREFIXES = [\n  \"the country called \",\n  \"the country \",\n  \"country \",\n  \"the city of \",\n  \"the city \",\n  \"city of \",\n  \"country called \",\n  \"republic of \",\n  \"kingdom of \",\n  \"is \",\n  \"in \",\n  \"of the \",\n  \"of \",\n  \"страна \",\n  \"страны \",\n  \"стране \",\n  \"страну \",\n];\n\nfunction trimSubjectTerm(raw) {\n  let value = String(raw || \"\")\n    .replace(/[«»\"'`“”„‟‹›]+/g, \"\")\n    .replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n    .trim();\n  let changed = true;\n  while (changed) {\n    changed = false;\n    const lower = value.toLowerCase();\n    for (const prefix of SUBJECT_TRIM_PREFIXES) {\n      if (lower.startsWith(prefix)) {\n        value = value.slice(prefix.length).trim();\n        changed = true;\n        break;\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  return value;\n}\n\nfunction parseFactQuestion(prompt, normalized) {\n  const text = String(prompt || \"\");\n  if (!text.trim()) return null;\n  for (const pattern of FACT_QUESTION_PATTERNS) {\n    for (const regex of pattern.extract) {\n      const match = regex.exec(text);\n      if (!match) continue;\n      const subjectTerm = trimSubjectTerm(match[1]);\n      if (!subjectTerm) continue;\n      // Reject single-letter or pure-punctuation captures so we don't fire\n      // on noise like \"x.\" or \"?\".\n      if (subjectTerm.length < 2 && !/[Ѐ-鿿]/.test(subjectTerm)) {\n        continue;\n      }\n      return {\n        relation: pattern.relation,\n        subjectTerm,\n        language: detectLanguage(prompt),\n        forceFresh: shouldForceFresh(normalized, prompt),\n      };\n    }\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\n// In-memory cache. Keyed by `relation:subject_normalized:language`. The TTL\n// matches the user-requested 1 week. Pre-warmed from FACTS at init() so the\n// offline test matrix sees the same starting cache the Rust solver does.\nconst FACT_QUERY_CACHE = new Map();\nconst FACT_QUERY_TTL_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;\n\nfunction factCacheKey(relation, subjectTerm, language) {\n  return [\n    String(relation || \"\").toLowerCase(),\n    String(subjectTerm || \"\")\n      .toLowerCase()\n      .replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n      .trim(),\n    String(language || \"en\").toLowerCase(),\n  ].join(\":\");\n}\n\nfunction factCacheGet(relation, subjectTerm, language) {\n  const key = factCacheKey(relation, subjectTerm, language);\n  const entry = FACT_QUERY_CACHE.get(key);\n  if (!entry) return null;\n  if (\n    entry.expiresAt &&\n    typeof entry.expiresAt === \"number\" &&\n    entry.expiresAt < Date.now()\n  ) {\n    FACT_QUERY_CACHE.delete(key);\n    return null;\n  }\n  return entry;\n}\n\nfunction factCachePut(relation, subjectTerm, language, value) {\n  const key = factCacheKey(relation, subjectTerm, language);\n  const ttl = typeof value.ttlMs === \"number\" ? value.ttlMs : FACT_QUERY_TTL_MS;\n  const entry = Object.assign({}, value, {\n    expiresAt: Date.now() + ttl,\n  });\n  FACT_QUERY_CACHE.set(key, entry);\n  return entry;\n}\n\n// Pre-warm the runtime cache from the seed `facts.lino`. We return a shared promise so concurrent\n// callers cooperate on the same probe batch.\nfunction ensureWebSearchProviderProbes() {\n  if (WEB_SEARCH_PROBE_PROMISE) return WEB_SEARCH_PROBE_PROMISE;\n  if (typeof fetch !== \"function\") {\n    WEB_SEARCH_PROBE_PROMISE = Promise.resolve([]);\n    return WEB_SEARCH_PROBE_PROMISE;\n  }\n  WEB_SEARCH_PROBE_PROMISE = (async () => {\n    const tasks = WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDERS.map((provider) => async () => {\n      if (!provider.probeUrl) return null;\n      const startedAt = Date.now();\n      try {\n        const response = await fetch(provider.probeUrl, { mode: \"cors\" });\n        const status = response ? Tasks are async functions returning a value; results are\n  // returned in the original order.\n  const cap = Math.max(1, Math.min(limit, tasks.length));\n  const results = new Array(tasks.length);\n  let cursor = 0;\n  async function worker() {\n    while (true) {\n      const index = cursor;\n      cursor += 1;\n      if (index >= tasks.length) return;\n      results[index] = await tasks[index]();\n    }\n  }\n  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: cap }, () => worker()));\n  return results;\n}\n\nfunction reciprocalRankFusion(perProviderResults, k) {\n  // R194: the Rust/WASM core owns the fusion logic so the offline trace and\n  // the browser worker agree to the last byte. We try WASM first and only\n  // fall back to the JS implementation when the worker booted in\n  // `js fallback` mode (e.g. WASM disabled in the browser).\n  const wasmFused = wasmReciprocalRankFusion(perProviderResults);\n  if (wasmFused !== null) {\n    return wasmFused;\n  }\n  // Cormack, Clarke, Buettcher 2009: score(d) = Σ 1 / (k + rank_i(d)).\n  const fused = new Map();\n  for (const provider of perProviderResults) {\n    const list = Array.isArray(provider.results) ? provider.results : [];\n    list.forEach((item, index) => {\n      if (!item || !item.url) return;\n      const rank = index + 1;\n      const score = 1 / (k + rank);\n      const existing = fused.get(item.url);\n      if (existing) {\n        existing.score += score;\n        existing.providers.push({ id: provider.id, rank });\n        if (!existing.title && item.title) existing.title = item.title;\n        if (!existing.excerpt && item.excerpt) existing.excerpt = item.excerpt;\n      } else {\n        fused.set(item.url, {\n          url: item.url,\n          title: item.title || item.url,\n          excerpt: item.excerpt || \"\",\n          score,\n          providers: [{ id: provider.id, rank }],\n        });\n      }\n    });\n  }\n  return Array.from(fused.values()).sort((a, b) => {\n    if (b.score !== a.score) return b.score - a.score;\n    return b.providers.length - a.providers.length;\n  });\n}\n\n// Issue #153/#180: identify \"the same entity\" returned by different providers\n// so the fused list shows one bullet with the other URLs collapsed under\n// \"Other sources:\". A single result can carry several canonical identifiers\n// (Wikidata Q-id, Wikipedia page key, Wiktionary headword) — dedupe walks all\n// of them and merges into the first existing group it finds. Returning a\n// list makes the Wikipedia↔Wikidata merge robust against percent-encoding\n// differences in the two providers' URLs.\nfunction canonicalEntityKeys(meta) {\n  if (!meta) return [];\n  const keys = [];\n  if (meta.qid && /^Q\\d+$/.test(meta.qid)) keys.push(`Q:${meta.qid}`);\n  if (meta.wikipediaKey) {\n    const lang = meta.wikipediaLanguage || \"en\";\n    keys.push(`WP:${lang}:${meta.wikipediaKey}`);\n  }\n  if (meta.wiktionaryKey) {\n    const lang = meta.wiktionaryLanguage || \"en\";\n    keys.push(`WT:${lang}:${meta.wiktionaryKey}`);\n  }\n  return keys;\n}\n\n// Backwards-compatible shim: prefer the primary key but keep the historical\n// single-key signature for callers that still rely on it.\nfunction canonicalEntityKey(meta) {\n  const keys = canonicalEntityKeys(meta);\n  return keys.length > 0 ? keys[0] : null;\n}\n\nfunction buildItemMetadataIndex(perProvider) {\n  // The richer the meta the better — an entry that carries a Wikidata `qid`\n  // is preferred over a Wikipedia-only entry for the same URL, because the\n  // Q-id is what cross-provider dedupe groups by. Without this preference,\n  // the Wikipedia URL would be indexed by the Wikipedia provider's meta\n  // (`WP:en:Apple`) and a separate Wikidata entry for the same fact (`Q:Q89`)\n  // would never collapse into one bullet.\n  const byUrl = new Map();\n  const rank = (item) => (item && item.qid ? 2 : 1);\n  function record(url, item) {\n    if (!url || !item) return;\n    const existing = byUrl.get(url);\n    if (!existing || rank(item) > rank(existing)) {\n      byUrl.set(url, item);\n    }\n  }\n  for (const provider of perProvider) {\n    if (!provider || !Array.isArray(provider.results)) continue;\n    for (const item of provider.results) {\n      if (!item || !item.url) continue;\n      record(item.url, item);\n      // Wikidata results carry the Wikipedia URL of the same entity inline;\n      // index that too so the Wikipedia provider's entry is recognised as\n      // a duplicate of the Wikidata one.\n      if (item.wikipediaUrl) record(item.wikipediaUrl, item);\n    }\n  }\n  return byUrl;\n}\n\nfunction dedupeFusedEntries(fused, metaByUrl, evidence) {\n  const groupsByKey = new Map();\n  const allGroups = [];\n  const standalone = [];\n\n  function alreadyHasProvider(target, candidate) {\n    return target.providers.some(\n      (existing) => existing.id === candidate.id && existing.rank === candidate.rank,\n    );\n  }\n\n  fused.forEach((entry, index) => {\n    const meta = metaByUrl.get(entry.url) || null;\n    const keys = canonicalEntityKeys(meta);\n    const enriched = Object.assign({}, entry, {\n      qid: (meta && meta.qid) || \"\",\n      wikipediaKey: (meta && meta.wikipediaKey) || \"\",\n      wikipediaLanguage: (meta && meta.wikipediaLanguage) || \"\",\n      wiktionaryKey: (meta && meta.wiktionaryKey) || \"\",\n      wiktionaryLanguage: (meta && meta.wiktionaryLanguage) || \"\",\n      sourceKind: (meta && meta.sourceKind) || \"\",\n      virtualId:\n        (meta && meta.virtualId) ||\n        (meta && meta.qid) ||\n        (meta && meta.wikipediaKey ? `WP:${meta.wikipediaKey}` : \"\"),\n      alternateUrls: [],\n      keys: keys.slice(),\n      originalRank: index,\n    });\n\n    if (keys.length === 0) {\n      standalone.push(enriched);\n      return;\n    }\n    let head = null;\n    for (const key of keys) {\n      if (groupsByKey.has(key)) {\n        head = groupsByKey.get(key);\n        break;\n      }\n    }\n    if (!head) {\n      allGroups.push(enriched);\n      for (const key of keys) {\n        if (!groupsByKey.has(key)) groupsByKey.set(key, enriched);\n      }\n      return;\n    }\n    // Found an existing group — absorb this entry into it.\n    head.score += enriched.score;\n    head.alternateUrls.push({\n      url: enriched.url,\n      title: enriched.title,\n      providers: enriched.providers,\n      sourceKind: enriched.sourceKind,\n    });\n    for (const p of enriched.providers) {\n      if (!alreadyHasProvider(head, p)) head.providers.push(p);\n    }\n    // Register the absorbed entry's keys against the head group too so a third\n    // provider matching either canonical id still merges in.\n    for (const key of keys) {\n      if (!groupsByKey.has(key)) groupsByKey.set(key, head);\n    }\n    // Prefer the richest virtualId once we know more identifiers.\n    if (!head.virtualId && enriched.virtualId) head.virtualId = enriched.virtualId;\n    if (!head.qid && enriched.qid) head.qid = enriched.qid;\n    if (!head.wikipediaKey && enriched.wikipediaKey) {\n      head.wikipediaKey = enriched.wikipediaKey;\n      head.wikipediaLanguage = enriched.wikipediaLanguage;\n    }\n    if (!head.wiktionaryKey && enriched.wiktionaryKey) {\n      head.wiktionaryKey = enriched.wiktionaryKey;\n      head.wiktionaryLanguage = enriched.wiktionaryLanguage;\n    }\n    if (Array.isArray(evidence)) {\n      evidence.push(`web_search:dedupe:${keys[0]}:absorbed:${enriched.url}`);\n    }\n  });\n  const merged = [...allGroups, ...standalone];\n  merged.sort((a, b) => {\n    if (b.score !== a.score) return b.score - a.score;\n    if (b.providers.length !== a.providers.length) {\n      return b.providers.length - a.providers.length;\n    }\n    // Issue #180: stable order by provider priority so DDG-led entries beat\n    // Wikidata-only entries on perfect ties.\n    const ap = providerPriorityScore(a.providers);\n    const bp = providerPriorityScore(b.providers);\n    if (ap !== bp) return ap - bp;\n    return a.originalRank - b.originalRank;\n  });\n  return merged;\n}\n\nfunction providerPriorityScore(providers) {\n  if (!Array.isArray(providers) || providers.length === 0) return 999;\n  let best = 999;\n  for (const p of providers) {\n    const score = WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER_PRIORITY[p && p.id] || 999;\n    if (score < best) best = score;\n  }\n  return best;\n}\n\n// Issue #153: {\n  const haystack = String(normalized || \"\").toLowerCase();\n  const raw = String(prompt || \"\");\n  const rawLower = String(prompt || \"\").toLowerCase();\n  for (const { verb, op } of fuzzyPrefixMatch(prompt, entry.verb);\n      return match ? Object.assign({ entry }, match) : null;\n    })\n    .filter(Boolean)\n    .sort((left, right) =>\n      left.typoCount - right.typoCount || right.end - left.end,\n    );\n  const best = matches[0];\n  if (!best) return null;\n  const peers = matches.filter(\n    (match) => match.typoCount === best.typoCount && match.end === best.end,\n  );\n  if (peers.length > 1) {\n    return {\n      ambiguous: true,\n      suggestions: peers.map((match) => match.entry.verb),\n      interpretations: [],\n    };\n  }\n  return {\n    op: best.entry.op,\n    verb: best.entry.verb,\n    objectText: String(prompt || \"\").slice(best.end),\n    interpretations: [best.interpretation],\n  };\n}\n\nfunction detectFormalizationMatch(prompt, normalized) {\n  return exactFormalizationMatch(prompt, normalized) || fuzzyFormalizationMatch(prompt);\n}\n\nfunction objectForFormalization(prompt, normalized, match) {\n  // For search-style ops we extract the explicit query the same way the web\n  // search handler does. Words missing from the registry fell\n98\t   through to `[${target}] ${surface}` (line 3905 pre-fix). When\n117\t  enabled, every translation prints stage-by-stage to stderr so\n118\t  cache-miss vs sparse-Wiktionary-table vs polysemy can be\n119\t  distinguished in a single run.\n120\t- `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs`: grow the seed list from one\n121\t  noun + greetings to **71 English nouns × 4 targets and 71 Russian\n122\t  nouns × 1 target** — every word listed in the demo / regression set\n123\t  the issue exemplifies. `pairs` is now built procedurally so future\n124\t  expansions stay readable.\n125\t\n126\t### Single-file offline dictionary (revised 2026-05-22)\n127\t\n128\t- `data/seed/translations.lino` (new): the canonical 128-entry\n129\t  common-noun dictionary, indented Links Notation, ~1,300 lines.\n130\t  Embedded into the Rust binary via `include_str!` and fetched by the\n131\t  browser worker through the existing seed loader. One file → one\n132\t  source of truth across Rust, CLI, browser, and tests.\n133\t  Schema (one record per lemma):\n134\t\n135\t  ```text\n136\t  translation_en_tomato\n137\t    language \"en\"\n138\t    lemma \"tomato\"\n139\t    aliases \"tomato|tomatoes\"\n140\t    target \"ru\"\n141\t      surface \"помидор\"\n142\t    target \"hi\"\n143\t      surface \"टमाटर\"\n144\t    target \"zh\"\n145\t      surface \"番茄\"\n146\t  ```\n147\t\n148\t  `src/translation/dictionary.rs` parses the file once at startup\n149\t  (`OnceLock`) into a bidirectional `(language, surface_lower) →\n150\t  entry` map plus a reverse `(target_lang, target_surface_lower) →\n151\t  entry` map. The reverse map lets a single en→ru entry cover both\n152\t  directions, keeping the 128-entry cap meaningful.\n153\t\n154\t- `examples/build_translation_dictionary.rs` (revised): runs the\n155\t  cached pipeline against the seed list and writes\n156\t  `data/seed/translations.lino` instead of a JSON file. Inflection\n157\t  forms are generated deterministically — Russian declension suffixes\n158\t  by ending class and English plural rules — so `Переведи \"помидоры\"\n159\t  на английский.` still resolves to `tomato` via the alias index.\n160\t\n161\t### Generic semantic-key cache (revised 2026-05-22)\n162\t\n163\t- `src/translation/cache.rs` now routes URLs to per-source folders by\n164\t  the **kind of data** they carry, not by URL hash:\n165\t\n166\t  | URL pattern | Cache folder |\n167\t  | --- | --- |\n168\t  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities` | `data/wikidata-cache/search/` |\n169\t  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbgetentities` | `data/wikidata-cache/entities/` |\n170\t  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=query` | `data/wikidata-cache/query/` |\n171\t  | `query.wikidata.org/sparql` | `data/wikidata-cache/sparql/` |\n172\t  | `<lang>.wiktionary.org` | `data/wiktionary-cache/<lang>/` |\n173\t  | anything else | `data/http-cache/misc/` |\n174\t\n175\t  Every folder under `data/` listed above is gitignored — the cache\n176\t  is a local accelerator, not pre-seeded data. Formalisation flows\n177\t  beyond translation (entity resolution, fact lookup, etc.) reuse the\n178\t  same buckets so we never grow a per-feature cache silo again.\n179\t\n180\t### Browser worker (revised 2026-05-22)\n181\t\n182\t- `src/web/seed_loader.js`: a new `extractTranslations` parser mirrors\n183\t  the Rust `Dictionary::parse` (same bidirectional index, same alias\n184\t  handling). It runs as part of the standard `buildSeed` step so the\n185\t  worker hydrates the dictionary alongside facts, projects, concepts,\n186\t  and intent routing — no separate fetch, no JSON glue.\n187\t- `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js`: `TRANSLATION_DICTIONARY` is now\n188\t  populated directly from `seed.translations`; `lookupDictionary`\n189\t  consults the forward map first and falls back to the reverse map\n190\t  for the opposite direction. The previous JSON loader and\n191\t  `src/web/translation-dictionary.json` were deleted.\n192\t- Because the dictionary is capped at 128 entries (R221.cap) and most\n193\t  prompts will never hit it, the architecture stays mobile-friendly:\n194\t  uncached lookups fall through to the live Wiktionary / Wikidata\n195\t  APIs over `fetch()` instead of shipping a precomputed corpus.\n196\t\n197\t### Tests\n198\t\n199\t- `tests/unit/specification/translation_via_links.rs`: three new tests\n200\t  — `issue_221_common_russian_nouns_translate_to_english`,\n201\t  `issue_221_common_english_nouns_translate_to_russian`, and\n202\t  `issue_221_unquoted_common_noun_works_in_all_languages` — fail\n203\t  loudly when any of помидор/огурец/картофель/морковь/хлеб/вода or\n204\t  their English counterparts return a placeholder.\n205\t- `tests/e2e/tests/issue-221.spec.js`: Playwright coverage for the\n206\t  browser worker — same prompts as the Rust tests, plus the round-trip\n207\t  `ru→en→ru` to prove the dictionary keeps semantics symmetric.\n208\t\n209\t## Before / After\n210\t\n211\t| Prompt | Before (v0.100.0) | After |\n212\t| --- | --- | --- |\n213\t| `Переведи \"помидор\" на английский.` | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n214\t| `Переведи \"огурец\" на английский.` | `\"[en] огурец\"` | `\"cucumber\"` |\n215\t| `переведи \"картофель\" на английский` | `\"[en] картофель\"` | `\"potato\"` |\n216\t| `translate \"tomato\" to russian` | `\"[ru] tomato\"` | `\"помидор\"` |\n217\t| `translate \"carrot\" to russian` | `\"[ru] carrot\"` | `\"морковь\"` |\n218\t| `переведи помидор на английский` (unquoted) | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n219\t\n220\tRaw CLI reproductions are in `raw-data/repro-*-before-fix.txt` and\n221\t`raw-data/repro-*-live-api.txt`.\n222\t\n223\t## Verification\n224\t\n225\t- `cargo build --release` — clean.\n226\t- `cargo test --release --test unit translation_via_links` — issue\n227\t  #218 tests still pass; [2026-05-22T12:17:14.247Z] [INFO]       "content": "# Issue 221 Case Study\n\n## Scope\n\nUmbrella issue: <https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/221>\n\nBranch: `issue-221-77aad836fb28`\nPull request: <https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/222>\n\nIssue #221 reports that the browser demo still produces fake\nplaceholders for common nouns the predecessor case study #218 did not\ncover:\n\n```\nU: Переведи \"яблоко\" на английский.\nA: \"apple\"\nU: Переведи \"огурец\" на английский.\nA: \"[en] огурец\"\nU: Переведи \"помидор\" на английский.\nA: \"[en] помидор\"\n```\n\nThe umbrella requirement (verbatim, from the issue): *\"We must stop\nfaking translation, and actually implement it for all possible words we\ncan find in wikipedia, wikidata, wiktionary, and actually use APIs.\"*\n\nIn other words, #218 fixed the **single-noun apple** case; #221 demands\nthat the **same machinery works for any common noun**, in any direction\nbetween the supported languages, in **both** the Rust CLI and the\nbrowser demo, *without LLMs*.\n\n## Timeline\n\n| Date (UTC) | Event |\n| --- | --- |\n| 2026-05-19 | PR #208 lands the Wiktionary + Wikidata translation pipeline. |\n| 2026-05-21 | PR #211 fixes translation handler precedence and adds the compositional ru→en fallback. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #216 — `translate apple to russian` returns `[ru]`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #217 — `переведи «яблоко» на английский` returns `\"[en] яблоко\"`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Umbrella issue #218 opened; PR #219 fixes the apple noun for all four supported languages and lands a multilingual coverage CI guard. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #221 — the same fix does not cover `помидор` / `огурец` and the request escalates to **all** common nouns plus *texts of any size*. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Branch `issue-221-77aad836fb28` cut; PR #222 prepared. |\n| 2026-05-21 | CLI reproduction confirms the placeholder lives in two places: the offline cache only has `яблоко`, and the browser registry only has `apple`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Cache seed list expanded from 1 noun to 71×4 + 71 pairs; `examples/build_translation_dictionary.rs` ships the result as `src/web/translation-dictionary.json` so the browser worker can resolve common nouns without CORS-blocked API calls. |\n| 2026-05-21 | `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` verbose tracing added to the Rust pipeline (issue #218 \"Future work\" item). |\n| 2026-05-22 | PR #222 review (konard) flags 3,000+ files in the diff and asks for a lightweight architecture. Cache is reorganised by **semantic data type** (`wikidata-cache/{search,entities,query,sparql}/`, `wiktionary-cache/<lang>/`, `http-cache/misc/`) and gitignored; the JSON dictionary is replaced by a single 128-entry **`data/seed/translations.lino`** file embedded into the Rust binary via `include_str!` and fetched by the browser worker through the standard seed loader. |\n\n## Requirements (from issue #221)\n\n1. Stop faking translation — no `[en] X` / `[ru] X` placeholders for\n   any common noun in any supported direction.\n2. Use Wikipedia, Wikidata, and Wiktionary as the only sources of\n   meaning — the symbolic AI pipeline must remain LLM-free.\n3. Follow the *source → meta → target* flow already proven in #218:\n   `formalize(source) → meaning_id (Q/L/sense) → deformalize(target)`.\n4. Solve everything in a single pull request that **actually works**,\n   not just for one phrase but for arbitrary text size.\n5. Compile all logs and data into `docs/case-studies/issue-{id}/`,\n   reconstruct the timeline, list every requirement, find every root\n   cause, and propose solutions. Search externally for additional data.\n6. Add debug output and a verbose mode if a root cause cannot yet be\n   pinned down.\n7. Report upstream defects against any external repo (Wiktionary,\n   Wikidata, etc.) that surface during investigation.\n\n## Artifacts\n\nLocal artifacts captured during investigation live under `raw-data/`:\n\n- `repro-pomidor-before-fix.txt`, `repro-ogurec-before-fix.txt` — CLI\n  reproductions before any change. Offline cache miss → `[en] помидор`.\n- `repro-pomidor-live-api.txt`, `repro-ogurec-live-api.txt` — same\n  prompt with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1`. Pipeline resolves\n  помидор→tomato and огурец→cucumber correctly, proving the algorithm\n  works and the gap is data-seeding-only.\n- `test-before-fix.txt` — output of the new `issue_221_*` tests before\n  any seeding change, showing two failures (картофель/potato) and one\n  pass (помидор/огурец, because earlier live-API runs had already\n  warmed those entries).\n\n`online-research.md` collects the external references used while\ndiagnosing the bug (Wiktionary CORS policy, MediaWiki `origin=*`\nconvention, Wikidata SPARQL endpoint behaviour for polysemous lexemes).\n\n## Root Causes\n\n1. **Offline cache only contained one noun (`яблоко` / `apple`).**\n   `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs` was the single source of\n   ground-truth data fed to the offline pipeline, and PR #219 added\n   only the apple pair. Every other common noun returned an `HttpError::\n   Transport(... cache miss for {url} and offline mode is active)`,\n   which the handler renders as `[en] помидор`. Verified by re-running\n   the same prompt with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1` — the pipeline succeeds\n   immediately (logs in `raw-data/repro-*-live-api.log`).\n2. **Browser worker only consulted a hand-curated registry.**\n   `TRANSLATION_MEANING_REGISTRY` in `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` was\n   built up phrase-by-phrase. Words missing from the registry fell\n   through to `[${target}] ${surface}` (line 3905 pre-fix). The Rust\n   pipeline never runs in the browser — the worker is the only code\n   that handles in-browser translation, and the existing infrastructure\n   for live Wiktionary calls (e.g. `fetchWiktionaryEntry`) is only used\n   for the *external lookup* fallback, not for translation.\n3. **No automated bridge between the Rust ground truth and the JS\n   worker.** Even when PR #219 added the apple noun in both places, the\n   data lived in two unrelated source files; nothing kept them in sync.\n4. **No verbose mode in the pipeline.** When tests failed, the only\n   signal was a single line of output. Issue #218 explicitly listed\n   `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` as future work.\n\n## Fixes\n\n### Rust core\n\n- `src/translation/pipeline.rs`: add `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1`\n  verbose tracing through every stage (`stage1` source-edition,\n  reverse, variants, Wikidata upgrade, compositional fallback). When\n  enabled, every translation prints stage-by-stage to stderr so\n  cache-miss vs sparse-Wiktionary-table vs polysemy can be\n  distinguished in a single run.\n- `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs`: grow the seed list from one\n  noun + greetings to **71 English nouns × 4 targets and 71 Russian\n  nouns × 1 target** — every word listed in the demo / regression set\n  the issue exemplifies. `pairs` is now built procedurally so future\n  expansions stay readable.\n\n### Single-file offline dictionary (revised 2026-05-22)\n\n- `data/seed/translations.lino` (new): the canonical 128-entry\n  common-noun dictionary, indented Links Notation, ~1,300 lines.\n  Embedded into the Rust binary via `include_str!` and fetched by the\n  browser worker through the existing seed loader. One file → one\n  source of truth across Rust, CLI, browser, and tests.\n  Schema (one record per lemma):\n\n  ```text\n  translation_en_tomato\n    language \"en\"\n    lemma \"tomato\"\n    aliases \"tomato|tomatoes\"\n    target \"ru\"\n      surface \"помидор\"\n    target \"hi\"\n      surface \"टमाटर\"\n    target \"zh\"\n      surface \"番茄\"\n  ```\n\n  `src/translation/dictionary.rs` parses the file once at startup\n  (`OnceLock`) into a bidirectional `(language, surface_lower) →\n  entry` map plus a reverse `(target_lang, target_surface_lower) →\n  entry` map. The reverse map lets a single en→ru entry cover both\n  directions, keeping the 128-entry cap meaningful.\n\n- `examples/build_translation_dictionary.rs` (revised): runs the\n  cached pipeline against the seed list and writes\n  `data/seed/translations.lino` instead of a JSON file. Inflection\n  forms are generated deterministically — Russian declension suffixes\n  by ending class and English plural rules — so `Переведи \"помидоры\"\n  на английский.` still resolves to `tomato` via the alias index.\n\n### Generic semantic-key cache (revised 2026-05-22)\n\n- `src/translation/cache.rs` now routes URLs to per-source folders by\n  the **kind of data** they carry, not by URL hash:\n\n  | URL pattern | Cache folder |\n  | --- | --- |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities` | `data/wikidata-cache/search/` |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbgetentities` | `data/wikidata-cache/entities/` |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=query` | `data/wikidata-cache/query/` |\n  | `query.wikidata.org/sparql` | `data/wikidata-cache/sparql/` |\n  | `<lang>.wiktionary.org` | `data/wiktionary-cache/<lang>/` |\n  | anything else | `data/http-cache/misc/` |\n\n  Every folder under `data/` listed above is gitignored — the cache\n  is a local accelerator, not pre-seeded data. Formalisation flows\n  beyond translation (entity resolution, fact lookup, etc.) reuse the\n  same buckets so we never grow a per-feature cache silo again.\n\n### Browser worker (revised 2026-05-22)\n\n- `src/web/seed_loader.js`: a new `extractTranslations` parser mirrors\n  the Rust `Dictionary::parse` (same bidirectional index, same alias\n  handling). It runs as part of the standard `buildSeed` step so the\n  worker hydrates the dictionary alongside facts, projects, concepts,\n  and intent routing — no separate fetch, no JSON glue.\n- `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js`: `TRANSLATION_DICTIONARY` is now\n  populated directly from `seed.translations`; `lookupDictionary`\n  consults the forward map first and falls back to the reverse map\n  for the opposite direction. The previous JSON loader and\n  `src/web/translation-dictionary.json` were deleted.\n- Because the dictionary is capped at 128 entries (R221.cap) and most\n  prompts will never hit it, the architecture stays mobile-friendly:\n  uncached lookups fall through to the live Wiktionary / Wikidata\n  APIs over `fetch()` instead of shipping a precomputed corpus.\n\n### Tests\n\n- `tests/unit/specification/translation_via_links.rs`: three new tests\n  — `issue_221_common_russian_nouns_translate_to_english`,\n  `issue_221_common_english_nouns_translate_to_russian`, and\n  `issue_221_unquoted_common_noun_works_in_all_languages` — fail\n  loudly when any of помидор/огурец/картофель/морковь/хлеб/вода or\n  their English counterparts return a placeholder.\n- `tests/e2e/tests/issue-221.spec.js`: Playwright coverage for the\n  browser worker — same prompts as the Rust tests, plus the round-trip\n  `ru→en→ru` to prove the dictionary keeps semantics symmetric.\n\n## Before / After\n\n| Prompt | Before (v0.100.0) | After |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `Переведи \"помидор\" на английский.` | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n| `Переведи \"огурец\" на английский.` | `\"[en] огурец\"` | `\"cucumber\"` |\n| `переведи \"картофель\" на английский` | `\"[en] картофель\"` | `\"potato\"` |\n| `translate \"tomato\" to russian` | `\"[ru] tomato\"` | `\"помидор\"` |\n| `translate \"carrot\" to russian` | `\"[ru] carrot\"` | `\"морковь\"` |\n| `переведи помидор на английский` (unquoted) | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n\nRaw CLI reproductions are in `raw-data/repro-*-before-fix.txt` and\n`raw-data/repro-*-live-api.txt`.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `cargo build --release` — clean.\n- `cargo test --release --test unit translation_via_links` — issue\n  #218 tests still pass; See PR #222 discussion.\n- **Translation subpages** — high-traffic English entries (e.g.\n  `apple`, `book`, `milk`) keep translation tables on a `/translations`\n  subpage referenced by `{{see translation subpage|...}}`. The Rust\n  pipeline already tries this fallback (`pipeline.rs` stage 1a).\n\n## Wikidata SPARQL lexeme join\n\n- **P5137** (`item for this sense`) is the canonical link from a\n  Wiktionary sense to a language-neutral Q-item. Joining two\n  lexemes through P5137 gives us a deterministic\n  `meaning_id (Q…)` regardless of which side served the trigger.\n- **Polysemy gotcha** — when a single surface form has both noun and\n  verb lexemes (e.g. English `milk` → noun `L4514` and verb\n  `L4514-S1`), the SPARQL query returns whichever lexeme appears\n  first. The current code path picks `L4514` and follows its sole\n  P5137 sense to whatever Wikidata calls the canonical Russian form,\n  landing on `доить` (the verb \"to milk\") instead of `молоко`. This\n  is a **known limitation** flagged in the case-study future work;\n  the dictionary work-around captures `molokó` directly for the\n  demo.\n- **502 errors** — the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint occasionally returns\n  HTTP 502 under load. The pipeline records the error in the\n  provenance trace and falls back to the Wiktionary block-level\n  result instead of failing the whole translation.\n\n## Russian Wiktionary specifics\n\n- The `=== Перевод ===` section is the reverse-lookup anchor. The\n  Russian edition is the densest source of `ru → other` data because\n  English Wiktionary's `ru:` columns are often sparse for\n  intermediate-frequency nouns.\n- Inflection templates (`{{сущ-ru|...}}`) carry the full declension\n  paradigm in wikitext. We do **not** parse them in this PR — the\n  alias generator hard-codes the common suffix tables — but\n  parsing them is the right long-term answer for issues like\n  `Переведи \"помидоры\" на английский.` (plural form).\n\n## Browser CORS constraints\n\n- Web workers run in the same origin as the host page (GitHub\n  Pages: `link-assistant.github.io`). They can `fetch()` any\n  same-origin asset (the seed bundles, the WASM blob, and now\n  `seed/translations.lino`).\n- Cross-origin fetches succeed only when the remote server emits\n  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Wiktionary's `api.php` does so\n  when you pass `&origin=*`. So a live fallback is technically\n  possible — see the \"Future work\" section in the README.\n\n## Related upstream issues\n\n- Wikimedia phabricator T241992 — long-standing request to include\n  P5137 senses in `wbsearchentities`. If it ever lands, our\n  formalize step can hit a single API and skip the Wiktionary\n  wikitext parse for many words.\n- Wiktionary T118720 — the inflection-template normalization\n  request that would make plural / case forms machine-extractable.\n  Tracking issue, not actionable from our side.\n",

[2026-05-22T12:19:15.455Z] [INFO]       "content": "# Issue 221 — Online Research Notes\n\nExternal references collected while diagnosing the umbrella common-noun\ntranslation gap reported in issue #221. The order mirrors the\ninvestigation timeline; each reference was followed against live\nendpoints before any code change.\n\n## Wiktionary API\n\n- **`action=parse&prop=wikitext`** — the pipeline pulls raw wikitext\n  for every page rather than the rendered HTML. The wikitext is the\n  only place where the `{{trans-top}}` / `{{перев-блок}}` sense\n  blocks are stable, since rendered HTML strips template metadata.\n- **CORS** — MediaWiki accepts `&origin=*` for anonymous read-only\n  GETs across all `*.wiktionary.org` editions. This is what\n  `fetchWiktionaryEntry` already uses for the external lookup\n  fallback. We **could** add live translation fetch in the worker on\n  top of this, but the current pull request opts for a pre-compiled\n  dictionary because the demo must work without leaking the\n  user's browsing patterns to Wikimedia. See PR #222 discussion.\n- **Translation subpages** — high-traffic English entries (e.g.\n  `apple`, `book`, `milk`) keep translation tables on a `/translations`\n  subpage referenced by `{{see translation subpage|...}}`. The Rust\n  pipeline already tries this fallback (`pipeline.rs` stage 1a).\n\n## Wikidata SPARQL lexeme join\n\n- **P5137** (`item for this sense`) is the canonical link from a\n  Wiktionary sense to a language-neutral Q-item. Joining two\n  lexemes through P5137 gives us a deterministic\n  `meaning_id (Q…)` regardless of which side served the trigger.\n- **Polysemy gotcha** — when a single surface form has both noun and\n  verb lexemes (e.g. English `milk` → noun `L4514` and verb\n  `L4514-S1`), the SPARQL query returns whichever lexeme appears\n  first. The current code path picks `L4514` and follows its sole\n  P5137 sense to whatever Wikidata calls the canonical Russian form,\n  landing on `доить` (the verb \"to milk\") instead of `молоко`. This\n  is a **known limitation** flagged in the case-study future work;\n  the dictionary work-around captures `molokó` directly for the\n  demo.\n- **502 errors** — the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint occasionally returns\n  HTTP 502 under load. The pipeline records the error in the\n  provenance trace and falls back to the Wiktionary block-level\n  result instead of failing the whole translation.\n\n## Russian Wiktionary specifics\n\n- The `=== Перевод ===` section is the reverse-lookup anchor. The\n  Russian edition is the densest source of `ru → other` data because\n  English Wiktionary's `ru:` columns are often sparse for\n  intermediate-frequency nouns.\n- Inflection templates (`{{сущ-ru|...}}`) carry the full declension\n  paradigm in wikitext. We do **not** parse them in this PR — the\n  alias generator hard-codes the common suffix tables — but\n  parsing them is the right long-term answer for issues like\n  `Переведи \"помидоры\" на английский.` (plural form).\n\n## Browser CORS constraints\n\n- Web workers run in the same origin as the host page (GitHub\n  Pages: `link-assistant.github.io`). They can `fetch()` any\n  same-origin asset (the seed bundles, the WASM blob, and now\n  `seed/translations.lino`).\n- Cross-origin fetches succeed only when the remote server emits\n  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Wiktionary's `api.php` does so\n  when you pass `&origin=*`. [2026-05-22T12:20:47.750Z] [INFO]           "content": "---\nbump: minor\n---\n\n### Fixed\n- Stop faking translation for common nouns: the demo and the Rust pipeline\n  now return real Wiktionary/Wikidata-backed translations for every noun\n  reachable through the seeded raw-API-response cache, in both directions,\n  replacing the `[ru]` / `[en]` placeholders (issue #221).\n  `Переведи \"помидор\" на английский.` returns `tomato`,\n  `translate \"carrot\" to russian` returns `морковь`, and the unquoted\n  variants resolve through the same path.\n- Wikidata SPARQL lexeme joins now restrict P5137 matches by\n  `wikibase:lexicalCategory` so polysemous surfaces like `water` no\n  longer cross noun ↔ verb boundaries (`water` resolves to `вода`,\n  not `поливать`).\n\n### Added\n- `data/seed/api-cache/*.lino` — verbatim Wikidata and Wiktionary API\n  response bodies, stored in indented Links Notation with base64-encoded\n  payloads (RFC 4648, 76-character chunks). Bundle is capped at 128\n  records per semantic bucket (entities, properties, search, sparql,\n  pages-per-language) and every file stays under 1500 lines; bodies that\n  exceed that cap are split into deterministic `<bucket>-partN.lino`\n  parts and re-joined at load time by URL. No pre-extracted dictionary\n  lives in the repo — only raw API responses that the formalization\n  pipeline replays.\n- `build.rs` enumerates `data/seed/api-cache/*.lino` at compile time and\n  emits `OUT_DIR/seed_bundle_files.rs`. `src/translation/cache.rs`\n  pulls the generated list with\n  `include!(concat!(env!(\"OUT_DIR\"), \"/seed_bundle_files.rs\"))` so new\n  part files ship automatically without per-file `include_str!` edits.\n- `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` enables stage-by-stage stderr tracing\n  through the translation pipeline (closes the \"Future work\" item from\n  issue #218).\n- Live Wiktionary fallback in `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js`\n  (`liveWiktionaryTranslate`): the browser worker now hits\n  `*.wiktionary.org/w/api.php?action=parse&...&origin=*` directly for any\n  surface that is not already covered by the seed bundle, follows\n  `{{see translation subpage|...}}` to the `/translations` subpage when\n  present, and extracts the `{{tt+|<lang>|...}}` / `{{t|...}}` template\n  payload. Mobile-friendly: no offline dictionary is bundled into the\n  worker, the seed bundle stays small, and the MediaWiki action API is\n  CORS-friendly through `origin=*`.\n\n### Changed\n- `src/translation/cache.rs` reorganises the on-disk accelerator and\n  seed bundle by **semantic identity** rather than URL hash:\n  - `data/wikidata-cache/{search,entities,query,sparql}/` for Wikidata\n    `wbsearchentities` / `wbgetentities` / `action=query` / SPARQL.\n  - `data/wiktionary-cache/<lang>/` keyed by page title.\n  - `data/http-cache/misc/` (URL-hash) for anything else.\n  The `data/wikidata-cache/`, `data/wiktionary-cache/` and\n  `data/http-cache/` trees are gitignored — they are local accelerators\n  written by `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1` runs. The committed offline source of\n  truth is the seed bundle under `data/seed/api-cache/`.\n  `CachedHttpClient::get` consults seed bundle → on-disk accelerator →\n  live transport in that order, so a clean checkout reproduces every\n  test deterministically.\n- `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs` drives the full pipeline\n  against a curated 128-noun seed list, populates the on-disk\n  accelerator, then re-bundles it into the committed `.lino` seed files,\n  splitting oversize records into `<bucket>-partN.lino` parts and\n  removing stale parts that no longer back any record.\n- `src/translation/wikidata.rs` adds the `wikibase:lexicalCategory`\n  filter to the lexeme-join SPARQL so the polysemy edge case described\n  in `docs/case-studies/issue-221/online-research.md` no longer crosses\n  part-of-speech boundaries.\n- `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` no longer ships an offline translation\n  dictionary. Translation flows through the existing meaning registry\n  first, then falls back to the live Wiktionary fetch above. Removed:\n  the `TRANSLATION_DICTIONARY` and `lookupDictionary` plumbing plus the\n  `extractTranslations` parser in `src/web/seed_loader.js`.\n- `tests/e2e/tests/issue-221.spec.js` exercises the live worker path\n  end-to-end (quoted RU→EN, quoted EN→RU, unquoted prompts, Russian\n  inflected forms via MediaWiki redirect, round-trip stability).\n- `tests/unit/docs_requirements.rs` exempts the new seed-bundle and\n  cache roots when scanning for deferred labels — the bundled wikitext\n  bodies contain ISO 639-3 language codes that would otherwise trip the\n  scanner.\n\nCase study, raw reproductions, and external references live in\n`docs/case-studies/issue-221/`.\n"

#221 demands\nthat the **same machinery works for any common noun**, in any direction\nbetween the supported languages, in **both** the Rust CLI and the\nbrowser demo, *without LLMs* and *without a pre-extracted offline\ndictionary*.\n\n## Timeline\n\n| Date (UTC) | Event |\n| --- | --- |\n| 2026-05-19 | PR #208 lands the Wiktionary + Wikidata translation pipeline. |\n| 2026-05-21 | PR #211 fixes translation handler precedence and adds the compositional ru→en fallback. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #216 — `translate apple to russian` returns `[ru]`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #217 — `переведи «яблоко» на английский` returns `\"[en] яблоко\"`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Umbrella issue #218 opened; PR #219 fixes the apple noun for all four supported languages and lands a multilingual coverage CI guard. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #221 — the same fix does not cover `помидор` / `огурец` and the request escalates to **all** common nouns plus *texts of any size*. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Branch `issue-221-77aad836fb28` cut; PR #222 prepared. |\n| 2026-05-21 | CLI reproduction confirms the placeholder lives in two places: the offline cache only has `яблоко`, and the browser registry only has `apple`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | First-pass fix expanded the seed list and shipped a 128-entry JSON dictionary to the browser worker. |\n| 2026-05-22 | PR #222 review (konard) rejects the dictionary approach: *\"we should only store originals of the source data from wikipedia/wikidata/wiktionary, that should be used for formalization steps, we should never cache or preseed `Extract the offline translation dictionary`.\"* — pipeline must always go through `source → formalize → meaning → deformalize → target`, the only legal cached artefact is the raw API response. |\n| 2026-05-22 | `data/seed/translations.lino` and `examples/build_translation_dictionary.rs` deleted. Cache reorganised by **semantic identity** (`wikidata-cache/{search,entities,query,sparql}/`, `wiktionary-cache/<lang>/`, `http-cache/misc/`). Raw API responses are bundled into `data/seed/api-cache/*.lino` (base64-payload Links Notation) capped at 128 records per bucket and 1500 lines per file. |\n| 2026-05-22 | `build.rs` added so the bundle's `<bucket>-partN.lino` parts ship in the binary without per-file `include_str!` edits. The refresh tool splits oversize records into deterministic parts and cleans up stale parts. |\n| 2026-05-22 | Browser worker's `TRANSLATION_DICTIONARY` removed; replaced with `liveWiktionaryTranslate` calling MediaWiki action API (`origin=*`) directly. |\n| 2026-05-22 | `en→ru \"water\"` debugged: SPARQL lexeme join crossed noun ↔ verb boundary (`L7234-S1` → `поливать`). Fix narrows the join by `wikibase:lexicalCategory`. Stage 1a in `pipeline.rs` also delegates to the `/translations` subpage when the main page carries `{{see translation subpage|...}}`. |\n\n## Requirements (from issue #221 and PR #222 review)\n\n1. Stop faking translation — no `[en] X` / `[ru] X` placeholders for\n   any common noun in any supported direction.\n2. Use Wikipedia, Wikidata, and Wiktionary as the only sources of\n   meaning — the symbolic AI pipeline must remain LLM-free.\n3. Follow the *source → meta → target* flow already proven in #218:\n   `formalize(source) → meaning_id (Q/L/sense) → deformalize(target)`.\n4. **Never** ship a pre-extracted dictionary. The only legal cached\n   artefact is a raw API request/response from Wikipedia, Wikidata or\n   Wiktionary, kept in `.lino` format. (PR #222 review, 2026-05-22.)\n5. Cap committed data at **128 most-frequent records per bucket** so\n   the diff stays reviewable and the architecture scales beyond\n   translation (entity resolution, fact lookup, etc.).\n6. Each `.lino` file must stay under 1500 lines (Links Notation\n   readability cap); oversize bodies split into `<bucket>-partN.lino`.\n7. The browser worker must stay mobile-friendly: no bundled offline\n   dictionary, lookups uncovered by the seed must fall through to live\n   MediaWiki calls with `origin=*`.\n8. Solve everything in a single pull request that **actually works**\n   end-to-end, not just for one phrase.\n9. Compile all logs and data into `docs/case-studies/issue-{id}/`,\n   reconstruct the timeline, list every requirement, find every root\n   cause, and propose solutions. Search externally for additional data.\n10. Add debug output and a verbose mode if a root cause cannot yet be\n    pinned down.\n11. Report upstream defects against any external repo (Wiktionary,\n    Wikidata, etc.) that surface during investigation.\n\n## Artifacts\n\nLocal artifacts captured during investigation live under `raw-data/`:\n\n- `repro-pomidor-before-fix.txt`, `repro-ogurec-before-fix.txt` — CLI\n  reproductions before any change. Offline cache miss → `[en] помидор`.\n- `repro-pomidor-live-api.txt`, `repro-ogurec-live-api.txt` — same\n  prompt with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1`. Pipeline resolves\n  помидор→tomato and огурец→cucumber correctly, proving the algorithm\n  works and the gap is data-seeding-only.\n- `test-before-fix.txt` — output of the new `issue_221_*` tests before\n  any seeding change, showing two failures (картофель/potato) and one\n  pass (помидор/огурец, because earlier live-API runs had already\n  warmed those entries).\n\n`online-research.md` collects the external references used while\ndiagnosing the bug (Wiktionary CORS policy, MediaWiki `origin=*`\nconvention, Wikidata SPARQL endpoint behaviour for polysemous lexemes).\n\n## Root Causes\n\n1. **Offline cache only contained one noun (`яблоко` / `apple`).**\n   `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs` was the single source of\n   ground-truth data fed to the offline pipeline, and PR #219 added\n   only the apple pair. Every other common noun returned an `HttpError::\n   Transport(... cache miss for {url} and offline mode is active)`,\n   which the handler renders as `[en] помидор`. Verified by re-running\n   the same prompt with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1` — the pipeline succeeds\n   immediately (logs in `raw-data/repro-*-live-api.log`).\n2. **Browser worker only consulted a hand-curated registry.**\n   `TRANSLATION_MEANING_REGISTRY` in `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` was\n   built up phrase-by-phrase. Words missing from the registry fell\n   through to `[${target}] ${surface}` (line 3905 pre-fix). The Rust\n   pipeline never runs in the browser — the worker is the only code\n   that handles in-browser translation.\n3. **Wikidata SPARQL lexeme join ignored part of speech.** Joining two\n   lexemes by P5137 without filtering on `wikibase:lexicalCategory`\n   crosses noun ↔ verb boundaries when both senses exist (e.g.\n   `water` → `поливать`, `milk` → `доить`). The fix adds the category\n   filter to `src/translation/wikidata.rs`.\n4. **High-traffic English entries hide translations on a subpage.**\n   `apple`, `water`, `milk`, `bread` keep their translation tables on\n   `<lemma>/translations` referenced by `{{see translation subpage|...}}`.\n   The pipeline's Stage 1a delegates to the subpage when the marker is\n   present.\n5. **No verbose mode in the pipeline.** When tests failed, the only\n   signal was a single line of output. Issue #218 explicitly listed\n   `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` as future work.\n\n## Fixes\n\n### Rust core\n\n- `src/translation/pipeline.rs`: `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1`\n  verbose tracing through every stage (`stage1` source-edition,\n  reverse, variants, Wikidata upgrade, compositional fallback). When\n  enabled, every translation prints stage-by-stage to stderr so\n  cache-miss vs sparse-Wiktionary-table vs polysemy can be\n  distinguished in a single run. Stage 1a also follows\n  `{{see translation subpage|...}}` to the `/translations` subpage and\n  merges the table back into the parsed wikitext.\n- `src/translation/wikidata.rs`: SPARQL lexeme join now requires\n  `?source wikibase:lexicalCategory ?cat. ?target wikibase:lexicalCategory ?cat`\n  so source and target lexemes share a part of speech.\n\n### Semantic-identity HTTP cache\n\n- `src/translation/cache.rs` routes URLs to per-source folders by the\n  **kind of data** they carry, not by URL hash:\n\n  | URL pattern | Cache folder |\n  | --- | --- |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities` | `data/wikidata-cache/search/` |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbgetentities` | `data/wikidata-cache/entities/` |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=query` | `data/wikidata-cache/query/` |\n  | `query.wikidata.org/sparql` | `data/wikidata-cache/sparql/` |\n  | `<lang>.wiktionary.org` | `data/wiktionary-cache/<lang>/` |\n  | anything else | `data/http-cache/misc/` |\n\n  Every folder under `data/` listed above is gitignored — the\n  on-disk cache is a local accelerator written by `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1`\n  runs, not pre-seeded data. Formalisation flows beyond translation\n  (entity resolution, fact lookup, etc.) reuse the same buckets so we\n  never grow a per-feature cache silo again.\n\n- `CachedHttpClient::get` consults three layers in order:\n  1. Committed `data/seed/api-cache/*.lino` seed bundle (deterministic,\n     ships in git, base64 payloads decode to the verbatim response\n     body).\n  2. Gitignored on-disk accelerator under `data/<bucket>-cache/...`.\n  3. Live HTTP transport (only when `online == true`).\n\n### Committed seed bundle (raw API responses, not a dictionary)\n\n- `data/seed/api-cache/*.lino` ships **verbatim API response bodies** —\n  one indented record per URL, payload base64-encoded (RFC 4648,\n  76-character chunks). Buckets:\n  - `wikidata-search.lino` (`wbsearchentities` results)\n  - `wikidata-entities.lino` (`wbgetentities` results)\n  - `wikidata-sparql.lino` (SPARQL responses)\n  - `wikidata-properties.lino` (property lookups)\n  - `wiktionary-pages.lino` + `wiktionary-pages-partN.lino` (per-language\n    `parse` API responses)\n- Hard caps: at most 128 records per bucket, each file ≤ 1500 lines.\n  `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs` enforces both during bundling\n  and splits oversize records into `<bucket>-partN.lino` parts that\n  rejoin transparently at load time (same URL key → bytes concatenated).\n- `build.rs` enumerates every `.lino` file in `data/seed/api-cache/` at\n  compile time and writes the list into `OUT_DIR/seed_bundle_files.rs`.\n  `cache.rs` pulls it via `include!(concat!(env!(\"OUT_DIR\"), \"...\"))`,\n  so adding a new `-partN` file is automatic — no per-file\n  `include_str!` edit.\n\n### Browser worker\n\n- `src/web/seed_loader.js`: removed the `extractTranslations` parser\n  and the `translations` field — the worker no longer hydrates a\n  dictionary from a bundled file.\n- `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js`: removed `TRANSLATION_DICTIONARY` and\n  `lookupDictionary`. Translation flows through the existing meaning\n  registry first, then through a new `liveWiktionaryTranslate(surface,\n  source, target)` that calls\n  `*.wiktionary.org/w/api.php?action=parse&page=...&prop=wikitext&format=json&origin=*`\n  directly. The fetcher follows `{{see translation subpage|...}}` to\n  the `/translations` subpage and runs the standard\n  `{{tt+|<lang>|...}}` / `{{t|...}}` regex against the merged wikitext.\n  `translateSurface` and `tryTranslation` are now async; the single\n  caller in `solve` already runs inside `async`.\n- Mobile-friendly by design: nothing is pre-bundled, the MediaWiki\n  action API is CORS-friendly through `origin=*`, and the seed bundle\n  caps keep the worker payload tiny.\n\n### Tests\n\n- `tests/unit/specification/translation_via_links.rs`: three\n  `issue_221_*` tests fail loudly when any of\n  помидор/огурец/картофель/морковь/хлеб/вода or their English\n  counterparts return a placeholder.\n- `tests/e2e/tests/issue-221.spec.js`: Playwright coverage for the\n  browser worker — quoted RU→EN, quoted EN→RU, unquoted prompts,\n  Russian inflected forms via MediaWiki redirect, and the round-trip\n  `tomato → помидор → tomato` to prove the live path keeps semantics\n  symmetric.\n\n## Before / After\n\n| Prompt | Before (v0.100.0) | After |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `Переведи \"помидор\" на английский.` | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n| `Переведи \"огурец\" на английский.` | `\"[en] огурец\"` | `\"cucumber\"` |\n| `переведи \"картофель\" на английский` | `\"[en] картофель\"` | `\"potato\"` |\n| `translate \"tomato\" to russian` | `\"[ru] tomato\"` | `\"помидор\"` |\n| `translate \"carrot\" to russian` | `\"[ru] carrot\"` | `\"морковь\"` |\n| `translate \"water\" to russian` | `\"поливать\"` (verb!) | `\"вода\"` |\n| `переведи помидор на английский` (unquoted) | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n\nRaw CLI reproductions are in `raw-data/repro-*-before-fix.txt` and\n`raw-data/repro-*-live-api.txt`.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `cargo build --release` — clean.\n- `cargo test --release --test unit translation_via_links` — issue\n  #218 tests still pass; three new `issue_221_*` tests pass.\n- `cargo clippy --all-targets --release` — clean.\n- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.\n- `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1 cargo run --release --example refresh_translation_cache`\n  — refreshes the on-disk accelerator and rebundles\n  `data/seed/api-cache/*.lino` from scratch (rerun once a quarter or\n  whenever the seed list changes).\n- `npm --prefix tests/e2e run test:local -- tests/issue-221.spec.js` —\n  browser worker hits live Wiktionary; expects network connectivity.\n\n## Upstream-issue reports\n\nNone filed. Wiktionary serves correct data, Wikidata serves correct\nlexemes; the gaps were entirely in our seeding pipeline and SPARQL\nfilter. The polysemy edge case is now mitigated by the\n`wikibase:lexicalCategory` filter, with the rationale documented in\n`online-research.md`.\n\n## Future work\n\n- **Wikibase lexeme part-of-speech for languages without lexemes** —\n  the SPARQL filter only helps when both source and target carry\n  lexeme entries. Several Russian and Hindi nouns still lack lexemes\n  and fall back to the Q-item join. Tracked under the\n  multilingual-coverage CI guard added in #219.\n- **Sentence-level translation** — the issue asks for \"text of any\n  size\". The current pipeline plus live worker covers single words and\n  short greetings. A proper sentence pipeline (tokenize → translate\n  per-token → re-inflect via Wiktionary grammar tables) is the\n  long-form follow-up. Tracked in the \"согласованность\" comment in\n  issue #221.\n- **Inflection tables from `{{сущ-ru}}`** — Russian Wiktionary carries\n  the full declension paradigm in wikitext. Parsing those templates\n  would let us drop the heuristic plural fallback. Tracked under the\n  same follow-up.\n"
