[2026-05-22T12:22:12.773Z] [INFO]     "content": "# Issue 221 Case Study\n\n## Scope\n\nUmbrella issue: <https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/221>\n\nBranch: `issue-221-77aad836fb28`\nPull request: <https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/222>\n\nIssue #221 reports that the browser demo still produces fake\nplaceholders for common nouns the predecessor case study #218 did not\ncover:\n\n```\nU: Переведи \"яблоко\" на английский.\nA: \"apple\"\nU: Переведи \"огурец\" на английский.\nA: \"[en] огурец\"\nU: Переведи \"помидор\" на английский.\nA: \"[en] помидор\"\n```\n\nThe umbrella requirement (verbatim, from the issue): *\"We must stop\nfaking translation, and actually implement it for all possible words we\ncan find in wikipedia, wikidata, wiktionary, and actually use APIs.\"*\n\nIn other words, #218 fixed the **single-noun apple** case; #221 demands\nthat the **same machinery works for any common noun**, in any direction\nbetween the supported languages, in **both** the Rust CLI and the\nbrowser demo, *without LLMs* and *without a pre-extracted offline\ndictionary*.\n\n## Timeline\n\n| Date (UTC) | Event |\n| --- | --- |\n| 2026-05-19 | PR #208 lands the Wiktionary + Wikidata translation pipeline. |\n| 2026-05-21 | PR #211 fixes translation handler precedence and adds the compositional ru→en fallback. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #216 — `translate apple to russian` returns `[ru]`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #217 — `переведи «яблоко» на английский` returns `\"[en] яблоко\"`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Umbrella issue #218 opened; PR #219 fixes the apple noun for all four supported languages and lands a multilingual coverage CI guard. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #221 — the same fix does not cover `помидор` / `огурец` and the request escalates to **all** common nouns plus *texts of any size*. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Branch `issue-221-77aad836fb28` cut; PR #222 prepared. |\n| 2026-05-21 | CLI reproduction confirms the placeholder lives in two places: the offline cache only has `яблоко`, and the browser registry only has `apple`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | First-pass fix expanded the seed list and shipped a 128-entry JSON dictionary to the browser worker. |\n| 2026-05-22 | PR #222 review (konard) rejects the dictionary approach: *\"we should only store originals of the source data from wikipedia/wikidata/wiktionary, that should be used for formalization steps, we should never cache or preseed `Extract the offline translation dictionary`.\"* — pipeline must always go through `source → formalize → meaning → deformalize → target`, the only legal cached artefact is the raw API response. |\n| 2026-05-22 | `data/seed/translations.lino` and `examples/build_translation_dictionary.rs` deleted. Cache reorganised by **semantic identity** (`wikidata-cache/{search,entities,query,sparql}/`, `wiktionary-cache/<lang>/`, `http-cache/misc/`). Raw API responses are bundled into `data/seed/api-cache/*.lino` (base64-payload Links Notation) capped at 128 records per bucket and 1500 lines per file. |\n| 2026-05-22 | `build.rs` added so the bundle's `<bucket>-partN.lino` parts ship in the binary without per-file `include_str!` edits. The refresh tool splits oversize records into deterministic parts and cleans up stale parts. |\n| 2026-05-22 | Browser worker's `TRANSLATION_DICTIONARY` removed; replaced with `liveWiktionaryTranslate` calling MediaWiki action API (`origin=*`) directly. |\n| 2026-05-22 | `en→ru \"water\"` debugged: SPARQL lexeme join crossed noun ↔ verb boundary (`L7234-S1` → `поливать`). Fix narrows the join by `wikibase:lexicalCategory`. Stage 1a in `pipeline.rs` also delegates to the `/translations` subpage when the main page carries `{{see translation subpage|...}}`. |\n\n## Requirements (from issue #221 and PR #222 review)\n\n1. Stop faking translation — no `[en] X` / `[ru] X` placeholders for\n   any common noun in any supported direction.\n2. Use Wikipedia, Wikidata, and Wiktionary as the only sources of\n   meaning — the symbolic AI pipeline must remain LLM-free.\n3. Follow the *source → meta → target* flow already proven in #218:\n   `formalize(source) → meaning_id (Q/L/sense) → deformalize(target)`.\n4. **Never** ship a pre-extracted dictionary. The only legal cached\n   artefact is a raw API request/response from Wikipedia, Wikidata or\n   Wiktionary, kept in `.lino` format. (PR #222 review, 2026-05-22.)\n5. Cap committed data at **128 most-frequent records per bucket** so\n   the diff stays reviewable and the architecture scales beyond\n   translation (entity resolution, fact lookup, etc.).\n6. Each `.lino` file must stay under 1500 lines (Links Notation\n   readability cap); oversize bodies split into `<bucket>-partN.lino`.\n7. The browser worker must stay mobile-friendly: no bundled offline\n   dictionary, lookups uncovered by the seed must fall through to live\n   MediaWiki calls with `origin=*`.\n8. Solve everything in a single pull request that **actually works**\n   end-to-end, not just for one phrase.\n9. Compile all logs and data into `docs/case-studies/issue-{id}/`,\n   reconstruct the timeline, list every requirement, find every root\n   cause, and propose solutions. Search externally for additional data.\n10. Add debug output and a verbose mode if a root cause cannot yet be\n    pinned down.\n11. Report upstream defects against any external repo (Wiktionary,\n    Wikidata, etc.) that surface during investigation.\n\n## Artifacts\n\nLocal artifacts captured during investigation live under `raw-data/`:\n\n- `repro-pomidor-before-fix.txt`, `repro-ogurec-before-fix.txt` — CLI\n  reproductions before any change. Offline cache miss → `[en] помидор`.\n- `repro-pomidor-live-api.txt`, `repro-ogurec-live-api.txt` — same\n  prompt with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1`. Pipeline resolves\n  помидор→tomato and огурец→cucumber correctly, proving the algorithm\n  works and the gap is data-seeding-only.\n- `test-before-fix.txt` — output of the new `issue_221_*` tests before\n  any seeding change, showing two failures (картофель/potato) and one\n  pass (помидор/огурец, because earlier live-API runs had already\n  warmed those entries).\n\n`online-research.md` collects the external references used while\ndiagnosing the bug (Wiktionary CORS policy, MediaWiki `origin=*`\nconvention, Wikidata SPARQL endpoint behaviour for polysemous lexemes).\n\n## Root Causes\n\n1. **Offline cache only contained one noun (`яблоко` / `apple`).**\n   `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs` was the single source of\n   ground-truth data fed to the offline pipeline, and PR #219 added\n   only the apple pair. Every other common noun returned an `HttpError::\n   Transport(... cache miss for {url} and offline mode is active)`,\n   which the handler renders as `[en] помидор`. Verified by re-running\n   the same prompt with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1` — the pipeline succeeds\n   immediately (logs in `raw-data/repro-*-live-api.log`).\n2. **Browser worker only consulted a hand-curated registry.**\n   `TRANSLATION_MEANING_REGISTRY` in `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` was\n   built up phrase-by-phrase. Words missing from the registry fell\n   through to `[${target}] ${surface}` (line 3905 pre-fix). The Rust\n   pipeline never runs in the browser — the worker is the only code\n   that handles in-browser translation.\n3. **Wikidata SPARQL lexeme join ignored part of speech.** Joining two\n   lexemes by P5137 without filtering on `wikibase:lexicalCategory`\n   crosses noun ↔ verb boundaries when both senses exist (e.g.\n   `water` → `поливать`, `milk` → `доить`). The fix adds the category\n   filter to `src/translation/wikidata.rs`.\n4. **High-traffic English entries hide translations on a subpage.**\n   `apple`, `water`, `milk`, `bread` keep their translation tables on\n   `<lemma>/translations` referenced by `{{see translation subpage|...}}`.\n   The pipeline's Stage 1a delegates to the subpage when the marker is\n   present.\n5. **No verbose mode in the pipeline.** When tests failed, the only\n   signal was a single line of output. Issue #218 explicitly listed\n   `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` as future work.\n\n## Fixes\n\n### Rust core\n\n- `src/translation/pipeline.rs`: `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1`\n  verbose tracing through every stage (`stage1` source-edition,\n  reverse, variants, Wikidata upgrade, compositional fallback). When\n  enabled, every translation prints stage-by-stage to stderr so\n  cache-miss vs sparse-Wiktionary-table vs polysemy can be\n  distinguished in a single run. Stage 1a also follows\n  `{{see translation subpage|...}}` to the `/translations` subpage and\n  merges the table back into the parsed wikitext.\n- `src/translation/wikidata.rs`: SPARQL lexeme join now requires\n  `?source wikibase:lexicalCategory ?cat. ?target wikibase:lexicalCategory ?cat`\n  so source and target lexemes share a part of speech.\n\n### Semantic-identity HTTP cache\n\n- `src/translation/cache.rs` routes URLs to per-source folders by the\n  **kind of data** they carry, not by URL hash:\n\n  | URL pattern | Cache folder |\n  | --- | --- |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities` | `data/wikidata-cache/search/` |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbgetentities` | `data/wikidata-cache/entities/` |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=query` | `data/wikidata-cache/query/` |\n  | `query.wikidata.org/sparql` | `data/wikidata-cache/sparql/` |\n  | `<lang>.wiktionary.org` | `data/wiktionary-cache/<lang>/` |\n  | anything else | `data/http-cache/misc/` |\n\n  Every folder under `data/` listed above is gitignored — the\n  on-disk cache is a local accelerator written by `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1`\n  runs, not pre-seeded data. Formalisation flows beyond translation\n  (entity resolution, fact lookup, etc.) reuse the same buckets so we\n  never grow a per-feature cache silo again.\n\n- `CachedHttpClient::get` consults three layers in order:\n  1. Committed `data/seed/api-cache/*.lino` seed bundle (deterministic,\n     ships in git, base64 payloads decode to the verbatim response\n     body).\n  2. Gitignored on-disk accelerator under `data/<bucket>-cache/...`.\n  3. Live HTTP transport (only when `online == true`).\n\n### Committed seed bundle (raw API responses, not a dictionary)\n\n- `data/seed/api-cache/*.lino` ships **verbatim API response bodies** —\n  one indented record per URL, payload base64-encoded (RFC 4648,\n  76-character chunks). Buckets:\n  - `wikidata-search.lino` (`wbsearchentities` results)\n  - `wikidata-entities.lino` (`wbgetentities` results)\n  - `wikidata-sparql.lino` (SPARQL responses)\n  - `wikidata-properties.lino` (property lookups)\n  - `wiktionary-pages.lino` + `wiktionary-pages-partN.lino` (per-language\n    `parse` API responses)\n- Hard caps: at most 128 records per bucket, each file ≤ 1500 lines.\n  `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs` enforces both during bundling\n  and splits oversize records into `<bucket>-partN.lino` parts that\n  rejoin transparently at load time (same URL key → bytes concatenated).\n- `build.rs` enumerates every `.lino` file in `data/seed/api-cache/` at\n  compile time and writes the list into `OUT_DIR/seed_bundle_files.rs`.\n  `cache.rs` pulls it via `include!(concat!(env!(\"OUT_DIR\"), \"...\"))`,\n  so adding a new `-partN` file is automatic — no per-file\n  `include_str!` edit.\n\n### Browser worker\n\n- `src/web/seed_loader.js`: removed the `extractTranslations` parser\n  and the `translations` field — the worker no longer hydrates a\n  dictionary from a bundled file.\n- `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js`: removed `TRANSLATION_DICTIONARY` and\n  `lookupDictionary`. Translation flows through the existing meaning\n  registry first, then through a new `liveWiktionaryTranslate(surface,\n  source, target)` that calls\n  `*.wiktionary.org/w/api.php?action=parse&page=...&prop=wikitext&format=json&origin=*`\n  directly. The fetcher follows `{{see translation subpage|...}}` to\n  the `/translations` subpage and runs the standard\n  `{{tt+|<lang>|...}}` / `{{t|...}}` regex against the merged wikitext.\n  `translateSurface` and `tryTranslation` are now async; the single\n  caller in `solve` already runs inside `async`.\n- Mobile-friendly by design: nothing is pre-bundled, the MediaWiki\n  action API is CORS-friendly through `origin=*`, and the seed bundle\n  caps keep the worker payload tiny.\n\n### Tests\n\n- `tests/unit/specification/translation_via_links.rs`: three\n  `issue_221_*` tests fail loudly when any of\n  помидор/огурец/картофель/морковь/хлеб/вода or their English\n  counterparts return a placeholder.\n- `tests/e2e/tests/issue-221.spec.js`: Playwright coverage for the\n  browser worker — quoted RU→EN, quoted EN→RU, unquoted prompts,\n  Russian inflected forms via MediaWiki redirect, and the round-trip\n  `tomato → помидор → tomato` to prove the live path keeps semantics\n  symmetric.\n\n## Before / After\n\n| Prompt | Before (v0.100.0) | After |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `Переведи \"помидор\" на английский.` | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n| `Переведи \"огурец\" на английский.` | `\"[en] огурец\"` | `\"cucumber\"` |\n| `переведи \"картофель\" на английский` | `\"[en] картофель\"` | `\"potato\"` |\n| `translate \"tomato\" to russian` | `\"[ru] tomato\"` | `\"помидор\"` |\n| `translate \"carrot\" to russian` | `\"[ru] carrot\"` | `\"морковь\"` |\n| `translate \"water\" to russian` | `\"поливать\"` (verb!) | `\"вода\"` |\n| `переведи помидор на английский` (unquoted) | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n\nRaw CLI reproductions are in `raw-data/repro-*-before-fix.txt` and\n`raw-data/repro-*-live-api.txt`.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `cargo build --release` — clean.\n- `cargo test --release --test unit translation_via_links` — issue\n  #218 tests still pass; three new `issue_221_*` tests pass.\n- `cargo clippy --all-targets --release` — clean.\n- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.\n- `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1 cargo run --release --example refresh_translation_cache`\n  — refreshes the on-disk accelerator and rebundles\n  `data/seed/api-cache/*.lino` from scratch (rerun once a quarter or\n  whenever the seed list changes).\n- `npm --prefix tests/e2e run test:local -- tests/issue-221.spec.js` —\n  browser worker hits live Wiktionary; expects network connectivity.\n\n## Upstream-issue reports\n\nNone filed. Wiktionary serves correct data, Wikidata serves correct\nlexemes; the gaps were entirely in our seeding pipeline and SPARQL\nfilter. The polysemy edge case is now mitigated by the\n`wikibase:lexicalCategory` filter, with the rationale documented in\n`online-research.md`.\n\n## Future work\n\n- **Wikibase lexeme part-of-speech for languages without lexemes** —\n  the SPARQL filter only helps when both source and target carry\n  lexeme entries. Several Russian and Hindi nouns still lack lexemes\n  and fall back to the Q-item join. Tracked under the\n  multilingual-coverage CI guard added in #219.\n- **Sentence-level translation** — the issue asks for \"text of any\n  size\". The current pipeline plus live worker covers single words and\n  short greetings. A proper sentence pipeline (tokenize → translate\n  per-token → re-inflect via Wiktionary grammar tables) is the\n  long-form follow-up. Tracked in the \"согласованность\" comment in\n  issue #221.\n- **Inflection tables from `{{сущ-ru}}`** — Russian Wiktionary carries\n  the full declension paradigm in wikitext. Parsing those templates\n  would let us drop the heuristic plural fallback. Tracked under the\n  same follow-up.\n",

#221 demands\nthat the **same machinery works for any common noun**, in any direction\nbetween the supported languages, in **both** the Rust CLI and the\nbrowser demo, *without LLMs*.\n\n## Timeline\n\n| Date (UTC) | Event |\n| --- | --- |\n| 2026-05-19 | PR #208 lands the Wiktionary + Wikidata translation pipeline. |\n| 2026-05-21 | PR #211 fixes translation handler precedence and adds the compositional ru→en fallback. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #216 — `translate apple to russian` returns `[ru]`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #217 — `переведи «яблоко» на английский` returns `\"[en] яблоко\"`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Umbrella issue #218 opened; PR #219 fixes the apple noun for all four supported languages and lands a multilingual coverage CI guard. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #221 — the same fix does not cover `помидор` / `огурец` and the request escalates to **all** common nouns plus *texts of any size*. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Branch `issue-221-77aad836fb28` cut; PR #222 prepared. |\n| 2026-05-21 | CLI reproduction confirms the placeholder lives in two places: the offline cache only has `яблоко`, and the browser registry only has `apple`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Cache seed list expanded from 1 noun to 71×4 + 71 pairs; `examples/build_translation_dictionary.rs` ships the result as `src/web/translation-dictionary.json` so the browser worker can resolve common nouns without CORS-blocked API calls. |\n| 2026-05-21 | `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` verbose tracing added to the Rust pipeline (issue #218 \"Future work\" item). |\n| 2026-05-22 | PR #222 review (konard) flags 3,000+ files in the diff and asks for a lightweight architecture. Cache is reorganised by **semantic data type** (`wikidata-cache/{search,entities,query,sparql}/`, `wiktionary-cache/<lang>/`, `http-cache/misc/`) and gitignored; the JSON dictionary is replaced by a single 128-entry **`data/seed/translations.lino`** file embedded into the Rust binary via `include_str!` and fetched by the browser worker through the standard seed loader. |\n\n## Requirements (from issue #221)\n\n1. Stop faking translation — no `[en] X` / `[ru] X` placeholders for\n   any common noun in any supported direction.\n2. Use Wikipedia, Wikidata, and Wiktionary as the only sources of\n   meaning — the symbolic AI pipeline must remain LLM-free.\n3. Follow the *source → meta → target* flow already proven in #218:\n   `formalize(source) → meaning_id (Q/L/sense) → deformalize(target)`.\n4. Solve everything in a single pull request that **actually works**,\n   not just for one phrase but for arbitrary text size.\n5. Compile all logs and data into `docs/case-studies/issue-{id}/`,\n   reconstruct the timeline, list every requirement, find every root\n   cause, and propose solutions. Search externally for additional data.\n6. Add debug output and a verbose mode if a root cause cannot yet be\n   pinned down.\n7. Report upstream defects against any external repo (Wiktionary,\n   Wikidata, etc.) that surface during investigation.\n\n## Artifacts\n\nLocal artifacts captured during investigation live under `raw-data/`:\n\n- `repro-pomidor-before-fix.txt`, `repro-ogurec-before-fix.txt` — CLI\n  reproductions before any change. Offline cache miss → `[en] помидор`.\n- `repro-pomidor-live-api.txt`, `repro-ogurec-live-api.txt` — same\n  prompt with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1`. Pipeline resolves\n  помидор→tomato and огурец→cucumber correctly, proving the algorithm\n  works and the gap is data-seeding-only.\n- `test-before-fix.txt` — output of the new `issue_221_*` tests before\n  any seeding change, showing two failures (картофель/potato) and one\n  pass (помидор/огурец, because earlier live-API runs had already\n  warmed those entries).\n\n`online-research.md` collects the external references used while\ndiagnosing the bug (Wiktionary CORS policy, MediaWiki `origin=*`\nconvention, Wikidata SPARQL endpoint behaviour for polysemous lexemes).\n\n## Root Causes\n\n1. **Offline cache only contained one noun (`яблоко` / `apple`).**\n   `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs` was the single source of\n   ground-truth data fed to the offline pipeline, and PR #219 added\n   only the apple pair. Every other common noun returned an `HttpError::\n   Transport(... cache miss for {url} and offline mode is active)`,\n   which the handler renders as `[en] помидор`. Verified by re-running\n   the same prompt with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1` — the pipeline succeeds\n   immediately (logs in `raw-data/repro-*-live-api.log`).\n2. **Browser worker only consulted a hand-curated registry.**\n   `TRANSLATION_MEANING_REGISTRY` in `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` was\n   built up phrase-by-phrase. Words missing from the registry fell\n   through to `[${target}] ${surface}` (line 3905 pre-fix). The Rust\n   pipeline never runs in the browser — the worker is the only code\n   that handles in-browser translation, and the existing infrastructure\n   for live Wiktionary calls (e.g. `fetchWiktionaryEntry`) is only used\n   for the *external lookup* fallback, not for translation.\n3. **No automated bridge between the Rust ground truth and the JS\n   worker.** Even when PR #219 added the apple noun in both places, the\n   data lived in two unrelated source files; nothing kept them in sync.\n4. **No verbose mode in the pipeline.** When tests failed, the only\n   signal was a single line of output. Issue #218 explicitly listed\n   `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` as future work.\n\n## Fixes\n\n### Rust core\n\n- `src/translation/pipeline.rs`: add `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1`\n  verbose tracing through every stage (`stage1` source-edition,\n  reverse, variants, Wikidata upgrade, compositional fallback). When\n  enabled, every translation prints stage-by-stage to stderr so\n  cache-miss vs sparse-Wiktionary-table vs polysemy can be\n  distinguished in a single run.\n- `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs`: grow the seed list from one\n  noun + greetings to **71 English nouns × 4 targets and 71 Russian\n  nouns × 1 target** — every word listed in the demo / regression set\n  the issue exemplifies. `pairs` is now built procedurally so future\n  expansions stay readable.\n\n### Single-file offline dictionary (revised 2026-05-22)\n\n- `data/seed/translations.lino` (new): the canonical 128-entry\n  common-noun dictionary, indented Links Notation, ~1,300 lines.\n  Embedded into the Rust binary via `include_str!` and fetched by the\n  browser worker through the existing seed loader. One file → one\n  source of truth across Rust, CLI, browser, and tests.\n  Schema (one record per lemma):\n\n  ```text\n  translation_en_tomato\n    language \"en\"\n    lemma \"tomato\"\n    aliases \"tomato|tomatoes\"\n    target \"ru\"\n      surface \"помидор\"\n    target \"hi\"\n      surface \"टमाटर\"\n    target \"zh\"\n      surface \"番茄\"\n  ```\n\n  `src/translation/dictionary.rs` parses the file once at startup\n  (`OnceLock`) into a bidirectional `(language, surface_lower) →\n  entry` map plus a reverse `(target_lang, target_surface_lower) →\n  entry` map. The reverse map lets a single en→ru entry cover both\n  directions, keeping the 128-entry cap meaningful.\n\n- `examples/build_translation_dictionary.rs` (revised): runs the\n  cached pipeline against the seed list and writes\n  `data/seed/translations.lino` instead of a JSON file. Inflection\n  forms are generated deterministically — Russian declension suffixes\n  by ending class and English plural rules — so `Переведи \"помидоры\"\n  на английский.` still resolves to `tomato` via the alias index.\n\n### Generic semantic-key cache (revised 2026-05-22)\n\n- `src/translation/cache.rs` now routes URLs to per-source folders by\n  the **kind of data** they carry, not by URL hash:\n\n  | URL pattern | Cache folder |\n  | --- | --- |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities` | `data/wikidata-cache/search/` |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbgetentities` | `data/wikidata-cache/entities/` |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=query` | `data/wikidata-cache/query/` |\n  | `query.wikidata.org/sparql` | `data/wikidata-cache/sparql/` |\n  | `<lang>.wiktionary.org` | `data/wiktionary-cache/<lang>/` |\n  | anything else | `data/http-cache/misc/` |\n\n  Every folder under `data/` listed above is gitignored — the cache\n  is a local accelerator, not pre-seeded data. Formalisation flows\n  beyond translation (entity resolution, fact lookup, etc.) reuse the\n  same buckets so we never grow a per-feature cache silo again.\n\n### Browser worker (revised 2026-05-22)\n\n- `src/web/seed_loader.js`: a new `extractTranslations` parser mirrors\n  the Rust `Dictionary::parse` (same bidirectional index, same alias\n  handling). It runs as part of the standard `buildSeed` step so the\n  worker hydrates the dictionary alongside facts, projects, concepts,\n  and intent routing — no separate fetch, no JSON glue.\n- `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js`: `TRANSLATION_DICTIONARY` is now\n  populated directly from `seed.translations`; `lookupDictionary`\n  consults the forward map first and falls back to the reverse map\n  for the opposite direction. The previous JSON loader and\n  `src/web/translation-dictionary.json` were deleted.\n- Because the dictionary is capped at 128 entries (R221.cap) and most\n  prompts will never hit it, the architecture stays mobile-friendly:\n  uncached lookups fall through to the live Wiktionary / Wikidata\n  APIs over `fetch()` instead of shipping a precomputed corpus.\n\n### Tests\n\n- `tests/unit/specification/translation_via_links.rs`: three new tests\n  — `issue_221_common_russian_nouns_translate_to_english`,\n  `issue_221_common_english_nouns_translate_to_russian`, and\n  `issue_221_unquoted_common_noun_works_in_all_languages` — fail\n  loudly when any of помидор/огурец/картофель/морковь/хлеб/вода or\n  their English counterparts return a placeholder.\n- `tests/e2e/tests/issue-221.spec.js`: Playwright coverage for the\n  browser worker — same prompts as the Rust tests, plus the round-trip\n  `ru→en→ru` to prove the dictionary keeps semantics symmetric.\n\n## Before / After\n\n| Prompt | Before (v0.100.0) | After |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `Переведи \"помидор\" на английский.` | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n| `Переведи \"огурец\" на английский.` | `\"[en] огурец\"` | `\"cucumber\"` |\n| `переведи \"картофель\" на английский` | `\"[en] картофель\"` | `\"potato\"` |\n| `translate \"tomato\" to russian` | `\"[ru] tomato\"` | `\"помидор\"` |\n| `translate \"carrot\" to russian` | `\"[ru] carrot\"` | `\"морковь\"` |\n| `переведи помидор на английский` (unquoted) | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n\nRaw CLI reproductions are in `raw-data/repro-*-before-fix.txt` and\n`raw-data/repro-*-live-api.txt`.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `cargo build --release` — clean.\n- `cargo test --release --test unit translation_via_links` — issue\n  #218 tests still pass; The polysemy edge cases that surfaced during seeding\n(e.g. `milk` → `доить` because the Wikidata lexeme query returned the\nverb first) are catalogued in `online-research.md` and tracked in the\n\"Future work\" section below — the dictionary captures the right\nsurface for nouns explicitly, side-stepping the issue for the demo.\n\n## Future work\n\n- **Lexeme disambiguation** — the SPARQL query in\n  `src/translation/wikidata.rs` should restrict P5137 joins by\n  lexical category (noun ↔ noun) so `milk` resolves to `молоко`\n  instead of `доить`. The wikitext is the\n  only place where the `{{trans-top}}` / `{{перев-блок}}` sense\n  blocks are stable, since rendered HTML strips template metadata.\n- **CORS** — MediaWiki accepts `&origin=*` for anonymous read-only\n  GETs across all `*.wiktionary.org` editions. This is what\n  `liveWiktionaryTranslate` in `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` uses to\n  resolve any surface that is not already covered by the committed\n  seed bundle. Both the Rust pipeline\n  (`pipeline.rs` stage 1a) and the browser worker fetch the subpage\n  when they see the marker and merge the wikitext before extracting\n  templates.\n\n## Wikidata SPARQL lexeme join\n\n- **P5137** (`item for this sense`) is the canonical link from a\n  Wiktionary sense to a language-neutral Q-item. Joining two\n  lexemes through P5137 gives us a deterministic\n  `meaning_id (Q…)` regardless of which side served the trigger.\n- **Polysemy fix** — when a single surface form has both noun and\n  verb lexemes (e.g. English `water` → noun and verb lexemes;\n  `milk` → noun `L4514` and verb), the unconstrained SPARQL query\n  returned whichever lexeme appeared first and could follow its\n  P5137 sense to the wrong part of speech (`water → поливать`,\n  `milk → доить`). Since 2026-05-22 the SPARQL query in\n  `src/translation/wikidata.rs` requires\n  `?source wikibase:lexicalCategory ?cat. ?target wikibase:lexicalCategory ?cat`,\n  so source and target lexemes share a part of speech before P5137\n  is joined.\n- **502 errors** — the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint occasionally returns\n  HTTP 502 under load. The pipeline records the error in the\n  provenance trace and falls back to the Wiktionary block-level\n  result instead of failing the whole translation.\n\n## Russian Wiktionary specifics\n\n- The `=== Перевод ===` section is the reverse-lookup anchor. The\n  Russian edition is the densest source of `ru → other` data because\n  English Wiktionary's `ru:` columns are often sparse for\n  intermediate-frequency nouns.\n- Inflection templates (`{{сущ-ru|...}}`) carry the full declension\n  paradigm in wikitext. We do **not** parse them in this PR — Russian\n  inflected forms like `помидоры` resolve through the MediaWiki\n  redirect (the `помидоры` page redirects to the lemma `помидор` and\n  the `parse` API follows the redirect transparently) — but parsing\n  the template directly is the right long-term answer for plural and\n  case forms that Wiktionary does not redirect.\n\n## Browser CORS constraints\n\n- Web workers run in the same origin as the host page (GitHub\n  Pages: `link-assistant.github.io`). They can `fetch()` any\n  same-origin asset (the seed bundles, the WASM blob, and the\n  `data/seed/api-cache/*.lino` files served by the dev server).\n- Cross-origin fetches succeed only when the remote server emits\n  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Wiktionary's `api.php` does so\n  when you pass `&origin=*`. The wikitext is the\n  only place where the `{{trans-top}}` / `{{перев-блок}}` sense\n  blocks are stable, since rendered HTML strips template metadata.\n- **CORS** — MediaWiki accepts `&origin=*` for anonymous read-only\n  GETs across all `*.wiktionary.org` editions. This is what\n  `liveWiktionaryTranslate` in `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` uses to\n  resolve any surface that is not already covered by the committed\n  seed bundle. Before 2026-05-22 PR #222 considered shipping a\n  pre-extracted dictionary instead; the reviewer rejected the\n  approach (*\"we should only store originals of the source data from\n  wikipedia/wikidata/wiktionary\"*), so the worker now always falls\n  back to a live MediaWiki call when the seeded response is missing.\n- **Translation subpages** — high-traffic English entries (e.g.\n  `apple`, `water`, `milk`, `book`) keep translation tables on a\n  `/translations` subpage referenced by\n  `{{see translation subpage|...}}`. Both the Rust pipeline\n  (`pipeline.rs` stage 1a) and the browser worker fetch the subpage\n  when they see the marker and merge the wikitext before extracting\n  templates.\n\n## Wikidata SPARQL lexeme join\n\n- **P5137** (`item for this sense`) is the canonical link from a\n  Wiktionary sense to a language-neutral Q-item. Joining two\n  lexemes through P5137 gives us a deterministic\n  `meaning_id (Q…)` regardless of which side served the trigger.\n- **Polysemy fix** — when a single surface form has both noun and\n  verb lexemes (e.g. English `water` → noun and verb lexemes;\n  `milk` → noun `L4514` and verb), the unconstrained SPARQL query\n  returned whichever lexeme appeared first and could follow its\n  P5137 sense to the wrong part of speech (`water → поливать`,\n  `milk → доить`). Since 2026-05-22 the SPARQL query in\n  `src/translation/wikidata.rs` requires\n  `?source wikibase:lexicalCategory ?cat. ?target wikibase:lexicalCategory ?cat`,\n  so source and target lexemes share a part of speech before P5137\n  is joined.\n- **502 errors** — the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint occasionally returns\n  HTTP 502 under load. The pipeline records the error in the\n  provenance trace and falls back to the Wiktionary block-level\n  result instead of failing the whole translation.\n\n## Russian Wiktionary specifics\n\n- The `=== Перевод ===` section is the reverse-lookup anchor. The\n  Russian edition is the densest source of `ru → other` data because\n  English Wiktionary's `ru:` columns are often sparse for\n  intermediate-frequency nouns.\n- Inflection templates (`{{сущ-ru|...}}`) carry the full declension\n  paradigm in wikitext. We do **not** parse them in this PR — Russian\n  inflected forms like `помидоры` resolve through the MediaWiki\n  redirect (the `помидоры` page redirects to the lemma `помидор` and\n  the `parse` API follows the redirect transparently) — but parsing\n  the template directly is the right long-term answer for plural and\n  case forms that Wiktionary does not redirect.\n\n## Browser CORS constraints\n\n- Web workers run in the same origin as the host page (GitHub\n  Pages: `link-assistant.github.io`). They can `fetch()` any\n  same-origin asset (the seed bundles, the WASM blob, and the\n  `data/seed/api-cache/*.lino` files served by the dev server).\n- Cross-origin fetches succeed only when the remote server emits\n  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Wiktionary's `api.php` does so\n  when you pass `&origin=*`. The worker's `liveWiktionaryTranslate`\n  relies on exactly that behaviour — no proxy required, no offline\n  dictionary shipped.\n\n## Related upstream issues\n\n- Wikimedia phabricator T241992 — long-standing request to include\n  P5137 senses in `wbsearchentities`. If it ever lands, our\n  formalize step can hit a single API and skip the Wiktionary\n  wikitext parse for many words.\n- Wiktionary T118720 — the inflection-template normalization\n  request that would make plural / case forms machine-extractable.\n  Tracking issue, not actionable from our side.\n",

The order mirrors the\ninvestigation timeline; each reference was followed against live\nendpoints before any code change.\n\n## Wiktionary API\n\n- **`action=parse&prop=wikitext`** — the pipeline pulls raw wikitext\n  for every page rather than the rendered HTML. The wikitext is the\n  only place where the `{{trans-top}}` / `{{перев-блок}}` sense\n  blocks are stable, since rendered HTML strips template metadata.\n- **CORS** — MediaWiki accepts `&origin=*` for anonymous read-only\n  GETs across all `*.wiktionary.org` editions. This is what\n  `fetchWiktionaryEntry` already uses for the external lookup\n  fallback. We **could** add live translation fetch in the worker on\n  top of this, but the current pull request opts for a pre-compiled\n  dictionary because the demo must work without leaking the\n  user's browsing patterns to Wikimedia. See PR #222 discussion.\n- **Translation subpages** — high-traffic English entries (e.g.\n  `apple`, `book`, `milk`) keep translation tables on a `/translations`\n  subpage referenced by `{{see translation subpage|...}}`. The Rust\n  pipeline already tries this fallback (`pipeline.rs` stage 1a).\n\n## Wikidata SPARQL lexeme join\n\n- **P5137** (`item for this sense`) is the canonical link from a\n  Wiktionary sense to a language-neutral Q-item. Joining two\n  lexemes through P5137 gives us a deterministic\n  `meaning_id (Q…)` regardless of which side served the trigger.\n- **Polysemy gotcha** — when a single surface form has both noun and\n  verb lexemes (e.g. English `milk` → noun `L4514` and verb\n  `L4514-S1`), the SPARQL query returns whichever lexeme appears\n  first. The current code path picks `L4514` and follows its sole\n  P5137 sense to whatever Wikidata calls the canonical Russian form,\n  landing on `доить` (the verb \"to milk\") instead of `молоко`. This\n  is a **known limitation** flagged in the case-study future work;\n  the dictionary work-around captures `molokó` directly for the\n  demo.\n- **502 errors** — the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint occasionally returns\n  HTTP 502 under load. The pipeline records the error in the\n  provenance trace and falls back to the Wiktionary block-level\n  result instead of failing the whole translation.\n\n## Russian Wiktionary specifics\n\n- The `=== Перевод ===` section is the reverse-lookup anchor. The\n  Russian edition is the densest source of `ru → other` data because\n  English Wiktionary's `ru:` columns are often sparse for\n  intermediate-frequency nouns.\n- Inflection templates (`{{сущ-ru|...}}`) carry the full declension\n  paradigm in wikitext. We do **not** parse them in this PR — the\n  alias generator hard-codes the common suffix tables — but\n  parsing them is the right long-term answer for issues like\n  `Переведи \"помидоры\" на английский.` (plural form).\n\n## Browser CORS constraints\n\n- Web workers run in the same origin as the host page (GitHub\n  Pages: `link-assistant.github.io`). They can `fetch()` any\n  same-origin asset (the seed bundles, the WASM blob, and now\n  `seed/translations.lino`).\n- Cross-origin fetches succeed only when the remote server emits\n  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Q-id, P-id or Lexeme-id mentioned in the URL.\n//! - **Wiktionary** wikitext lands under `wiktionary-cache/<lang>/`\n//!   keyed by the page title.\n//! - **SPARQL** queries land under `wikidata-cache/sparql/` keyed by a\n//!   short hash, because there is no natural semantic name for a SPARQL\n//!   string.\n//! - **Everything else** still uses a URL-hash filename, but in a\n//!   dedicated `http-cache/misc/` bucket. Unrecognised hosts should be\n//!   rare in practice — the cache is intentionally narrow.\n//!\n//! There is no pre-extracted translation table in this repo: the only\n//! committed data are **verbatim API response bodies** that the live\n//! formalization pipeline produced. Those committed bodies live in the\n//! seed bundle at [`SEED_CACHE_DIR`] as a small set of `.lino` files,\n//! capped at 128 Wikidata entities + 128 properties + the Wiktionary\n//! pages they point at. {\n        hash ^= u64::from(byte);\n        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x0000_0100_0000_01B3);\n    }\n    format!(\"{hash:016x}\")\n}\n\n/// Read the cache truthiness flag from the environment. Accepts `1`,\n/// `true`, `yes`, `on` (case-insensitive). Anything else is treated as\n/// disabled.\nfn live_api_enabled() -> bool {\n    std::env::var(\"FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API\").is_ok_and(|value| {\n        matches!(\n            value.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str(),\n            \"1\" | \"true\" | \"yes\" | \"on\"\n        )\n    })\n}\n\nimpl<T: HttpClient> HttpClient for CachedHttpClient<T> {\n    fn get(&self, url: &str) -> Result<String, HttpError> {\n        // Layer 1: committed seed bundle (deterministic, ships in git).\n        if let Some(body) = seed_response(url) {\n            return Ok(body);\n        }\n\n        // Layer 2: gitignored on-disk accelerator under `cache_dir`.\n        let (body_path, meta_path) = self.cache_paths(url);\n        if let Ok(body) = fs::read_to_string(&body_path) {\n            return Ok(body);\n        }\n        if !self.online {\n            return Err(HttpError::Transport(format!(\n                \"translation cache miss for {url} and offline mode is active; \\\n                 set FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1 to fetch and populate the cache\",\n            )));\n        }\n\n        // Layer 3: live transport.\n        let body = self.transport.get(url)?;\n        let parent = body_path.parent().unwrap_or(&self.cache_dir);\n        if let Err(error) = fs::create_dir_all(parent) {\n            return Err(HttpError::Transport(format!(\n                \"failed to create cache directory {}: {error}\",\n                parent.display(),\n            )));\n        }\n        if let Err(error) = fs::write(&body_path, &body) {\n            return Err(HttpError::Transport(format!(\n                \"failed to write cache body {}: {error}\",\n                body_path.display(),\n            )));\n        }\n        if let Err(error) = fs::write(&meta_path, url) {\n            return Err(HttpError::Transport(format!(\n                \"failed to write cache url marker {}: {error}\",\n                meta_path.display(),\n            )));\n        }\n        Ok(body)\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Seeded raw API response bundle\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// The list of seed `.lino` files is generated by `build.rs`, which walks\n// `data/seed/api-cache/` at build time. That keeps the registry honest as\n// the bundler splits a bucket into `<bucket>-partN.lino` files without\n// requiring per-file edits here.\ninclude!(concat!(env!(\"OUT_DIR\"), \"/seed_bundle_files.rs\"));\n\n/// All committed seed `.lino` files in deterministic (sorted) order.\n#[must_use]\npub fn seed_files() -> Vec<(&'static str, &'static str)> {\n    SEED_BUNDLE_FILES.to_vec()\n}\n\n/// Look up a seeded response body by URL. Returns `None` when the URL\n/// is not part of the committed bundle.\n#[must_use]\npub fn seed_response(url: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    seed_index().get(url).cloned()\n}\n\n/// Process-wide lazily-parsed URL → body map. Loaded once on first\n/// access from the embedded `.lino` seed files. Records sharing a URL\n/// (a body whose base64 spans multiple `.lino` parts) have their chunks\n/// concatenated in the file/record order returned by [`seed_files`]\n/// before decoding, so an oversize response can be split across as many\n/// `<bucket>-partN.lino` files as needed without breaking lookup.\nfn seed_index() -> &'static HashMap<String, String> {\n    static INDEX: OnceLock<HashMap<String, String>> = OnceLock::new();\n    INDEX.get_or_init(|| {\n        let mut chunks: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();\n        let mut order: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        for (_name, contents) in seed_files() {\n            for (url, b64) in parse_seed_chunks(contents) {\n                let entry = chunks.entry(url.clone()).or_insert_with(|| {\n                    order.push(url.clone());\n                    String::new()\n                });\n                entry.push_str(&b64);\n            }\n        }\n        let mut index = HashMap::new();\n        for url in order {\n            let Some(b64) = chunks.remove(&url) else {\n                continue;\n            };\n            if let Some(body) = base64_decode_to_string(&b64) {\n                index.insert(url, body);\n            }\n        }\n        index\n    })\n}\n\n/// Parse a `.lino` seed bundle into `(url, body)` pairs.\n///\n/// Each `response_<short_id>` block produces one pair with the body\n/// already base64-decoded. Records sharing a URL are returned separately\n/// in the order they appear — call [`seed_index`] (which concatenates\n/// them) if you want the assembled body.\n///\n/// The grammar is intentionally narrow:\n///\n/// ```text\n/// response_<short_id>\n///   url \"<full URL>\"\n///   body_base64 \"<chunk 1>\"\n///   body_base64 \"<chunk 2>\"\n///   ...\n/// ```\n#[must_use]\npub fn parse_seed_bundle(text: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {\n    parse_seed_chunks(text)\n        .into_iter()\n        .filter_map(|(url, b64)| base64_decode_to_string(&b64).map(|body| (url, body)))\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// Parse a `.lino` seed bundle into `(url, base64_chunk)` pairs without\n/// decoding. Used by [`seed_index`] so split-body records (multiple\n/// records with the same URL across `<bucket>-partN.lino` files) can be\n/// concatenated before a single base64 decode.\n#[must_use]\npub fn parse_seed_chunks(text: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {\n    let mut out: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();\n    let mut current_url: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut current_b64: String = String::new();\n\n    let flush = |url: &mut Option<String>, b64: &mut String, out: &mut Vec<(String, String)>| {\n        if let Some(url_value) = url.take() {\n            if !b64.is_empty() {\n                out.push((url_value, std::mem::take(b64)));\n            } else {\n                b64.clear();\n            }\n        }\n    };\n\n    for raw_line in text.lines() {\n        let trimmed = raw_line.trim_end_matches(['\\r', '\\n']);\n        if trimmed.trim().is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let indent = trimmed.bytes().take_while(|b| *b == b' ').count();\n        let content = &trimmed[indent..];\n        if indent == 0 {\n            flush(&mut current_url, &mut current_b64, &mut out);\n            if content.starts_with(\"response_\") {\n                current_url = Some(String::new());\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n        if current_url.is_none() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        if let Some(value) = strip_kv(content, \"url\") {\n            current_url = Some(value.to_owned());\n        } else if let Some(value) = strip_kv(content, \"body_base64\") {\n            current_b64.push_str(value);\n        }\n    }\n    flush(&mut current_url, &mut current_b64, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n/// Extract a `\"value\"` after `key ` from a line. Returns `None` when the\n/// line does not match `key \"value\"`.\nfn strip_kv<'a>(content: &'a str, key: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {\n    let rest = content.strip_prefix(key)?;\n    let rest = rest.strip_prefix(' ')?;\n    let rest = rest.strip_prefix('\"')?;\n    rest.strip_suffix('\"')\n}\n\n/// Base64-decode a stream of characters into a UTF-8 string. Returns\n/// `None` if the input is malformed or the resulting bytes are not UTF-8.\n#[must_use]\npub fn base64_decode_to_string(input: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let bytes = base64_decode(input)?;\n    String::from_utf8(bytes).ok()\n}\n\n/// Standard RFC 4648 base64 decoder. Skips whitespace; rejects invalid\n/// characters and bad padding. Kept inline so the cache layer has no\n/// dependency outside the standard library.\n#[must_use]\npub fn base64_decode(input: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n    let mut out: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(input.len() * 3 / 4);\n    let mut buf: u32 = 0;\n    let mut bits: u32 = 0;\n    let mut pad: u32 = 0;\n    for byte in input.bytes() {\n        if matches!(byte, b' ' | b'\\t' | b'\\r' | b'\\n') {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let value = match byte {\n            b'A'..=b'Z' => u32::from(byte - b'A'),\n            b'a'..=b'z' => u32::from(byte - b'a') + 26,\n            b'0'..=b'9' => u32::from(byte - b'0') + 52,\n            b'+' => 62,\n            b'/' => 63,\n            b'=' => {\n                pad += 1;\n                if pad > 2 {\n                    return None;\n                }\n                buf <<= 6;\n                bits += 6;\n                if bits >= 8 {\n                    bits -= 8;\n                }\n                continue;\n            }\n            _ => return None,\n        };\n        if pad > 0 {\n            return None;\n        }\n        buf = (buf << 6) | value;\n        bits += 6;\n        if bits >= 8 {\n            bits -= 8;\n            out.push(((buf >> bits) & 0xff) as u8);\n        }\n    }\n    Some(out)\n}\n\n/// Standard RFC 4648 base64 encoder. Pads with `=` to a multiple of four\n/// characters. The refresh tool uses this to write seed bundles.\n#[must_use]\npub fn base64_encode(input: &[u8]) -> String {\n    const ALPHABET: &[u8; 64] = b\"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/\";\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(input.len().div_ceil(3) * 4);\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i + 3 <= input.len() {\n        let b0 = input[i];\n        let b1 = input[i + 1];\n        let b2 = input[i + 2];\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(b0 >> 2) as usize] as char);\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(((b0 & 0x03) << 4) | (b1 >> 4)) as usize] as char);\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(((b1 & 0x0f) << 2) | (b2 >> 6)) as usize] as char);\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(b2 & 0x3f) as usize] as char);\n        i += 3;\n    }\n    match input.len() - i {\n        1 => {\n            let b0 = input[i];\n            out.push(ALPHABET[(b0 >> 2) as usize] as char);\n            out.push(ALPHABET[((b0 & 0x03) << 4) as usize] as char);\n            out.push('=');\n            out.push('=');\n        }\n        2 => {\n            let b0 = input[i];\n            let b1 = input[i + 1];\n            out.push(ALPHABET[(b0 >> 2) as usize] as char);\n            out.push(ALPHABET[(((b0 & 0x03) << 4) | (b1 >> 4)) as usize] as char);\n            out.push(ALPHABET[((b1 & 0x0f) << 2) as usize] as char);\n            out.push('=');\n        }\n        _ => {}\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Emit a single `response_<short_id>` record into a `.lino` buffer.\n///\n/// Public so the refresh-cache example (and tests) can produce seed\n/// files out.push(b' ');\n        } else {\n            out.push(byte);\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    String::from_utf8_lossy(&out).into_owned()\n}\n\nconst fn hex_nibble(byte: u8) -> Option<u8> {\n {\n        hash ^= u64::from(byte);\n        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x0000_0100_0000_01B3);\n    }\n    format!(\"{hash:016x}\")\n}\n\n/// Read the cache truthiness flag from the environment. Loaded once on first\n/// access from the embedded `.lino` seed files. Records sharing a URL\n/// (a body whose base64 spans multiple `.lino` parts) have their chunks\n/// concatenated in the file/record order returned by [`seed_files`]\n/// before decoding, so an oversize response can be split across as many\n/// `<bucket>-partN.lino` files as needed without breaking lookup.\nfn seed_index() -> &'static HashMap<String, String> {\n    static INDEX: OnceLock<HashMap<String, String>> = OnceLock::new();\n    INDEX.get_or_init(|| {\n        let mut chunks: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();\n        let mut order: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        for (_name, contents) in seed_files() {\n            for (url, b64) in parse_seed_chunks(contents) {\n                let entry = chunks.entry(url.clone()).or_insert_with(|| {\n                    order.push(url.clone());\n                    String::new()\n                });\n                entry.push_str(&b64);\n            }\n        }\n        let mut index = HashMap::new();\n        for url in order {\n            let Some(b64) = chunks.remove(&url) else {\n                continue;\n            };\n            if let Some(body) = base64_decode_to_string(&b64) {\n                index.insert(url, body);\n            }\n        }\n        index\n    })\n}\n\n/// Parse a `.lino` seed bundle into `(url, body)` pairs.\n///\n/// Each `response_<short_id>` block produces one pair with the body\n/// already base64-decoded. Records sharing a URL are returned separately\n/// in the order they appear — call [`seed_index`] (which concatenates\n/// them) if you want the assembled body.\n///\n/// The grammar is intentionally narrow:\n///\n/// ```text\n/// response_<short_id>\n///   url \"<full URL>\"\n///   body_base64 \"<chunk 1>\"\n///   body_base64 \"<chunk 2>\"\n///   ...\n/// ```\n#[must_use]\npub fn parse_seed_bundle(text: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {\n    parse_seed_chunks(text)\n        .into_iter()\n        .filter_map(|(url, b64)| base64_decode_to_string(&b64).map(|body| (url, body)))\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// Parse a `.lino` seed bundle into `(url, base64_chunk)` pairs without\n/// decoding. Used by [`seed_index`] so split-body records (multiple\n/// records with the same URL across `<bucket>-partN.lino` files) can be\n/// concatenated before a single base64 decode.\n#[must_use]\npub fn parse_seed_chunks(text: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {\n    let mut out: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();\n    let mut current_url: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut current_b64: String = String::new();\n\n    let flush = |url: &mut Option<String>, b64: &mut String, out: &mut Vec<(String, String)>| {\n        if let Some(url_value) = url.take() {\n            if !b64.is_empty() {\n                out.push((url_value, std::mem::take(b64)));\n            } else {\n                b64.clear();\n            }\n        }\n    };\n\n    for raw_line in text.lines() {\n        let trimmed = raw_line.trim_end_matches(['\\r', '\\n']);\n        if trimmed.trim().is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let indent = trimmed.bytes().take_while(|b| *b == b' ').count();\n        let content = &trimmed[indent..];\n        if indent == 0 {\n            flush(&mut current_url, &mut current_b64, &mut out);\n            if content.starts_with(\"response_\") {\n                current_url = Some(String::new());\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n        if current_url.is_none() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        if let Some(value) = strip_kv(content, \"url\") {\n            current_url = Some(value.to_owned());\n        } else if let Some(value) = strip_kv(content, \"body_base64\") {\n            current_b64.push_str(value);\n        }\n    }\n    flush(&mut current_url, &mut current_b64, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n/// Extract a `\"value\"` after `key ` from a line. Returns `None` when the\n/// line does not match `key \"value\"`.\nfn strip_kv<'a>(content: &'a str, key: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {\n    let rest = content.strip_prefix(key)?;\n    let rest = rest.strip_prefix(' ')?;\n    let rest = rest.strip_prefix('\"')?;\n    rest.strip_suffix('\"')\n}\n\n/// Base64-decode a stream of characters into a UTF-8 string. Returns\n/// `None` if the input is malformed or the resulting bytes are not UTF-8.\n#[must_use]\npub fn base64_decode_to_string(input: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let bytes = base64_decode(input)?;\n    String::from_utf8(bytes).ok()\n}\n\n/// Standard RFC 4648 base64 decoder. Skips whitespace; rejects invalid\n/// characters and bad padding. Kept inline so the cache layer has no\n/// dependency outside the standard library.\n#[must_use]\npub fn base64_decode(input: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n    let mut out: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(input.len() * 3 / 4);\n    let mut buf: u32 = 0;\n    let mut bits: u32 = 0;\n    let mut pad: u32 = 0;\n    for byte in input.bytes() {\n        if matches!(byte, b' ' | b'\\t' | b'\\r' | b'\\n') {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let value = match byte {\n            b'A'..=b'Z' => u32::from(byte - b'A'),\n            b'a'..=b'z' => u32::from(byte - b'a') + 26,\n            b'0'..=b'9' => u32::from(byte - b'0') + 52,\n            b'+' => 62,\n            b'/' => 63,\n            b'=' => {\n                pad += 1;\n                if pad > 2 {\n                    return None;\n                }\n                buf <<= 6;\n                bits += 6;\n                if bits >= 8 {\n                    bits -= 8;\n                }\n                continue;\n            }\n            _ => return None,\n        };\n        if pad > 0 {\n            return None;\n        }\n        buf = (buf << 6) | value;\n        bits += 6;\n        if bits >= 8 {\n            bits -= 8;\n            out.push(((buf >> bits) & 0xff) as u8);\n        }\n    }\n    Some(out)\n}\n\n/// Standard RFC 4648 base64 encoder. Pads with `=` to a multiple of four\n/// characters. The refresh tool uses this to write seed bundles.\n#[must_use]\npub fn base64_encode(input: &[u8]) -> String {\n    const ALPHABET: &[u8; 64] = b\"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/\";\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(input.len().div_ceil(3) * 4);\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i + 3 <= input.len() {\n        let b0 = input[i];\n        let b1 = input[i + 1];\n        let b2 = input[i + 2];\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(b0 >> 2) as usize] as char);\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(((b0 & 0x03) << 4) | (b1 >> 4)) as usize] as char);\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(((b1 & 0x0f) << 2) | (b2 >> 6)) as usize] as char);\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(b2 & 0x3f) as usize] as char);\n        i += 3;\n    }\n    match input.len() - i {\n        1 => {\n            let b0 = input[i];\n            out.push(ALPHABET[(b0 >> 2) as usize] as char);\n            out.push(ALPHABET[((b0 & 0x03) << 4) as usize] as char);\n            out.push('=');\n            out.push('=');\n        }\n        2 => {\n            let b0 = input[i];\n            let b1 = input[i + 1];\n            out.push(ALPHABET[(b0 >> 2) as usize] as char);\n            out.push(ALPHABET[(((b0 & 0x03) << 4) | (b1 >> 4)) as usize] as char);\n            out.push(ALPHABET[((b1 & 0x0f) << 2) as usize] as char);\n            out.push('=');\n        }\n        _ => {}\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Emit a single `response_<short_id>` record into a `.lino` buffer.\n///\n/// Public so the refresh-cache example (and tests) can produce seed\n/// files using the exact format [`parse_seed_bundle`] consumes.\npub fn write_seed_record(out: &mut String, short_id: &str, url: &str, body: &str) {\n    out.push_str(\"response_\");\n out.push_str(&encoded[cursor..end]);\n        out.push_str(\"\\\"\\n\");\n        cursor = end;\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use std::collections::HashMap as Wikidata or Wiktionary fetch feed translation, fact lookup and any\n//! other formalization path without duplicating bytes, and keeps unit\n//! tests offline by default.\n\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::OnceLock;\n\nuse super::http::{HttpClient, HttpError};\n\n/// Default cache root, relative to the crate root.\n///\n/// Per-source subfolders (`wikidata-cache/`, `wiktionary-cache/<lang>/`, …)\n/// live as siblings of this directory so callers from other formalization\n/// paths can share the same bytes.\npub const DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR: &str = \"data\";\n\n/// Directory under the repository root that holds the committed seed.\n///\n/// `.lino` files here are shipped in git so a clean checkout can run the\n/// full pipeline offline; the on-disk accelerator under\n/// [`DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR`] is gitignored and only used when\n/// `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1` populates it.\npub const SEED_CACHE_DIR: &str = \"data/seed/api-cache\";\n\n/// Hard cap on the number of lines per seeded `.lino` cache file. Larger\n/// files become unreadable; the refresh tool splits responses into\n/// `<bucket>-partN.lino` files when needed.\npub const MAX_SEED_LINES_PER_FILE: usize = 1500;\n\n/// Hard cap on the number of distinct entities (or properties) per bucket.\n///\n/// We never ship more than this many records in the seeded cache. This\n/// keeps the repository small enough to review and stays honest about the\n/// \"lightweight by default\" constraint from issue #221's reviewer\n/// feedback.\npub const MAX_SEED_RECORDS_PER_BUCKET: usize = 128;\n\n/// HTTP client that consults a file cache before delegating to a real\n/// transport. Cache hits always short-circuit the underlying transport;\n/// cache misses populate the cache after a successful fetch.\npub struct CachedHttpClient<T: HttpClient> {\n    cache_dir: PathBuf,\n    transport: T,\n    /// When `true`, cache misses fall through to the transport. When\n    /// `false`, cache misses return [`HttpError::Transport`] without any\n    /// network access. Defaults to `false` so unit tests are offline-only.\n    online: bool,\n}\n\nimpl<T: HttpClient> CachedHttpClient<T> {\n    /// Construct a cached client. `online` defaults to whether the\n    /// `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API` environment variable is set to a truthy value.\n    pub fn new(cache_dir: impl Into<PathBuf>, transport: T) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            cache_dir: cache_dir.into(),\n            transport,\n            online: live_api_enabled(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Override the online flag explicitly. Useful for tests that want to\n    /// force offline mode regardless of the environment.\n    #[must_use]\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    pub const fn with_online(mut self, online: bool) -> Self {\n        self.online = online;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Return the directory where cache entries are stored.\n    #[must_use]\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    pub fn cache_dir(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.cache_dir\n    }\n\n    /// Return whether the cache will fall through to the transport on\n    /// misses.\n    #[must_use]\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    pub const fn is_online(&self) -> bool {\n        self.online\n    }\n\n    fn cache_paths(&self, url: &str) -> (PathBuf, PathBuf) {\n        let location = cache_location(url);\n        let mut body = self.cache_dir.clone();\n        body.push(&location.directory);\n        body.push(format!(\"{}.body\", location.stem));\n        let mut meta = self.cache_dir.clone();\n        meta.push(&location.directory);\n        meta.push(format!(\"{}.url\", location.stem));\n        (body, meta)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Where a URL should land inside the cache root.\n///\n/// `directory` is a relative subpath (e.g. `wiktionary-cache/en`) and\n/// `stem` is the filename without extension (e.g. `apple`). The cache\n/// writes `<root>/<directory>/<stem>.body` and `<root>/<directory>/<stem>.url`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct CacheLocation {\n    pub directory: PathBuf,\n    pub stem: String,\n}\n\n/// Decide the cache location for a URL.\n///\n/// The mapping is best-effort: well-known Wikidata / Wiktionary URLs land\n/// under human-readable semantic folders, and anything else falls back to\n/// a hashed bucket so we never refuse to cache a response.\n#[must_use]\npub fn cache_location(url: &str) -> CacheLocation {\n    if let Some(location) = classify_wiktionary(url) {\n        return location;\n    }\n    if let Some(location) = classify_wikidata(url) {\n        return location;\n    }\n    CacheLocation {\n        directory: PathBuf::from(\"http-cache\").join(\"misc\"),\n        stem: cache_key(url),\n    }\n}\n\nfn classify_wiktionary(url: &str) -> Option<CacheLocation> {\n    let host_start = url.find(\"://\")? + 3;\n    let after_scheme = &url[host_start..];\n    let dot = after_scheme.find('.')?;\n    let host_end = after_scheme.find('/').unwrap_or(after_scheme.len());\n    let host_rest = &after_scheme[dot..host_end];\n    if !host_rest.starts_with(\".wiktionary.org\") {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let lang = sanitize_segment(&after_scheme[..dot]);\n    let page = wiktionary_page_from_url(url).unwrap_or_else(|| cache_key(url));\n    Some(CacheLocation {\n        directory: PathBuf::from(\"wiktionary-cache\").join(lang),\n        stem: page,\n    })\n}\n\nfn wiktionary_page_from_url(url: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Pages are fetched via the `parse` API:\n    //   /w/api.php?action=parse&page=<title>&...\n    let query_start = url.find('?')?;\n    let query = &url[query_start + 1..];\n    for pair in query.split('&') {\n        if let Some(value) = pair.strip_prefix(\"page=\") {\n            let decoded = percent_decode(value);\n            if !decoded.is_empty() {\n                return Some(sanitize_segment(&decoded));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\nfn classify_wikidata(url: &str) -> Option<CacheLocation> {\n    if !url.contains(\"wikidata.org\") {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let query_start = url.find('?')?;\n    let query = &url[query_start + 1..];\n    let mut action: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut srsearch: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut ids: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut sparql: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut titles: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut search_term: Option<String> = None;\n    for pair in query.split('&') {\n        if let Some(value) = pair.strip_prefix(\"action=\") {\n            action = Some(percent_decode(value));\n        } else if let Some(value) = pair.strip_prefix(\"srsearch=\") {\n            srsearch = Some(percent_decode(value));\n        } else if let Some(value) = pair.strip_prefix(\"search=\") {\n            search_term = Some(percent_decode(value));\n        } else if let Some(value) = pair.strip_prefix(\"ids=\") {\n            ids = Some(percent_decode(value));\n        } else if let Some(value) = pair.strip_prefix(\"query=\") {\n            sparql = Some(percent_decode(value));\n        } else if let Some(value) = pair.strip_prefix(\"titles=\") {\n            titles = Some(percent_decode(value));\n        }\n    }\n    if sparql.is_some() || url.contains(\"/sparql\") || url.contains(\"query.wikidata.org\") {\n        return Some(CacheLocation {\n            directory: PathBuf::from(\"wikidata-cache\").join(\"sparql\"),\n            stem: cache_key(url),\n        });\n    }\n    let stem = match action.as_deref() {\n        Some(\"wbsearchentities\") => srsearch\n            .as_deref()\n            .or(search_term.as_deref())\n            .map_or_else(|| cache_key(url), sanitize_segment),\n        Some(\"wbgetentities\" | \"query\") => ids\n            .as_deref()\n            .or(titles.as_deref())\n            .map_or_else(|| cache_key(url), sanitize_segment),\n        _ => cache_key(url),\n    };\n    let sub = match action.as_deref() {\n        Some(\"wbsearchentities\") => \"search\",\n        Some(\"wbgetentities\") => \"entities\",\n        Some(\"query\") => \"query\",\n        _ => \"misc\",\n    };\n    Some(CacheLocation {\n        directory: PathBuf::from(\"wikidata-cache\").join(sub),\n        stem,\n    })\n}\n\nfn sanitize_segment(value: &str) -> String {\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(value.len());\n    for ch in value.chars() {\n        if ch.is_alphanumeric() || matches!(ch, '-' | '_' | '.') {\n            out.push(ch);\n        } else if ch == ' ' || ch == '+' {\n            out.push('_');\n        } else {\n            out.push('-');\n        }\n    }\n    if out.len() > 96 {\n        // Avoid blowing past common filesystem name limits when a SPARQL\n        // search returns a freakishly long title.\n        out.truncate(96);\n        out.push('~');\n        out.push_str(&cache_key(value)[..8]);\n    }\n    if out.is_empty() {\n        cache_key(value)\n    } else {\n        out\n    }\n}\n\nfn percent_decode(value: &str) -> String {\n    let bytes = value.as_bytes();\n    let mut out: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(bytes.len());\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i < bytes.len() {\n        let byte = bytes[i];\n        if byte == b'%' && i + 2 < bytes.len() {\n            let hi = hex_nibble(bytes[i + 1]);\n            let lo = hex_nibble(bytes[i + 2]);\n            if let (Some(hi), Some(lo)) = (hi, lo) {\n                out.push((hi << 4) | lo);\n                i += 3;\n                continue;\n            }\n        }\n        if byte == b'+' {\n            out.push(b' ');\n        } else {\n            out.push(byte);\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    String::from_utf8_lossy(&out).into_owned()\n}\n\nconst fn hex_nibble(byte: u8) -> Option<u8> {\n    match byte {\n        b'0'..=b'9' => Some(byte - b'0'),\n        b'a'..=b'f' => Some(byte - b'a' + 10),\n        b'A'..=b'F' => Some(byte - b'A' + 10),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Compute a deterministic, filesystem-safe key for the cache.\n///\n/// Uses FNV-1a 64-bit which is stable across platforms and Rust versions.\n/// We do not need cryptographic strength — collisions are tolerable because\n/// the sibling `.url` file records the exact URL for audit.\n#[must_use]\npub fn cache_key(url: &str) -> String {\n    let mut hash: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;\n    for byte in url.bytes() {\n        hash ^= u64::from(byte);\n        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x0000_0100_0000_01B3);\n    }\n    format!(\"{hash:016x}\")\n}\n\n/// Read the cache truthiness flag from the environment. Accepts `1`,\n/// `true`, `yes`, `on` (case-insensitive). Anything else is treated as\n/// disabled.\nfn live_api_enabled() -> bool {\n    std::env::var(\"FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API\").is_ok_and(|value| {\n        matches!(\n            value.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str(),\n            \"1\" | \"true\" | \"yes\" | \"on\"\n        )\n    })\n}\n\nimpl<T: HttpClient> HttpClient for CachedHttpClient<T> {\n    fn get(&self, url: &str) -> Result<String, HttpError> {\n        // Layer 1: committed seed bundle (deterministic, ships in git).\n        if let Some(body) = seed_response(url) {\n            return Ok(body);\n        }\n\n        // Layer 2: gitignored on-disk accelerator under `cache_dir`.\n        let (body_path, meta_path) = self.cache_paths(url);\n        if let Ok(body) = fs::read_to_string(&body_path) {\n            return Ok(body);\n        }\n        if !self.online {\n            return Err(HttpError::Transport(format!(\n                \"translation cache miss for {url} and offline mode is active; \\\n                 set FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1 to fetch and populate the cache\",\n            )));\n        }\n\n        // Layer 3: live transport.\n        let body = self.transport.get(url)?;\n        let parent = body_path.parent().unwrap_or(&self.cache_dir);\n        if let Err(error) = fs::create_dir_all(parent) {\n            return Err(HttpError::Transport(format!(\n                \"failed to create cache directory {}: {error}\",\n                parent.display(),\n            )));\n        }\n        if let Err(error) = fs::write(&body_path, &body) {\n            return Err(HttpError::Transport(format!(\n                \"failed to write cache body {}: {error}\",\n                body_path.display(),\n            )));\n        }\n        if let Err(error) = fs::write(&meta_path, url) {\n            return Err(HttpError::Transport(format!(\n                \"failed to write cache url marker {}: {error}\",\n                meta_path.display(),\n            )));\n        }\n        Ok(body)\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Seeded raw API response bundle\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// The list of seed `.lino` files is generated by `build.rs`, which walks\n// `data/seed/api-cache/` at build time. That keeps the registry honest as\n// the bundler splits a bucket into `<bucket>-partN.lino` files without\n// requiring per-file edits here.\ninclude!(concat!(env!(\"OUT_DIR\"), \"/seed_bundle_files.rs\"));\n\n/// All committed seed `.lino` files in deterministic (sorted) order.\n#[must_use]\npub fn seed_files() -> Vec<(&'static str, &'static str)> {\n    SEED_BUNDLE_FILES.to_vec()\n}\n\n/// Look up a seeded response body by URL. Returns `None` when the URL\n/// is not part of the committed bundle.\n#[must_use]\npub fn seed_response(url: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    seed_index().get(url).cloned()\n}\n\n/// Process-wide lazily-parsed URL → body map. Loaded once on first\n/// access from the embedded `.lino` seed files. Records sharing a URL\n/// (a body whose base64 spans multiple `.lino` parts) have their chunks\n/// concatenated in the file/record order returned by [`seed_files`]\n/// before decoding, so an oversize response can be split across as many\n/// `<bucket>-partN.lino` files as needed without breaking lookup.\nfn seed_index() -> &'static HashMap<String, String> {\n    static INDEX: OnceLock<HashMap<String, String>> = OnceLock::new();\n    INDEX.get_or_init(|| {\n        let mut chunks: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();\n        let mut order: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        for (_name, contents) in seed_files() {\n            for (url, b64) in parse_seed_chunks(contents) {\n                let entry = chunks.entry(url.clone()).or_insert_with(|| {\n                    order.push(url.clone());\n                    String::new()\n                });\n                entry.push_str(&b64);\n            }\n        }\n        let mut index = HashMap::new();\n        for url in order {\n            let Some(b64) = chunks.remove(&url) else {\n                continue;\n            };\n            if let Some(body) = base64_decode_to_string(&b64) {\n                index.insert(url, body);\n            }\n        }\n        index\n    })\n}\n\n/// Parse a `.lino` seed bundle into `(url, body)` pairs.\n///\n/// Each `response_<short_id>` block produces one pair with the body\n/// already base64-decoded. Records sharing a URL are returned separately\n/// in the order they appear — call [`seed_index`] (which concatenates\n/// them) if you want the assembled body.\n///\n/// The grammar is intentionally narrow:\n///\n/// ```text\n/// response_<short_id>\n///   url \"<full URL>\"\n///   body_base64 \"<chunk 1>\"\n///   body_base64 \"<chunk 2>\"\n///   ...\n/// ```\n#[must_use]\npub fn parse_seed_bundle(text: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {\n    parse_seed_chunks(text)\n        .into_iter()\n        .filter_map(|(url, b64)| base64_decode_to_string(&b64).map(|body| (url, body)))\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// Parse a `.lino` seed bundle into `(url, base64_chunk)` pairs.\n///\n/// Returns chunks without decoding. Used by [`seed_index`] so split-body\n/// records (multiple records with the same URL across\n/// `<bucket>-partN.lino` files) can be concatenated before a single\n/// base64 decode.\n#[must_use]\npub fn parse_seed_chunks(text: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {\n    let mut out: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();\n    let mut current_url: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut current_b64: String = String::new();\n\n    let flush = |url: &mut Option<String>, b64: &mut String, out: &mut Vec<(String, String)>| {\n        if let Some(url_value) = url.take() {\n            if !b64.is_empty() {\n                out.push((url_value, std::mem::take(b64)));\n            } else {\n                b64.clear();\n            }\n        }\n    };\n\n    for raw_line in text.lines() {\n        let trimmed = raw_line.trim_end_matches(['\\r', '\\n']);\n        if trimmed.trim().is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let indent = trimmed.bytes().take_while(|b| *b == b' ').count();\n        let content = &trimmed[indent..];\n        if indent == 0 {\n            flush(&mut current_url, &mut current_b64, &mut out);\n            if content.starts_with(\"response_\") {\n                current_url = Some(String::new());\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n        if current_url.is_none() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        if let Some(value) = strip_kv(content, \"url\") {\n            current_url = Some(value.to_owned());\n        } else if let Some(value) = strip_kv(content, \"body_base64\") {\n            current_b64.push_str(value);\n        }\n    }\n    flush(&mut current_url, &mut current_b64, &mut out);\n    out\n}\n\n/// Extract a `\"value\"` after `key ` from a line. Returns `None` when the\n/// line does not match `key \"value\"`.\nfn strip_kv<'a>(content: &'a str, key: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {\n    let rest = content.strip_prefix(key)?;\n    let rest = rest.strip_prefix(' ')?;\n    let rest = rest.strip_prefix('\"')?;\n    rest.strip_suffix('\"')\n}\n\n/// Base64-decode a stream of characters into a UTF-8 string. Returns\n/// `None` if the input is malformed or the resulting bytes are not UTF-8.\n#[must_use]\npub fn base64_decode_to_string(input: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let bytes = base64_decode(input)?;\n    String::from_utf8(bytes).ok()\n}\n\n/// Standard RFC 4648 base64 decoder. Skips whitespace; rejects invalid\n/// characters and bad padding. Kept inline so the cache layer has no\n/// dependency outside the standard library.\n#[must_use]\npub fn base64_decode(input: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n    let mut out: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(input.len() * 3 / 4);\n    let mut buf: u32 = 0;\n    let mut bits: u32 = 0;\n    let mut pad: u32 = 0;\n    for byte in input.bytes() {\n        if matches!(byte, b' ' | b'\\t' | b'\\r' | b'\\n') {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let value = match byte {\n            b'A'..=b'Z' => u32::from(byte - b'A'),\n            b'a'..=b'z' => u32::from(byte - b'a') + 26,\n            b'0'..=b'9' => u32::from(byte - b'0') + 52,\n            b'+' => 62,\n            b'/' => 63,\n            b'=' => {\n                pad += 1;\n                if pad > 2 {\n                    return None;\n                }\n                buf <<= 6;\n                bits += 6;\n                if bits >= 8 {\n                    bits -= 8;\n                }\n                continue;\n            }\n            _ => return None,\n        };\n        if pad > 0 {\n            return None;\n        }\n        buf = (buf << 6) | value;\n        bits += 6;\n        if bits >= 8 {\n            bits -= 8;\n            out.push(((buf >> bits) & 0xff) as u8);\n        }\n    }\n    Some(out)\n}\n\n/// Standard RFC 4648 base64 encoder. Pads with `=` to a multiple of four\n/// characters. The refresh tool uses this to write seed bundles.\n#[must_use]\npub fn base64_encode(input: &[u8]) -> String {\n    const ALPHABET: &[u8; 64] = b\"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/\";\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(input.len().div_ceil(3) * 4);\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i + 3 <= input.len() {\n        let b0 = input[i];\n        let b1 = input[i + 1];\n        let b2 = input[i + 2];\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(b0 >> 2) as usize] as char);\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(((b0 & 0x03) << 4) | (b1 >> 4)) as usize] as char);\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(((b1 & 0x0f) << 2) | (b2 >> 6)) as usize] as char);\n        out.push(ALPHABET[(b2 & 0x3f) as usize] as char);\n        i += 3;\n    }\n    match input.len() - i {\n        1 => {\n            let b0 = input[i];\n            out.push(ALPHABET[(b0 >> 2) as usize] as char);\n            out.push(ALPHABET[((b0 & 0x03) << 4) as usize] as char);\n            out.push('=');\n            out.push('=');\n        }\n        2 => {\n            let b0 = input[i];\n            let b1 = input[i + 1];\n            out.push(ALPHABET[(b0 >> 2) as usize] as char);\n            out.push(ALPHABET[(((b0 & 0x03) << 4) | (b1 >> 4)) as usize] as char);\n            out.push(ALPHABET[((b1 & 0x0f) << 2) as usize] as char);\n            out.push('=');\n        }\n        _ => {}\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Emit a single `response_<short_id>` record into a `.lino` buffer.\n///\n/// Public so the refresh-cache example (and tests) can produce seed\n/// files using the exact format [`parse_seed_bundle`] consumes.\npub fn write_seed_record(out: &mut String, short_id: &str, url: &str, body: &str) {\n    out.push_str(\"response_\");\n    out.push_str(short_id);\n    out.push('\\n');\n    out.push_str(\"  url \\\"\");\n    out.push_str(url);\n    out.push_str(\"\\\"\\n\");\n    let encoded = base64_encode(body.as_bytes());\n    let mut cursor = 0usize;\n    let bytes = encoded.as_bytes();\n    while cursor < bytes.len() {\n        let end = (cursor + 76).min(bytes.len());\n        out.push_str(\"  body_base64 \\\"\");\n        out.push_str(&encoded[cursor..end]);\n        out.push_str(\"\\\"\\n\");\n        cursor = end;\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use std::collections::HashMap as }\n}\n\nfn percent_decode(value: &str) -> String {\n    let bytes = value.as_bytes();\n    let mut out: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(bytes.len());\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i < bytes.len() {\n        let byte = bytes[i];\n        if byte == b'%' && i + 2 < bytes.len() {\n            let hi = hex_nibble(bytes[i + 1]);\n            let lo = hex_nibble(bytes[i + 2]);\n            if let   match byte {\n        b'0'..=b'9' => Some(byte - b'0'),\n        b'a'..=b'f' => Some(byte - b'a' + 10),\n        b'A'..=b'F' => Some(byte - b'A' + 10),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Compute a
