because\n/// the sibling `.url` file records the exact URL for audit.\n#[must_use]\npub fn cache_key(url: &str) -> String {\n    let mut hash: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;\n    for byte in url.bytes() {\n        hash ^= u64::from(byte);\n        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x0000_0100_0000_01B3);\n    }\n    format!(\"{hash:016x}\")\n}\n\n/// Read the cache truthiness flag from the environment. Accepts `1`,\n/// `true`, `yes`, `on` (case-insensitive). Anything else is treated as\n/// disabled.\nfn live_api_enabled() -> bool {\n    std::env::var(\"FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API\").is_ok_and(|value| {\n        matches!(\n            value.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str(),\n            \"1\" | \"true\" | \"yes\" | \"on\"\n        )\n    })\n}\n\nimpl<T: HttpClient> HttpClient for CachedHttpClient<T> {\n    fn get(&self, url: &str) -> Result<String, HttpError> {\n        // Layer 1: committed seed bundle (deterministic, ships in git).\n        if let Some(body) = seed_response(url) {\n            return Ok(body);\n        }\n\n        // Layer 2: gitignored on-disk accelerator under `cache_dir`.\n        let (body_path, meta_path) = self.cache_paths(url);\n        if let Ok(body) = fs::read_to_string(&body_path) {\n            return Ok(body);\n        }\n        if !self.online {\n            return Err(HttpError::Transport(format!(\n                \"translation cache miss for {url} and offline mode is active; \\\n                 set FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1 to fetch and populate the cache\",\n            )));\n        }\n\n        // Layer 3: live transport.\n        let body = self.transport.get(url)?;\n        let parent = body_path.parent().unwrap_or(&self.cache_dir);\n        if let Err(error) = fs::create_dir_all(parent) {\n            return Err(HttpError::Transport(format!(\n                \"failed to create cache directory {}: {error}\",\n                parent.display(),\n            )));\n        }\n        if let Err(error) = fs::write(&body_path, &body) {\n            return Err(HttpError::Transport(format!(\n                \"failed to write cache body {}: {error}\",\n                body_path.display(),\n            )));\n        }\n        if let Err(error) = fs::write(&meta_path, url) {\n            return Err(HttpError::Transport(format!(\n                \"failed to write cache url marker {}: {error}\",\n                meta_path.display(),\n            )));\n        }\n        Ok(body)\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Seeded raw API response bundle\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// The list of seed `.lino` files is generated by `build.rs`, which walks\n// `data/seed/api-cache/` at build time. Loaded once on first\n/// access from the embedded `.lino` seed files. Records sharing a URL\n/// (a body whose base64 spans multiple `.lino` parts) have their chunks\n/// concatenated in the file/record order returned by [`seed_files`]\n/// before decoding, so an oversize response can be split across as many\n/// `<bucket>-partN.lino` files as needed without breaking lookup.\nfn seed_index() -> &'static HashMap<String, String> {\n    static INDEX: OnceLock<HashMap<String, String>> = OnceLock::new();\n    INDEX.get_or_init(|| {\n        let mut chunks: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();\n        let mut order: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        for (_name, contents) in seed_files() {\n            for (url, b64) in parse_seed_chunks(contents) {\n                let entry = chunks.entry(url.clone()).or_insert_with(|| {\n                    order.push(url.clone());\n                    String::new()\n                });\n                entry.push_str(&b64);\n            }\n        }\n        let mut index = HashMap::new();\n        for url in order {\n            let Some(b64) = chunks.remove(&url) else {\n                continue;\n            };\n            if let Some(body) = base64_decode_to_string(&b64) {\n                index.insert(url, body);\n            }\n        }\n        index\n    })\n}\n\n/// Parse a `.lino` seed bundle into `(url, body)` pairs.\n///\n/// Each `response_<short_id>` block produces one pair with the body\n/// already base64-decoded. **This revision (2026-05-22) follows the PR review feedback:** the
previous 128-entry offline dictionary is gone. The only legal cached
artefact is now a **verbatim API response body** stored as base64
inside indented Links Notation files under `data/seed/api-cache/`,
capped at 128 records per semantic bucket and 1500 lines per file.
Anything that cannot be served from the bundle falls through to the
on-disk accelerator (gitignored) and then to live HTTP. The browser
worker has its own live fallback so it never needs a bundled
dictionary.

Full investigation lives in `docs/case-studies/issue-221/`
(timeline through 2026-05-22, eleven verbatim requirements, five root
causes, fixes, before/after table, verification commands, upstream
defect notes, and online research on Wiktionary CORS / Wikidata SPARQL
polysemy).

## Changes

### Raw API-response seed bundle (replaces the dictionary)
- `data/seed/api-cache/*.lino` — verbatim Wikidata and Wiktionary API
  response bodies, indented Links Notation with base64 payloads (RFC
  4648, 76-char chunks). Bundle is capped at 128 records per bucket
  (entities, properties, search, sparql, pages-per-language) and every
  file stays under 1500 lines; oversize bodies split into
  `<bucket>-partN.lino` parts that re-join at load by URL.
- `build.rs` enumerates the `.lino` files at compile time and emits
  `seed_bundle_files.rs` into `OUT_DIR`; `src/translation/cache.rs`
  picks it up via `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), ...))` so adding
  a new part file is automatic — no per-file `include_str!` edit.
- `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs` drives the full pipeline
  against a curated 128-noun seed list, populates the on-disk
  accelerator, then rebundles into the committed `.lino` files
  (splitting oversize records, cleaning stale parts).
- **Deleted**: `data/seed/translations.lino`,
  `src/translation/dictionary.rs`, `examples/build_translation_dictionary.rs`.

### Semantic-identity HTTP cache
- `src/translation/cache.rs` keys URLs by **kind of data**, not URL
  hash: `data/wikidata-cache/{search,entities,query,sparql}/`,
  `data/wiktionary-cache/<lang>/`, `data/http-cache/misc/`. All three
  roots are gitignored — the on-disk cache is a local accelerator
  written by `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1` runs; the committed source of
  truth is the seed bundle above.
- `CachedHttpClient::get` consults three layers in order: seed bundle
  → on-disk accelerator → live HTTP.

### Rust pipeline
- `src/translation/wikidata.rs` — SPARQL lexeme join now requires
  `wikibase:lexicalCategory` to match between source and target
  lexemes, so polysemous surfaces like `water` no longer cross
  noun ↔ verb boundaries (was `water → поливать`, now `water → вода`).
- `src/translation/pipeline.rs` — Stage 1a follows
  `{{see translation subpage|...}}` to the `/translations` subpage
  when the main page only carries the marker.
  `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` enables verbose stage-by-stage
  tracing (closes the issue #218 future-work item).

### Browser worker
- `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` — removed `TRANSLATION_DICTIONARY` and
  `lookupDictionary`. Added `liveWiktionaryTranslate(surface, source,
  target)` that calls
  `*.wiktionary.org/w/api.php?action=parse&page=...&prop=wikitext&format=json&origin=*`
  directly, follows `{{see translation subpage|...}}` to the
  `/translations` subpage, and extracts the `{{tt+|<lang>|...}}` /
  `{{t|...}}` template payload. `translateSurface` and `tryTranslation`
  are now async; the only caller already runs inside `async`.
- `src/web/seed_loader.js` — removed the `extractTranslations` parser
  and the `translations` field; the worker no longer hydrates an
  offline dictionary.
- Mobile-friendly by design: nothing pre-bundled, the MediaWiki action
  API is CORS-friendly through `origin=*`, the seed bundle keeps the
  worker payload tiny.

### Tests & docs
- `tests/unit/specification/translation_via_links.rs` — `issue_221_*`
  regressions covering quoted + unquoted common-noun translation in
  both directions.
- `tests/e2e/tests/issue-221.spec.js` — Playwright coverage of the
  live-worker path: quoted RU→EN, quoted EN→RU, unquoted prompts,
  Russian inflected forms via MediaWiki redirect, round-trip stability.
- `docs/case-studies/issue-221/{README.md,online-research.md}` —
  rewritten for the API-cache + live-worker architecture; preserves
  the original investigation timeline and adds the 2026-05-22 entries.
- `changelog.d/20260522_000500_issue_221_translation_common_nouns.md`
  — rewritten changelog fragment.

## Before / After

| Prompt | Before (v0.100.0) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Переведи "помидор" на английский.` | `"[en] помидор"` | `"tomato"` |
| `Переведи "огурец" на английский.` | `"[en] огурец"` | `"cucumber"` |
| `переведи "картофель" на английский` | `"[en] картофель"` | `"potato"` |
| `translate "tomato" to russian` | `"[ru] tomato"` | `"помидор"` |
| `translate "carrot" to russian` | `"[ru] carrot"` | `"морковь"` |
| `translate "water" to russian` | `"поливать"` (verb!) | `"вода"` |
| `переведи помидор на английский` (unquoted) | `"[en] помидор"` | `"tomato"` |
